sections.title: C1-M3-L1 — Rapports annuels et lettres aux actionnaires : lire au-delà des chiffres
sections.contentHtml:
Objectifs :

  • Distinguer, dans une lettre aux actionnaires de 350 à 450 mots, les résultats publiés (reported) des résultats retraités (underlying) et expliquer l'écart en une phrase.
  • Identifier au moins trois marqueurs de prudence (hedging) ou d'euphémisme et en restituer le sens implicite.
  • Qualifier l'attitude de l'auteur (confiance, prudence, autocritique, défense) en citant le passage qui la justifie, avec au moins 75 % de réponses correctes aux QCM.

Compétence C2 — niveau C1.1 — 40 min

Un rapport annuel n'est pas seulement un document comptable : c'est aussi un exercice de communication très contrôlé. La lettre du président (Chair's statement) et celle du directeur général (Chief Executive's review) cherchent à rassurer, à justifier des choix et à préparer les actionnaires aux mauvaises nouvelles sans jamais les dramatiser. Au niveau C1, on attend de vous que vous lisiez ce qui est dit, comment c'est dit et ce qui n'est pas dit.

1. Reported vs underlying. Les entreprises présentent souvent deux résultats : le résultat publié (reported loss / profit) et un résultat « retraité » qui exclut des éléments jugés exceptionnels (one-off items, non-cash impairment, restructuring costs). Repérez les tournures excluding this item, on an underlying basis, adjusted for. Une question classique demande d'expliquer pourquoi le résultat publié est mauvais alors que l'activité « courante » résiste.

2. Le langage de la prudence (hedging). Les dirigeants évitent les promesses : we remain cautiously optimistic, we do not expect conditions to improve materially, subject to market conditions, we believe, it is too early to say. Ces formules ne sont pas neutres : cautiously optimistic signale un optimisme limité ; not materially signifie « pas de façon significative ».

3. Les euphémismes. A challenging year = une mauvaise année ; headwinds = vents contraires, difficultés externes ; right-sizing our cost base = réduire les coûts, souvent les effectifs ; a more measured pace of expansion = un ralentissement. Savoir les « traduire » est indispensable pour répondre aux questions sur l'implicite.

4. Attitude et position. L'auteur peut se montrer défensif (Some of you have asked why…), autocritique (with hindsight, we were too slow to…), confiant (we are well placed to…) ou réservé envers un tiers, par exemple le régulateur (while we support the direction of travel, the pace of change…). La structure concessive while X, Y est un indice majeur : l'opinion réelle se trouve souvent dans la seconde partie.

5. Ce qui n'est pas dit. Un dividende « maintenu » accompagné de future distributions will be assessed in light of… laisse entendre qu'il pourrait baisser. Un nouveau directeur qui remercie son prédécesseur « for his contribution to the Group's early growth » suggère, en creux, que la période récente a été moins réussie.

Méthode pour les QCM C1 :

  • lisez d'abord les questions et repérez celles qui portent sur l'attitude, l'implicite ou le sens d'une expression ;
  • pour chaque question, retrouvez le passage exact (les questions suivent l'ordre du texte) ;
  • méfiez-vous des options qui exagèrent (certainly, entirely, guaranteed) : les textes C1 sont nuancés, la bonne réponse l'est aussi ;
  • éliminez les options qui reprennent les mots du texte mais inversent la relation logique (cause/conséquence, qui fait quoi).

Enfin, gardez en tête que le vocabulaire financier (guidance, covenant, net debt, impairment, attributable) est souvent testé à travers une reformulation plutôt qu'à travers une définition directe.

Langue clé

AnglaisFrançaisUsage
On an underlying basis, profit rose by 4%.Hors éléments exceptionnels, le bénéfice a progressé de 4 %.signale un résultat retraité, à distinguer du résultat publié
We remain cautiously optimistic about the second half.Nous restons prudemment optimistes pour le second semestre.optimisme limité, assorti de réserves
We do not expect conditions to improve materially.Nous ne prévoyons pas d'amélioration significative de la conjoncture.annonce prudente d'une situation qui reste difficile
With hindsight, we were too slow to adapt.Avec le recul, nous avons tardé à nous adapter.marqueur d'autocritique
Future distributions will be assessed in light of…Les distributions futures seront examinées au regard de…laisse entendre qu'un dividende pourrait baisser
While we support the direction of travel, the pace of change…Si nous soutenons l'orientation générale, le rythme des changements…concession suivie d'une réserve : l'avis réel est dans la seconde partie

Vocabulaire

TermeTraductionExemple
impairment chargedépréciation d'actifs (charge comptable)A non-cash impairment charge of €71 million weighed on reported results.
underlying profitbénéfice retraité, hors éléments exceptionnelsUnderlying profit was ahead of guidance despite the reported loss.
guidanceprévisions communiquées au marchéWe have raised our full-year guidance for the second time.
headwindsvents contraires, facteurs défavorablesCurrency headwinds reduced revenue by 3%.
covenantclause financière d'un contrat de prêtNet debt remains comfortably within our banking covenants.
net debtdette netteNet debt fell to €210 million at year end.
final dividendsolde du dividendeThe Board recommends a final dividend of 18 cents per share.
like-for-like salesventes à périmètre constantLike-for-like sales grew by 2.5%.
attributable to shareholdersrevenant aux actionnaires (part du groupe)Profit attributable to shareholders was €45 million.
one-off itemélément non récurrentExcluding one-off items, margins were stable.
to right-sizeredimensionner (souvent : réduire les effectifs)We have right-sized our European cost base.
resilientrésilient, qui résiste bienOur service division proved resilient.
forward-looking statementdéclaration prospectiveThis report contains forward-looking statements that involve risks.
disingenuousde mauvaise foi, peu sincèreIt would be disingenuous to call this a good year.

Dialogue : Décoder une lettre aux actionnaires avant une réunion d'investisseurs

Salle de réunion d'une société de gestion à Édimbourg. Une analyste senior prépare avec un analyste junior une réunion avec la direction d'un armateur coté.

PersonnageRépliqueTraduction
Fiona GalbraithRight, Daniel, you've read the CEO's letter. First impressions?Bon, Daniel, tu as lu la lettre de la directrice générale. Premières impressions ?
Daniel OseiHonestly, it reads quite well. A loss, but underlying profit beat guidance.Franchement, elle se lit plutôt bien. Une perte, mais le résultat retraité dépasse les prévisions.
Fiona GalbraithThat's exactly the impression it's designed to leave. Which figure do they lead with?C'est exactement l'impression qu'elle cherche à laisser. Quel chiffre mettent-ils en avant ?
Daniel OseiThe reported loss, actually. Then they move straight on to the impairment.La perte publiée, en fait. Puis ils passent directement à la dépréciation.
Fiona GalbraithGood. They're getting the bad news out of the way before framing it. That's a deliberate choice.Bien. Ils évacuent la mauvaise nouvelle avant de la mettre en perspective. C'est un choix délibéré.
Daniel OseiAnd the dividend is unchanged, so that's positive, isn't it?Et le dividende est inchangé, donc c'est positif, non ?
Fiona GalbraithRead the next sentence. 'Future distributions will be assessed in light of the investment requirements.'Lis la phrase suivante : « Les distributions futures seront examinées au regard des besoins d'investissement. »
Daniel OseiAh. So they're keeping it this year but preparing us for a cut.Ah. Donc ils le maintiennent cette année mais nous préparent à une baisse.
Fiona GalbraithThat's how I'd read it. Nobody writes that sentence if they're planning to raise it.C'est ma lecture. Personne n'écrit cette phrase s'il compte l'augmenter.
Daniel OseiWhat about the paragraph on regulation? It sounds supportive.Et le paragraphe sur la réglementation ? Il semble favorable.
Fiona GalbraithLook at the structure: 'while we support the direction of travel'. What comes after 'while'?Regarde la structure : « si nous soutenons l'orientation générale ». Qu'est-ce qui vient après « while » ?
Daniel OseiA complaint about the pace. So the real message is frustration with the regulator.Une critique sur le rythme. Donc le vrai message, c'est l'agacement envers le régulateur.
Fiona GalbraithPrecisely. Polite on the surface, critical underneath. Put that on our list of questions.Exactement. Courtois en surface, critique en dessous. Ajoute-le à notre liste de questions.
Daniel OseiI'll also ask what 'not materially' means in numbers for the first half.Je demanderai aussi ce que « pas significativement » représente en chiffres pour le premier semestre.
Fiona GalbraithPerfect. Make them translate the hedging into figures. That's our job.Parfait. Oblige-les à traduire leurs précautions oratoires en chiffres. C'est notre métier.

Exercices corrigés

Exercice 1 — C1-M3-L1-I1 (C2, C1.1)

Lisez la lettre aux actionnaires puis répondez aux questions. Les questions suivent l'ordre du texte.

Letter from the Chief Executive
Halvorsen Maritime plc — Annual Report 2025

Dear Shareholders,

It would be disingenuous to describe 2025 as anything other than a demanding year for Halvorsen Maritime. Freight rates on our core North Sea and Baltic routes fell by an average of 14% as new capacity entered the market, and the cost of complying with tighter emissions rules rose faster than we had anticipated. Against that backdrop, I am nonetheless proud of the way our crews and shore-based teams responded.

On a reported basis, the Group recorded a loss before tax of €38 million, compared with a profit of €52 million in 2024. This headline figure, however, includes a non-cash impairment charge of €71 million relating to four older vessels that we have decided to retire earlier than planned. Excluding this item, underlying profit before tax was €33 million — lower than last year, but comfortably ahead of the guidance we issued in July.

Some of you have asked why we chose to recognise the impairment now rather than spreading the impact over several years. The answer is simple: we would rather face the economics of our fleet squarely than carry assets on our balance sheet at values the market would not support. The decision also clears the way for the fleet renewal programme described on pages 22 to 27.

The Board is recommending a final dividend of 18 cents per share, leaving the total for the year unchanged. We considered this carefully. Our net debt remains well within our covenants, and we believe that a stable dividend signals our confidence in the Group's cash generation. Shareholders should, however, understand that future distributions will be assessed in light of the investment requirements of the renewal programme.

Looking ahead, we do not expect market conditions to improve materially in the first half of 2026. The regulatory environment will also continue to evolve, and while we support the direction of travel, the pace of change has at times left operators little room to plan. Our priority is therefore to protect margins through disciplined cost control and to secure long-term charters with our largest industrial customers.

I would like to thank our people for their commitment, and you, our shareholders, for your continued support through a year that tested us all.

Ingrid Solberg
Chief Executive Officer

1. In the first paragraph, how does the CEO present the year 2025?
A. She minimises its difficulties in order to reassure investors about the Group's future prospects.
B. She suggests that the difficulties were entirely foreseeable.
C. She attributes the poor results mainly to the crews' performance.
D. She admits it was hard but praises how staff responded.

2. According to the letter, the reported loss is mainly due to
A. a fall in underlying profit below the July guidance.
B. a one-time accounting charge on vessels that will be withdrawn early.
C. the cost of complying with new emissions rules.
D. a sharp increase in the Group's net debt.

3. What does the phrase “face the economics of our fleet squarely” suggest?
A. Honestly accepting what the old vessels are worth.
B. Selling the whole fleet quickly before its market value falls any further.
C. Asking customers to share the cost of the vessels.
D. Spreading the cost of the vessels over several years.

4. What is implied about future dividends?
A. They will be increased once the renewal programme is complete.
B. They are guaranteed at 18 cents per share.
C. They could be reduced if investment needs require it.
D. They will be suspended in the first half of 2026.

5. What is the CEO's attitude towards the new regulations?
A. She rejects their objectives as unrealistic.
B. She backs their aim but doubts their pace.
C. She considers that they have had no real impact on the way operators plan their activities.
D. She expects them to push freight rates up in 2026.

Corrigé

1. D — She admits it was hard but praises how staff responded.. « It would be disingenuous to describe 2025 as anything other than a demanding year » = il serait malhonnête de dire autre chose : elle reconnaît franchement la difficulté, puis « I am nonetheless proud » salue les équipes. L'option « minimises » dit le contraire ; quant au caractère prévisible, le texte dit que les coûts ont augmenté « faster than we had anticipated ».
2. B — a one-time accounting charge on vessels that will be withdrawn early.. La perte publiée de 38 M€ inclut une dépréciation « non-cash » de 71 M€ sur quatre navires retirés plus tôt que prévu ; hors cet élément, le bénéfice est de 33 M€. Le piège porte sur la guidance : le résultat retraité est « comfortably ahead of » la prévision de juillet, pas en dessous.
3. A — Honestly accepting what the old vessels are worth.. « squarely » = de front, sans détour : la direction préfère reconnaître la vraie valeur des navires plutôt que de les garder au bilan à une valeur que le marché ne justifie pas. L'étalement sur plusieurs années est précisément l'option qu'elle a écartée.
4. C — They could be reduced if investment needs require it.. « future distributions will be assessed in light of the investment requirements » prépare les actionnaires à une possible baisse, sans l'annoncer. « guaranteed » est trop fort ; aucune suspension n'est annoncée.
5. B — She backs their aim but doubts their pace.. Structure concessive : « while we support the direction of travel » (accord sur l'orientation), « the pace of change has at times left operators little room to plan » (réserve sur le rythme). Elle ne rejette pas les objectifs : c'est le piège principal.

Exercice 2 — C1-M3-L1-I2 (C2, C1.2)

Lisez la déclaration du président du conseil d'administration et répondez aux questions dans l'ordre du texte.

Chair's Statement
Corvane Systems plc — Annual Report 2025

This is my first statement to you as Chair, and I want to begin by being clear about where the company stands. Corvane has excellent engineers, loyal customers and a product portfolio that remains highly regarded in the industrial automation market. What it has lacked in recent years is focus.

Between 2021 and 2024, the Group expanded into eleven new countries and launched four new product lines. Each decision could be justified on its own terms. Taken together, however, they stretched management attention and capital to a point where execution suffered. Revenue grew, but margins fell in three consecutive years, and our two largest acquisitions have yet to deliver the returns set out when they were approved.

In October, Mark Ellery stepped down as Chief Executive after nine years. The Board is grateful to Mark for his contribution to the Group's early growth and for the energy he brought to building our international presence. We were fortunate to appoint Priya Raman, previously Chief Operating Officer of a leading European controls business, as his successor. Priya has spent her first months listening to customers and colleagues, and she will set out her priorities at our Capital Markets Day in March.

The Board itself has changed. Two directors who had served for more than nine years did not seek re-election, and we have appointed two independent non-executive directors with deep experience in operations and capital allocation. I believe the Board now has the right balance of continuity and challenge. Our shareholders have, rightly, asked us to be more demanding of management, and we intend to be.

I do not want to understate the work ahead. Some of the markets we entered will not reach sufficient scale, and we will need to make difficult choices about them. Those choices will be guided by one question: where can Corvane earn attractive returns over time? We will not pursue growth for its own sake.

Finally, I would like to thank all our employees, who have continued to serve customers with professionalism during a period of considerable change.

Helena Marchetti
Chair

1. According to the Chair, what has been the company's main weakness?
A. The quality of its engineering teams.
B. A lack of customer loyalty in its core market.
C. An excessive dispersion of effort and resources.
D. An outdated product portfolio.

2. What does the Chair imply about the expansion decisions taken between 2021 and 2024?
A. They were reasonable one by one but damaging as a whole.
B. They were taken without the Board's approval.
C. They were all mistakes that should never have been made.
D. They were successful overall, since revenue continued to grow throughout the period.

3. How should the Board's thanks to Mark Ellery most probably be interpreted?
A. As unreserved praise for everything he achieved during his nine years as Chief Executive.
B. As polite praise limited to his early years.
C. As an announcement that he will remain on the Board.
D. As criticism of his successor's lack of experience.

4. In the fourth paragraph, the phrase “the right balance of continuity and challenge” refers to
A. a Board composed only of new directors.
B. the need to replace the Chief Executive every nine years.
C. a mix of experienced members and new directors able to question management.
D. a compromise between shareholders and employees.

5. What does the final part of the statement suggest about the coming year?
A. Some recent markets will probably be abandoned.
B. The Group will accelerate its expansion into new countries.
C. The new CEO has already announced a detailed list of the markets the Group will exit.
D. Employees should expect significant salary increases.

Corrigé

1. C — An excessive dispersion of effort and resources.. « What it has lacked in recent years is focus » puis l'énumération (onze pays, quatre gammes) qui ont « stretched management attention and capital ». Les ingénieurs, les clients et les produits sont au contraire présentés comme des atouts.
2. A — They were reasonable one by one but damaging as a whole.. « Each decision could be justified on its own terms. Taken together, however… execution suffered. » : chaque décision était défendable isolément, c'est leur accumulation qui a nui. « all mistakes » est trop catégorique ; la croissance du chiffre d'affaires est mise en balance avec la baisse des marges.
3. B — As polite praise limited to his early years.. Remercier pour la contribution à la « early growth » (la croissance des débuts) et à l'expansion internationale, que le texte vient de critiquer, revient à suggérer en creux que la période récente a été moins réussie. Ce n'est donc pas un éloge sans réserve.
4. C — a mix of experienced members and new directors able to question management.. Le paragraphe décrit le départ de deux administrateurs anciens et l'arrivée de deux indépendants : la « continuity » vient des membres restants, le « challenge » des nouveaux, chargés d'être « more demanding of management ». Le conseil n'est pas entièrement renouvelé.
5. A — Some recent markets will probably be abandoned.. « Some of the markets we entered will not reach sufficient scale, and we will need to make difficult choices about them » laisse entendre des retraits, sans les annoncer formellement. Le piège : la nouvelle directrice n'a encore rien annoncé, elle présentera ses priorités en mars.

Exercice 3 — C1-M3-L1-I3 (C2, C1.1)

Lisez l'extrait de la section « Perspectives et principaux risques » d'un rapport annuel et répondez aux questions.

Outlook and Principal Risks
Ardent Biofoods N.V. — Annual Report 2025 (extract)

Trading in the first weeks of the new financial year has been broadly in line with our expectations. Volumes in our plant-based dairy range continue to grow, albeit at a more measured pace than in 2024, when demand benefited from an exceptional promotional programme with two major retailers. We therefore expect revenue growth in 2026 to be in the mid-single digits, compared with 11% in the year under review.

Input costs remain the most significant uncertainty. Oat and pea protein prices have stabilised since the summer, but they remain some 20% above their five-year average, and our hedging arrangements cover only the first half of the year. Should prices rise again in the autumn, we would seek to recover part of the increase through pricing, although our ability to do so will depend on the competitive environment in each market. We are not, at this stage, in a position to quantify the potential impact with any precision.

The Board has also reviewed the risk associated with customer concentration. Our three largest customers accounted for 46% of revenue in 2025, up from 41% the previous year. These relationships are long-standing and, in our view, mutually beneficial; nonetheless, the loss or significant renegotiation of any one of them would have a material adverse effect on the Group's results. Diversifying our customer base, notably through the food-service channel, is one of the objectives of the strategy presented on page 14.

Regarding regulation, proposed changes to labelling rules for plant-based products in two of our markets could require us to rename several items. We have engaged constructively with the authorities and believe that any changes can be managed within existing budgets, provided that a reasonable transition period is granted.

Taking these factors into account, the Board remains cautiously optimistic. The fundamentals of the category are sound, our brands are well positioned, and our balance sheet gives us the flexibility to continue investing through the cycle.

1. Why do the directors expect slower revenue growth in 2026?
A. Because consumers are losing interest in plant-based products.
B. Because 2025 benefited from a one-off promotion.
C. Because two major retailers have decided to stop selling the plant-based dairy range altogether.
D. Because the company has decided to raise its prices.

2. What does the report suggest about input costs?
A. The company is fully protected against any rise in input prices for the whole of 2026 thanks to its hedging.
B. Prices have returned to their five-year average.
C. The company has already raised its prices to offset them.
D. The company's protection against price rises is incomplete and their impact cannot yet be measured.

3. How do the directors present the relationship with their three largest customers?
A. As valuable but a source of serious risk.
B. As deteriorating and likely to be renegotiated soon.
C. As a risk that has decreased, since the three customers now account for a smaller share of revenue.
D. As a reason to abandon the food-service channel.

4. In the last paragraph, “cautiously optimistic” indicates that the Board
A. expects results to exceed all its previous forecasts.
B. has serious doubts about the future of the category.
C. is confident overall but unwilling to make firm commitments.
D. plans to reduce investment until the cycle improves.

Corrigé

1. B — Because 2025 benefited from a one-off promotion.. La croissance de l'année écoulée « benefited from an exceptional promotional programme » : la base de comparaison est donc gonflée. Les volumes continuent de croître, ce qui exclut la perte d'intérêt des consommateurs ; les distributeurs n'ont pas cessé de vendre la gamme.
2. D — The company's protection against price rises is incomplete and their impact cannot yet be measured.. Les couvertures ne portent que sur le premier semestre et « we are not, at this stage, in a position to quantify the potential impact ». « fully protected » est faux ; les prix restent 20 % au-dessus de la moyenne ; la hausse des prix de vente n'est qu'une hypothèse (« Should prices rise… we would seek to… »).
3. A — As valuable but a source of serious risk.. « long-standing and… mutually beneficial; nonetheless, the loss… would have a material adverse effect » : jugement positif, puis concession sur le risque. La part de ces clients est passée de 41 % à 46 % : le risque a augmenté, il n'a pas diminué.
4. C — is confident overall but unwilling to make firm commitments.. « cautiously optimistic » = optimisme réel mais mesuré, sans engagement ferme, ce que confirme la liste des incertitudes. Le texte dit au contraire que le bilan permet de « continue investing through the cycle ».

Exercice 4 — C1-M3-L1-I4 (C2, C1.1)

Complétez cet extrait de rapport annuel avec le terme qui convient dans chaque liste.

Despite currency [1] _____ that reduced reported revenue by 3%, like-for-like sales grew by 4.2%. The reported loss reflects a non-cash [2] _____ charge on our Latin American assets; on an [3] _____ basis, operating profit rose by 6%. Net debt remains comfortably within our banking [4] _____, and we are therefore confirming our full-year [5] _____. Profit [6] _____ to shareholders reached €45 million.

[1] tailwinds / headwinds / downturns / setbacks

[2] impairment / depreciation / write-up / allowance

[3] outlying / undermining / overall / underlying

[4] conventions / convenants / covenants / commitments

[5] guidelines / guidance / forecasting / advice

[6] attributable / attributed / allocated / accountable

Corrigé

[1] headwinds. « currency headwinds » = effets de change défavorables, cohérent avec la baisse de 3 %. « tailwinds » désigne au contraire des facteurs favorables.
[2] impairment. « impairment charge » = dépréciation exceptionnelle d'un actif. « depreciation » désigne l'amortissement régulier, et non une charge ponctuelle liée à une perte de valeur.
[3] underlying. « on an underlying basis » = hors éléments exceptionnels, ce qui explique la hausse malgré la perte publiée. « overall » ne marquerait pas le retraitement.
[4] covenants. Les « banking covenants » sont les ratios financiers imposés par les prêteurs. « convenants » est une faute d'orthographe fréquente ; « commitments » est trop général.
[5] guidance. « full-year guidance » = prévisions annuelles communiquées au marché. « guidelines » signifie lignes directrices, règles à suivre.
[6] attributable. Expression figée : « profit attributable to shareholders » (résultat part du groupe). « attributed » ne s'emploie pas dans cette formule comptable.

title: C1-M3 — Éditoriaux et tribunes économiques : repérer la position et le ton de l'auteur
description: Distinguer dans une tribune de 350 à 450 mots l'opinion de l'auteur des points de vue qu'il rapporte pour les discuter. Qualifier le ton d'un éditorial (sceptique, ironique, mesuré, alarmiste, conciliant) à l'aide d'au moins deux indices textuels. Expliquer le sens en contexte d'au moins quatre expressions idiomatiques de la presse économique, avec au moins 75 % de réponses correctes aux QCM.
