sections.title: C1-M3-L5 — Politiques internes : ESG, conformité et lancement d'alerte
sections.contentHtml:
Objectifs :

  • Repérer dans une politique interne de 350 à 450 mots le champ d'application, les obligations, les seuils et les exceptions.
  • Distinguer le degré de contrainte exprimé par must, are required to, should, are expected to et are encouraged to.
  • Évaluer la précision d'un engagement ESG (cible chiffrée, échéance, périmètre) et repérer au moins deux formulations vagues, avec au moins 75 % de réponses correctes aux QCM.

Compétence C2 — niveau C1.1 — 40 min

Les politiques internes (policies, codes of conduct, procedures) sont des textes normatifs : elles disent qui doit faire quoi, dans quelles limites et avec quelles conséquences. Les politiques ESG (environnement, social, gouvernance), elles, mêlent souvent engagement réel et communication. Au niveau C1, vous devez savoir mesurer la force d'une règle et la précision d'un engagement.

1. La structure type. Purpose (objet), Scope (à qui et à quoi s'applique la politique), Definitions, Policy statement (règles), Roles and responsibilities, Reporting / Speaking up, Breaches (sanctions), Review (date de révision). Une question classique porte sur le champ d'application : la politique vise-t-elle aussi les sous-traitants, les intérimaires, les membres du conseil ?

2. L'échelle de contrainte. Du plus fort au plus faible :

  • must / shall / are required to / may not : obligation ou interdiction ;
  • should / are expected to : règle attendue, mais un écart justifié est possible ;
  • are encouraged to / may wish to : simple recommandation.

Les distracteurs transforment souvent une recommandation en obligation, ou l'inverse.

3. Seuils et exceptions. Les politiques anticorruption fixent des seuils (gifts with a value of more than €75), des procédures (must be recorded in the gifts register, require prior approval from) et des exceptions (except where…, other than). Lisez chaque chiffre avec sa condition : un cadeau peut être autorisé mais devoir être déclaré.

4. Les engagements ESG : précis ou flous ? Un engagement crédible comporte une cible chiffrée, une échéance, une année de référence et un périmètre (a 42% reduction in Scope 1 and 2 emissions by 2030 against a 2022 baseline). À l'inverse, les formules we aim to, where feasible, we are exploring, ambition, climate-positive ou un recours massif à la compensation (offsetting) signalent un engagement plus faible, voire un risque d'écoblanchiment (greenwashing). Les Scope 3 emissions (chaîne de valeur : fournisseurs, usage des produits) sont souvent les plus importantes… et les plus souvent exclues.

5. Le lancement d'alerte (speak-up / whistleblowing). Repérez les canaux (line manager, compliance team, independent hotline), la possibilité d'anonymat, la protection contre les représailles (retaliation) et la notion de bonne foi (reasonable belief) : on est protégé même si l'alerte se révèle infondée, tant qu'elle était sincère.

6. L'implicite. Une politique qui insiste lourdement sur un point (we wish to remind all staff that…) révèle souvent un incident passé. Une note de conformité qui dit recent events have shown signale un problème sans le nommer.

Méthode : soulignez les modaux, encadrez les chiffres et leurs conditions, puis vérifiez pour chaque question la personne concernée et le degré d'obligation. Les réponses fausses sont souvent « presque justes » : bonne règle, mauvais seuil ; bon seuil, mauvaise catégorie de personnel.

Langue clé

AnglaisFrançaisUsage
This policy applies to all employees, contractors and directors.La présente politique s'applique à tous les salariés, prestataires et administrateurs.définit le champ d'application
Employees must not accept cash or cash equivalents.Il est interdit aux salariés d'accepter des espèces ou équivalents.interdiction stricte
Managers are expected to lead by example.Les managers sont censés montrer l'exemple.attente forte, moins contraignante que must
Staff are encouraged to raise concerns at an early stage.Le personnel est invité à faire part de ses préoccupations au plus tôt.simple recommandation
…against a 2022 baseline…par rapport à l'année de référence 2022élément de précision d'un objectif ESG
No one will suffer retaliation for raising a concern in good faith.Personne ne subira de représailles pour avoir signalé un problème de bonne foi.protection du lanceur d'alerte

Vocabulaire

TermeTraductionExemple
scope (of a policy)champ d'applicationTemporary staff fall within the scope of this policy.
hospitalityinvitations (repas, événements)Hospitality above €150 requires prior approval.
gifts registerregistre des cadeauxAll gifts over €75 must be entered in the gifts register.
facilitation paymentpaiement de facilitation (petit pot-de-vin)Facilitation payments are prohibited in all circumstances.
conflict of interestconflit d'intérêtsDeclare any conflict of interest to your manager.
whistleblowing / speaking uplancement d'alerteOur speak-up hotline is run by an independent provider.
retaliationreprésaillesRetaliation against whistleblowers is a disciplinary offence.
in good faithde bonne foiYou are protected if you report in good faith.
baseline yearannée de référenceTargets are measured against a 2022 baseline year.
Scope 3 emissionsémissions indirectes de la chaîne de valeur (scope 3)Scope 3 emissions represent 85% of our footprint.
offsettingcompensation (carbone)Offsetting should be a last resort, not a strategy.
greenwashingécoblanchimentVague claims expose the company to accusations of greenwashing.
breachmanquement, violationBreaches may lead to disciplinary action.
due diligencevérifications préalables (diligence raisonnable)Due diligence is required before appointing an agent.

Dialogue : Engagement climat : ambitieux ou flou ?

Réunion en visioconférence entre la responsable RSE d'une enseigne de distribution et un administrateur indépendant qui relit le projet de politique climat avant publication.

PersonnageRépliqueTraduction
Richard OkaforSophie, I've read the draft climate policy. The headline is 'net zero by 2040'. What exactly is covered?Sophie, j'ai lu le projet de politique climat. Le titre annonce « zéro émission nette en 2040 ». Qu'est-ce qui est couvert exactement ?
Sophie LindgrenOur stores, warehouses and vehicles — Scope 1 and 2.Nos magasins, entrepôts et véhicules — les scopes 1 et 2.
Richard OkaforAnd Scope 3? Our suppliers and the products we sell?Et le scope 3 ? Nos fournisseurs et les produits que nous vendons ?
Sophie LindgrenThat's where it gets difficult. The draft says we 'aim to engage suppliers where feasible'.C'est là que ça se complique. Le projet dit que nous « visons à mobiliser les fournisseurs lorsque c'est possible ».
Richard OkaforWhich, if I'm honest, commits us to almost nothing. How big is Scope 3 for us?Ce qui, honnêtement, ne nous engage quasiment à rien. Que représente le scope 3 pour nous ?
Sophie LindgrenAround eighty-five per cent of our total footprint.Environ quatre-vingt-cinq pour cent de notre empreinte totale.
Richard OkaforSo the headline target covers fifteen per cent of the problem. Journalists will spot that immediately.Donc l'objectif phare couvre quinze pour cent du problème. Les journalistes le verront tout de suite.
Sophie LindgrenI agree. I argued for a numerical Scope 3 target, but finance was worried about committing too early.Je suis d'accord. J'ai plaidé pour un objectif chiffré sur le scope 3, mais la finance craignait de s'engager trop tôt.
Richard OkaforUnderstandable. But a modest, precise target is more credible than a grand, vague one.Compréhensible. Mais un objectif modeste et précis est plus crédible qu'un objectif grandiose et flou.
Sophie LindgrenWhat if we committed to a thirty per cent reduction in Scope 3 by 2032, against a 2023 baseline?Et si nous nous engagions sur une réduction de trente pour cent du scope 3 d'ici 2032, par rapport à 2023 ?
Richard OkaforThat I could defend in front of investors. And the offsetting paragraph?Ça, je pourrais le défendre devant les investisseurs. Et le paragraphe sur la compensation ?
Sophie LindgrenIt currently says offsets 'may play a role'. I'd like to add that they won't count towards the reduction targets.Il dit actuellement que la compensation « peut jouer un rôle ». J'aimerais préciser qu'elle ne comptera pas dans les objectifs de réduction.
Richard OkaforGood. Put both changes in a revised draft and I'll support it at the board.Bien. Mets les deux modifications dans un nouveau projet et je le soutiendrai au conseil.
Sophie LindgrenThank you. I'll circulate it by Thursday.Merci. Je le diffuserai d'ici jeudi.

Exercices corrigés

Exercice 1 — C1-M3-L5-I1 (C2, C1.1)

Lisez la politique « cadeaux et invitations » et répondez aux questions dans l'ordre du texte.

MERIDALE RETAIL GROUP — GIFTS, HOSPITALITY AND ANTI-BRIBERY POLICY (Version 4, effective 1 March 2026)

  1. Purpose and scope

Meridale is committed to conducting business honestly and without the use of bribery in any form. This policy applies to all employees, temporary workers, contractors acting on our behalf and members of the Board. It covers gifts and hospitality both given and received, in every country in which we operate, including where local custom may suggest otherwise.

  1. General principles

Gifts and hospitality may be given or accepted only if they are reasonable, proportionate and not intended to influence a business decision. Employees must never offer or accept cash or cash equivalents, such as vouchers or gift cards, regardless of value. Facilitation payments — small unofficial payments made to speed up a routine government action — are prohibited in all circumstances, even where they are commonly expected.

  1. Thresholds and approval

Gifts with a value of up to €75 may be accepted without approval but must be recorded in the online gifts register within five working days. Gifts above €75, and any hospitality with a value above €150 per person, require the prior written approval of the employee's line manager. Where the value exceeds €500, approval must also be obtained from the Compliance team. Employees who are directly involved in an ongoing tender process must not accept any gift or hospitality from a participating supplier, whatever its value, until the contract has been awarded.

  1. Public officials

Any gift or hospitality offered to a public official, of any value, must be approved in advance by the Compliance team.

  1. Raising concerns

Employees who are unsure whether a gift is acceptable are encouraged to seek advice from their manager or from Compliance before accepting it. Any suspected breach of this policy should be reported through the channels described in our Speak-Up Policy.

  1. Breaches

Breaches of this policy will be treated as serious disciplinary matters and may result in dismissal. Where appropriate, the Group will also inform the relevant authorities.

We wish to remind colleagues in Buying and Merchandising that supplier-funded travel, including visits to factories and trade fairs, falls within the scope of this policy and must be approved in line with section 3.

1. According to section 1, who is covered by the policy?
A. Permanent employees only.
B. Employees and temporary workers, but not contractors or members of the Board.
C. All staff, contractors acting for the company and Board members.
D. Only staff working in countries where bribery is common.

2. An employee is offered a €50 gift card by a supplier. What should he do?
A. Accept it and record it in the gifts register.
B. Ask his line manager for prior approval.
C. Accept it, since its value is below the €75 threshold set out in section 3.
D. Decline it, as cash equivalents are never allowed.

3. A buyer working on a current tender is invited to a €90 dinner by one of the bidding suppliers. What does the policy require?
A. She must refuse the invitation until the contract has been awarded.
B. She may accept it after recording it in the register.
C. She needs her line manager's approval only.
D. She needs approval from both her manager and Compliance.

4. In section 5, what does “are encouraged to” indicate?
A. A strict obligation that applies to all gifts.
B. A recommendation to ask for advice in case of doubt.
C. A prohibition on accepting any gift whatsoever without the prior approval of Compliance.
D. An obligation that applies only to managers.

5. What does the final reminder suggest?
A. Supplier-funded travel was previously exempt from the policy.
B. Buying and Merchandising staff are no longer allowed to visit suppliers' factories or attend trade fairs.
C. The policy has recently been extended to trade fairs abroad only.
D. Some staff may have ignored the rules for such trips.

Corrigé

1. C — All staff, contractors acting for the company and Board members.. La politique vise « all employees, temporary workers, contractors acting on our behalf and members of the Board », dans tous les pays. Les intérimaires et prestataires sont inclus, ce qui exclut « permanent employees only ».
2. D — Decline it, as cash equivalents are never allowed.. Les « cash equivalents, such as vouchers or gift cards » sont interdits « regardless of value ». Le seuil de 75 € ne s'applique pas : c'est le distracteur le plus tentant.
3. A — She must refuse the invitation until the contract has been awarded.. La règle spécifique aux appels d'offres l'emporte : « must not accept any gift or hospitality from a participating supplier, whatever its value, until the contract has been awarded ». Sans appel d'offres en cours, 90 € resterait sous le seuil de 150 € pour les invitations.
4. B — A recommendation to ask for advice in case of doubt.. « are encouraged to » exprime une recommandation, plus faible que « must » ou « are required to ». Elle vise les salariés qui ont un doute, non tous les cadeaux.
5. D — Some staff may have ignored the rules for such trips.. « We wish to remind… » vise un service précis : cela laisse entendre que les règles n'étaient pas toujours appliquées aux voyages payés par les fournisseurs. Les visites ne sont pas interdites, elles doivent être approuvées ; rien n'indique une exemption antérieure.

Exercice 2 — C1-M3-L5-I2 (C2, C1.2)

Lisez la déclaration de politique climat et répondez aux questions. Évaluez la précision des engagements.

Corrigan Foods plc — Climate Policy Statement 2026

Our commitment
At Corrigan Foods, we believe that a healthy planet and a healthy business go hand in hand. As one of Europe's leading producers of chilled ready meals, we recognise that our activities have an impact on the climate, and we are determined to play our part in the transition to a low-carbon economy.

Operational emissions
We will reduce absolute Scope 1 and Scope 2 greenhouse gas emissions from our factories, warehouses and vehicle fleet by 50% by 2030 against a 2021 baseline, and reach net zero across these operations by 2040. Progress against this target will be verified annually by an independent assurance provider and published in our Sustainability Report. Since 2021, we have already reduced these emissions by 18%, mainly by switching four of our seven sites to renewable electricity.

Value chain emissions
The majority of our footprint — around 88% — lies outside our direct control, in agriculture, packaging and the refrigeration of our products in stores and homes. We aim to work collaboratively with our suppliers and customers to reduce these emissions over time, and we are exploring a range of initiatives, including regenerative farming pilots and lighter packaging, where commercially feasible.

Carbon offsetting
We recognise that some residual emissions will be difficult to eliminate. High-quality, independently certified offsets may therefore play a role in our journey to net zero. Offsets will not, however, be counted towards our 2030 operational reduction target.

Governance
The Board's Sustainability Committee oversees this policy. From 2027, a portion of the annual bonus of the executive team will be linked to progress on operational emissions. The Committee will review this policy every two years, or sooner if regulatory requirements or scientific guidance change significantly.

Our ambition is to become a climate-positive business, giving back more to nature than we take.

1. Which commitment in the text is the most precise?
A. The commitment to become a climate-positive business.
B. The commitment on value chain emissions.
C. The commitment to reduce operational emissions by 50% by 2030.
D. The commitment to play a part in the low-carbon transition.

2. What can be said about the section on value chain emissions?
A. It covers a small share of the footprint and is therefore less important.
B. It covers most of the footprint but sets no measurable target.
C. It sets a 2040 net zero target for suppliers.
D. It is verified each year by an independent assurance provider and published in the Sustainability Report.

3. What does the policy say about carbon offsets?
A. They will be used to meet the 2030 target.
B. They will be excluded altogether from the company's strategy for reaching net zero by 2040.
C. They will replace efforts to reduce operational emissions.
D. They may be used for residual emissions but not to achieve the 2030 reduction target.

4. How would a critical reader most probably regard the final sentence?
A. As an unsupported, mainly rhetorical claim.
B. As the most rigorous part of the policy.
C. As evidence that the company already removes more carbon from the atmosphere than it emits each year.
D. As a legal obligation enforced by the Board.

Corrigé

1. C — The commitment to reduce operational emissions by 50% by 2030.. C'est le seul engagement assorti d'un chiffre (50 %), d'une échéance (2030), d'une année de référence (2021), d'un périmètre (scopes 1 et 2) et d'une vérification indépendante. Les autres restent généraux.
2. B — It covers most of the footprint but sets no measurable target.. Ces émissions représentent environ 88 % de l'empreinte, mais le texte n'emploie que des formules vagues (« we aim to », « we are exploring », « where commercially feasible ») sans chiffre ni échéance. La vérification indépendante concerne les scopes 1 et 2.
3. D — They may be used for residual emissions but not to achieve the 2030 reduction target.. « may therefore play a role » pour les émissions résiduelles, mais « will not… be counted towards our 2030 operational reduction target ». La compensation n'est ni exclue ni substituée à la réduction.
4. A — As an unsupported, mainly rhetorical claim.. « ambition » et « climate-positive » ne sont ni définis ni chiffrés, alors que 88 % de l'empreinte n'a pas d'objectif : un lecteur critique y verrait une formule de communication. Le texte ne dit pas que l'entreprise est déjà « positive ».

Exercice 3 — C1-M3-L5-I3 (C2, C1.1)

Lisez la note de la responsable conformité et répondez aux questions dans l'ordre du texte.

MEMO
To: All staff, Halden Logistics Group
From: Marta Kowalczyk, Chief Compliance Officer
Date: 2 February 2026
Subject: Updated Speak-Up Policy — what has changed and why

Colleagues,

Following the Board's annual review, our Speak-Up Policy has been updated, and the new version takes effect today. I would like to highlight the main changes and, just as importantly, explain the thinking behind them.

First, you can now raise a concern through an independent hotline, operated by an external provider, by telephone or online, 24 hours a day and in eleven languages. You may choose to remain anonymous. Our existing channels — your line manager, HR and the Compliance team — remain available, and many of you will continue to prefer them. That is entirely your choice.

Second, the policy now states explicitly that you do not need proof before speaking up. A reasonable belief that something is wrong is sufficient. If a concern raised in good faith turns out to be unfounded, you will not face any negative consequences. Deliberately false reports, on the other hand, will be treated as a disciplinary matter.

Third, we have strengthened protection against retaliation. Any form of retaliation — including exclusion from meetings, unjustified changes to working hours or negative comments in performance reviews — will be treated as gross misconduct. Managers are expected to be particularly vigilant on this point, and all managers are required to complete a short training module by 31 March.

Why these changes? Our annual staff survey showed that while most colleagues knew how to raise a concern, fewer than half felt confident that they could do so without any impact on their careers. Recent events in parts of our business have also shown that problems which are not raised early tend to become much more serious, and much more costly, later on. A culture in which people speak up is not a sign that something is wrong; it is one of the best indicators that things are being done right.

The full policy is available on the intranet. If you have any questions, please contact me or any member of my team.

Marta Kowalczyk

1. What does the memo say about the existing reporting channels?
A. They have been replaced by the independent hotline.
B. They remain available alongside the new hotline.
C. They can now be used anonymously.
D. They are reserved for managers.

2. According to the memo, what happens to an employee whose honest report proves to be unfounded?
A. The employee will not suffer any negative consequences.
B. The employee will receive a formal warning.
C. The case will be treated as a disciplinary matter.
D. The employee must provide proof before the case is closed.

3. What is the difference between the two obligations placed on managers in the fourth paragraph?
A. Both are recommendations without a deadline.
B. Vigilance is compulsory, but the training is optional.
C. Vigilance is an expectation, while the training is a firm requirement with a deadline.
D. Both apply only to managers in Compliance.

4. What does the reference to “Recent events in parts of our business” suggest?
A. The company has just won an award for its compliance culture.
B. The staff survey results were incorrect.
C. The new independent hotline has already received a large number of reports since it was launched.
D. Problems raised too late became costly.

Corrigé

1. B — They remain available alongside the new hotline.. « Our existing channels… remain available, and many of you will continue to prefer them. » L'anonymat est mentionné pour la nouvelle ligne indépendante, pas pour les canaux internes.
2. A — The employee will not suffer any negative consequences.. « If a concern raised in good faith turns out to be unfounded, you will not face any negative consequences. » Seuls les signalements délibérément faux relèvent du disciplinaire : c'est le piège.
3. C — Vigilance is an expectation, while the training is a firm requirement with a deadline.. « are expected to be particularly vigilant » exprime une attente ; « are required to complete a short training module by 31 March » est une obligation datée. Le texte joue sur cette différence de degré.
4. D — Problems raised too late became costly.. La phrase établit un lien entre ces « événements récents » et le fait que des problèmes non signalés tôt deviennent « much more serious, and much more costly » : elle fait allusion à un incident sans le nommer.

Exercice 4 — C1-M3-L5-I4 (C2, C1.1)

Complétez l'extrait de code de conduite avec le terme qui convient.

This Code applies to all employees and contractors; agents fall within its [1] _____ once they have passed our [2] _____ checks. Any [3] _____ of interest must be declared to your manager. [4] _____ payments are prohibited, even where they are customary. No employee will suffer [5] _____ for reporting a concern in [6] _____. Our climate target is measured against a 2022 [7] _____, and we will not rely on [8] _____ to meet it.

[1] range / scope / scale / field

[2] due diligence / due care / good diligence / fair diligence

[3] clash / collision / contest / conflict

[4] Facility / Facilitating / Facilitation / Expediting

[5] revenge / retaliation / retribution / reprisal

[6] good faith / good will / good belief / fair faith

[7] base rate / benchmark / bottom line / baseline

[8] offloading / outsourcing / offsetting / onsetting

Corrigé

[1] scope. « fall within the scope of » = entrer dans le champ d'application. « range » et « field » ne s'emploient pas dans cette expression.
[2] due diligence. « due diligence checks » = vérifications préalables sur un partenaire. « due care » (prudence requise) n'est pas le terme pour ces contrôles.
[3] conflict. Expression figée : « conflict of interest ». Les autres mots n'entrent pas dans cette collocation.
[4] Facilitation. « facilitation payments » = petits paiements officieux pour accélérer une démarche administrative. « facility payment » désignerait un paiement lié à une ligne de crédit.
[5] retaliation. « retaliation » est le terme consacré des politiques d'alerte. « reprisal » existe mais s'emploie surtout au pluriel (« reprisals ») ; « revenge » relève du registre courant.
[6] good faith. « in good faith » = de bonne foi. « goodwill » signifie bienveillance ou survaleur, sens différent.
[7] baseline. « against a 2022 baseline » = par rapport à l'année de référence 2022. « benchmark » désigne un point de comparaison externe ; « base rate » est un taux directeur.
[8] offsetting. « offsetting » = compensation carbone, que l'entreprise s'interdit d'utiliser pour atteindre son objectif de réduction.

sections.title: C1-M3-L6 — Correspondance sensible : ton, euphémismes et sous-entendus
sections.contentHtml:
Objectifs :

  • Identifier dans un courriel ou un courrier de 300 à 450 mots le message réel derrière les formules de politesse (refus, reproche, menace d'escalade).
  • Repérer au moins quatre procédés d'atténuation ou de mise à distance (litote, passif, conditionnel, formules impersonnelles) et en expliquer l'effet.
  • Qualifier l'évolution du ton d'un échange et l'intention de l'auteur, avec au moins 75 % de réponses correctes aux QCM.

Compétence C2 — niveau C1.2 — 40 min

Dans la correspondance professionnelle délicate — réclamation, refus, mise en cause, réponse à une critique —, les auteurs anglophones (et particulièrement britanniques) disent rarement les choses frontalement. Le message réel se cache derrière des formules polies. Comprendre ces codes est au cœur du niveau C1 : identifier les attitudes et opinions implicites.

1. La litote (understatement). I was a little surprised peut signifier « j'ai été choqué » ; This is not ideal = c'est un vrai problème ; We were somewhat disappointed = nous sommes mécontents. Plus le contexte est grave, plus la litote est forte.

2. Les signaux d'escalade. Repérez :

  • les copies à la hiérarchie (cc: Managing Director) ;
  • For the record, As previously stated, I note that…, As per my email of 3 March : l'auteur constitue un dossier ;
  • I trust that… ou I am sure you will appreciate that… : attente ferme, parfois menaçante ;
  • We reserve the right to…, we will have no option but to… : avertissement formel ;
  • le passage du prénom au nom de famille, ou de Best à Yours sincerely.

3. La mise à distance de la responsabilité. Le passif (mistakes were made, the delivery was delayed) évite de nommer le responsable. We regret any inconvenience this may have caused n'est pas une vraie excuse : elle ne reconnaît ni faute ni conséquence certaine (may have). Comparez avec We are sorry that we failed to…, qui assume.

4. Le refus voilé. We have given your proposal careful consideration annonce souvent un non ; At this stage, for the time being, we will keep your details on file adoucissent un refus qui peut être définitif. Inversement, we would be open to revisiting this if… laisse une porte réellement ouverte : la condition indique ce qu'il faudrait changer.

5. Les formules de demande qui sont des reproches. Could you help me understand why…? ou I would be grateful if you could clarify… sont souvent des demandes d'explication pour une faute présumée. Just to clarify peut corriger poliment une affirmation fausse de l'interlocuteur.

6. Lire l'évolution du ton. Dans une chaîne de courriels, comparez l'ouverture et la clôture de chaque message. Un ton qui devient plus formel, plus bref, avec plus de dates et de références, signale une détérioration de la relation.

Méthode pour les QCM : pour chaque question sur le ton ou l'intention, (1) relevez les marqueurs (litote, passif, copie, conditionnel) ; (2) demandez-vous ce que l'auteur veut obtenir ; (3) éliminez les options trop littérales (« the writer is a little surprised ») ou trop extrêmes (« the writer threatens legal action » quand il ne fait que se réserver des droits). La bonne réponse décrit l'intention réelle, avec le bon degré d'intensité.

Langue clé

AnglaisFrançaisUsage
I must say I was somewhat surprised to learn that…Je dois dire que j'ai été pour le moins surpris d'apprendre que…litote exprimant un fort mécontentement
For the record, the specifications were confirmed on 4 May.Pour mémoire, les spécifications ont été confirmées le 4 mai.l'auteur constitue un dossier : signal d'escalade
I trust this will not happen again.Je compte sur vous pour que cela ne se reproduise pas.attente ferme, avertissement poli
We regret any inconvenience this may have caused.Nous regrettons la gêne que cela a pu occasionner.fausse excuse : ne reconnaît pas de faute
We are not in a position to proceed at this stage.Nous ne sommes pas en mesure de donner suite à ce stade.refus adouci
We would be open to revisiting this if…Nous serions disposés à réexaminer la question si…porte ouverte réelle, assortie d'une condition

Vocabulaire

TermeTraductionExemple
understatementlitote, euphémisme“Not ideal” is a typical British understatement.
to escalatefaire remonter (à la hiérarchie), aggraverIf there is no reply by Friday, I will escalate the matter.
for the recordpour mémoire, pour que ce soit consignéFor the record, we raised this issue in March.
to reserve the right tose réserver le droit deWe reserve the right to claim compensation.
to take something on boardprendre en compteWe have taken your feedback on board.
regrettableregrettable, fâcheuxThe delay is regrettable but was beyond our control.
to deflect blamerejeter la responsabilitéThe reply deflects blame onto the carrier.
veiledvoilé, impliciteThe letter contained a veiled threat.
to set the record straightrétablir les faitsI would like to set the record straight on one point.
goodwillbonne volonté, geste commercialAs a goodwill gesture, we will waive the fee.
tersesec, laconiqueHis reply was terse and formal.
conciliatoryconciliantThe second letter was much more conciliatory.
to be at faultêtre en tortThe supplier does not admit to being at fault.
without prejudicesous toutes réservesThis offer is made without prejudice to our rights.

Dialogue : Lire entre les lignes d'un courriel client

Open space d'un prestataire logistique à Rotterdam. Un chef de compte montre à sa responsable un courriel reçu d'un client important.

PersonnageRépliqueTraduction
Pieter van DijkClaire, have you got a minute? I've had an email from Fenwick Pharma. It's very polite, but something feels off.Claire, tu as une minute ? J'ai reçu un mail de Fenwick Pharma. Il est très poli, mais quelque chose cloche.
Claire Dubois-HartLet me see. Who's it copied to?Montre-moi. Qui est en copie ?
Pieter van DijkTheir Supply Chain Director. She's never been copied before.Leur directrice supply chain. Elle n'avait jamais été en copie.
Claire Dubois-HartThat's your first signal. They're putting this on the record.Voilà ton premier signal. Ils veulent que ce soit consigné.
Pieter van DijkHe says he was 'somewhat surprised' that the shipment arrived outside the temperature range.Il dit avoir été « quelque peu surpris » que l'envoi soit arrivé hors de la plage de température.
Claire Dubois-HartFor a pharma client, 'somewhat surprised' means seriously alarmed. It's understatement.Pour un client pharmaceutique, « quelque peu surpris » veut dire sérieusement inquiet. C'est une litote.
Pieter van DijkAnd he ends with 'I trust we will not need to revisit this conversation.'Et il termine par « Je compte sur vous pour que nous n'ayons pas à revenir sur cette conversation ».
Claire Dubois-HartThat's a polite final warning. Next time, it'll be a formal complaint, or worse, a tender.C'est un dernier avertissement poli. La prochaine fois, ce sera une réclamation formelle, ou pire, un appel d'offres.
Pieter van DijkI was going to reply that we regret any inconvenience this may have caused.J'allais répondre que nous regrettons la gêne que cela a pu occasionner.
Claire Dubois-HartPlease don't. That's a non-apology, and he'll read it as us deflecting blame.Surtout pas. C'est une fausse excuse, et il y verra une façon de nous dédouaner.
Pieter van DijkSo what do I say?Alors, je dis quoi ?
Claire Dubois-HartSay clearly what went wrong, that it was our failure, and exactly what we're changing, with dates.Dis clairement ce qui n'a pas fonctionné, que c'est notre erreur, et exactement ce que nous changeons, avec des dates.
Pieter van DijkAnd copy the director on our reply as well?Et je mets aussi la directrice en copie de notre réponse ?
Claire Dubois-HartYes — and copy me. If they've escalated, we should show we're taking it seriously at the same level.Oui, et mets-moi en copie. S'ils ont fait remonter le sujet, nous devons montrer que nous le prenons au sérieux au même niveau.

Exercices corrigés

Exercice 1 — C1-M3-L6-I1 (C2, C1.2)

Lisez le courriel d'un client et répondez aux questions. Attention aux litotes et aux signaux d'escalade.

From: Jonathan Pryce <j.pryce@fenwickpharma.example>
To: Pieter van Dijk <p.vandijk@elmstead-logistics.example>
Cc: Dr Alison Reeve, Supply Chain Director, Fenwick Pharma
Subject: Shipment FP-2291 — temperature excursion

Dear Mr van Dijk,

Thank you for your call on Tuesday regarding shipment FP-2291. I appreciate you letting us know about the issue before the consignment reached our Utrecht facility, and I recognise that your team acted quickly once the problem was identified.

I must say, however, that I was somewhat surprised to learn that the consignment had spent almost four hours outside the agreed 2–8°C range during the transfer at your Antwerp hub. As you know, these products are temperature-sensitive, and our quality team has had no choice but to quarantine the entire batch pending further testing. At best, this will delay supply to two hospital customers by around ten days. At worst, the batch will have to be destroyed.

For the record, this is the second temperature excursion involving the Antwerp hub in the past six months. Following the first incident in September, we were assured that additional monitoring had been put in place and that staff had received refresher training. I would be grateful if you could help me understand how a similar situation was able to occur despite those measures.

I would therefore ask you to provide, by Friday 14 November, a written report setting out the root cause of the excursion, the corrective actions you intend to take and the timescale for implementing them. We will also need to discuss the question of costs once the test results are available, and we reserve our position on this point.

We have valued our partnership with Elmstead over the past four years, and I have no wish to see it damaged. I trust, however, that you will understand why we cannot simply treat this as a one-off, and that we will not need to revisit this conversation.

Yours sincerely,

Jonathan Pryce
Head of Distribution Quality, Fenwick Pharma

1. What is the purpose of the first paragraph?
A. To withdraw the complaint made by phone on Tuesday.
B. To thank the supplier sincerely for having solved the temperature problem so quickly.
C. To credit the supplier before criticising it.
D. To announce that the batch has been destroyed.

2. What does “I was somewhat surprised” actually convey here?
A. Serious dissatisfaction expressed in a restrained way.
B. Mild curiosity about how the hub operates.
C. Genuine surprise that the shipment arrived early.
D. Indifference to the consequences of the incident.

3. Why does the writer mention the September incident?
A. To show that the problem identified in September has been fully solved since then.
B. To suggest that the corrective measures promised earlier were ineffective.
C. To explain that the September incident was more serious.
D. To thank the supplier for its refresher training.

4. What does “we reserve our position on this point” imply regarding costs?
A. Fenwick will pay all the costs itself.
B. Fenwick has already sent an invoice to Elmstead.
C. Fenwick has decided to take legal action against Elmstead immediately.
D. Fenwick may seek to recover costs from Elmstead later.

5. How would you describe the tone of the final paragraph?
A. Conciliatory but containing a clear warning.
B. Openly hostile and threatening to end the contract immediately.
C. Purely friendly, with no criticism.
D. Apologetic for having copied a director.

Corrigé

1. C — To credit the supplier before criticising it.. Le premier paragraphe reconnaît la réactivité du prestataire, puis « I must say, however… » introduit la critique : c'est une précaution avant le reproche. Le problème n'est pas résolu et le lot n'est pas encore détruit.
2. A — Serious dissatisfaction expressed in a restrained way.. C'est une litote : vu les conséquences décrites (lot en quarantaine, hôpitaux livrés en retard), l'expression traduit un fort mécontentement formulé avec retenue. Une lecture littérale (« mild curiosity ») passe à côté du ton.
3. B — To suggest that the corrective measures promised earlier were ineffective.. « For the record » + « we were assured… » + « how a similar situation was able to occur despite those measures » : il constitue un dossier et met en cause l'efficacité des mesures annoncées. La question polie (« help me understand ») est en réalité un reproche.
4. D — Fenwick may seek to recover costs from Elmstead later.. « reserve our position » = ne pas renoncer à ses droits : une demande d'indemnisation reste possible après les tests. Ce n'est pas encore une action en justice, ce qui serait une lecture excessive.
5. A — Conciliatory but containing a clear warning.. Il valorise le partenariat (« I have no wish to see it damaged ») tout en avertissant (« I trust… we will not need to revisit this conversation ») : conciliant en surface, avertissement en profondeur. Aucune résiliation immédiate n'est annoncée.

Exercice 2 — C1-M3-L6-I2 (C2, C1.2)

Lisez la réponse du prestataire au courriel précédent et répondez aux questions. Comparez la forme et le fond.

From: Martin Hale <m.hale@elmstead-logistics.example>
To: Jonathan Pryce <j.pryce@fenwickpharma.example>
Cc: Dr Alison Reeve; Pieter van Dijk
Subject: RE: Shipment FP-2291 — temperature excursion

Dear Mr Pryce,

Thank you for your email of 10 November, which Pieter has passed on to me. As Regional Operations Director, I wanted to respond personally.

We regret any inconvenience this incident may have caused to Fenwick Pharma and your hospital customers. Please be assured that Elmstead takes the integrity of temperature-controlled shipments extremely seriously, and that we operate to the highest industry standards across our network.

Our initial investigation indicates that the excursion occurred while the consignment was awaiting transfer to an onward vehicle. The vehicle in question, operated by a subcontracted haulier, arrived at the hub significantly later than scheduled owing to congestion on the approach roads. In addition, a sensor alert was generated but was not escalated in line with procedure, as it coincided with a shift change. These are regrettable circumstances, and we are reviewing our arrangements with the haulier concerned. In the meantime, a dedicated controller will oversee all pharmaceutical consignments at the Antwerp hub during shift changes, and sensor alerts will be routed directly to the duty manager.

I would, however, like to set the record straight on one point. Following the September incident, additional monitoring was indeed put in place, and it was this monitoring that allowed the excursion to be detected and reported to you so quickly on this occasion.

We will provide the full root cause report requested by Friday 14 November. With regard to costs, it would be premature to discuss liability before the test results are available, and any discussion will of course take place in accordance with the terms of our framework agreement.

We greatly value our relationship with Fenwick Pharma and remain fully committed to supporting you.

Kind regards,

Martin Hale
Regional Operations Director, Elmstead Logistics

1. How sincere is the apology in the second paragraph?
A. It is a full and unreserved apology that admits Elmstead was at fault.
B. It is a cautious expression of regret that admits no failure.
C. It is an apology addressed only to the hospital customers.
D. It is an offer of compensation.

2. How does the writer present the causes of the incident?
A. He accepts that Elmstead's own staff at the Antwerp hub were solely responsible for what happened.
B. He claims that the problem was caused mainly by the customer's packaging and labelling instructions.
C. He mainly blames external factors and mentions an internal lapse only briefly, in the passive.
D. He says the cause cannot be identified.

3. What is the writer doing in the fourth paragraph?
A. Admitting that the monitoring promised in September was never installed.
B. Apologising for the delay in detecting the problem.
C. Agreeing with all of Mr Pryce's criticisms.
D. Correcting an implied criticism by presenting the monitoring as a success.

4. How is Mr Pryce most likely to react to this reply?
A. He may find the reply defensive rather than accountable.
B. He will be fully reassured and close the matter.
C. He will be pleased that Elmstead has agreed to cover the costs of the quarantined batch.
D. He will be grateful for the immediate compensation offered.

Corrigé

1. B — It is a cautious expression of regret that admits no failure.. « We regret any inconvenience this incident may have caused » est une fausse excuse : pas de faute reconnue, et un dommage présenté comme hypothétique (« may have »). Le paragraphe enchaîne sur des déclarations générales rassurantes.
2. C — He mainly blames external factors and mentions an internal lapse only briefly, in the passive.. Il met en avant le sous-traitant et les embouteillages, et mentionne l'alerte non remontée au passif (« was not escalated »), sans nommer de responsable, en l'excusant par le changement d'équipe. C'est une mise à distance de la responsabilité.
3. D — Correcting an implied criticism by presenting the monitoring as a success.. « set the record straight » = rétablir les faits : il répond à l'insinuation de M. Pryce en affirmant que la surveillance a fonctionné, puisqu'elle a permis la détection rapide. C'est une contre-argumentation, pas un aveu.
4. A — He may find the reply defensive rather than accountable.. Fausse excuse, causes externalisées, correction de ses propos, refus de parler de responsabilité : la réponse est défensive, alors que le client demandait des explications après un second incident. Aucun coût n'est accepté ni aucune compensation proposée.

Exercice 3 — C1-M3-L6-I3 (C2, C1.1)

Lisez la lettre de réponse à une proposition de partenariat et répondez aux questions.

Ashgrove Hotels Group
Head Office, 14 Carrick Street, Glasgow

3 October 2026

Ms Elena Marchetti
Managing Director, Verdana Linen Services

Dear Ms Marchetti,

Partnership proposal — laundry and linen services

Thank you for your proposal of 12 September and for taking the time to present it to our operations team in person. My colleagues were impressed by the professionalism of your presentation, and by the environmental credentials of your new facility in Motherwell, which are clearly ahead of most of the market.

We have given your proposal careful consideration. On balance, however, we have concluded that we are not in a position to change our current arrangements for the hotels in our Scottish portfolio at this stage. As you may know, our existing contract runs until March 2028, and early termination would involve costs that we could not justify on the basis of the savings projected in your proposal.

I should add, in the interests of transparency, that some members of our team had reservations about the capacity of a single site to absorb the volume of our business, particularly during the summer peak, when our occupancy regularly exceeds 90%. I appreciate that your proposal addressed this point, but the contingency arrangements described were, in our view, not yet sufficiently detailed.

That said, we would be open to revisiting the question ahead of the tender for our next contract, which we expect to launch in the spring of 2027. If, by then, you are able to demonstrate a secondary processing site or a formal back-up agreement with another operator, I would be happy to ensure that Verdana is invited to take part.

In the meantime, we may have a requirement for a smaller pilot at our new boutique property in Perth, which opens next year and is not covered by our current contract. Our Head of Procurement, Mr Callum Reid, will be in touch if this materialises.

Thank you once again for your interest in working with Ashgrove.

Yours sincerely,

Fiona Lennox
Chief Operating Officer

1. What is the main message of the second paragraph?
A. Ashgrove has decided not to accept the proposal for now.
B. Ashgrove will terminate its current contract early.
C. Ashgrove needs more time to decide.
D. Ashgrove accepts the proposal in principle, subject to Verdana lowering its prices.

2. Why does the writer add the third paragraph “in the interests of transparency”?
A. To criticise the presentation made by Verdana's team.
B. To reveal a further, less diplomatic reason for the refusal.
C. To explain that Ashgrove's occupancy is falling.
D. To withdraw the objection about costs.

3. Is the offer to revisit the question genuine?
A. No, it is only a polite formula with no real meaning.
B. Yes, and Verdana has already been selected for the 2027 contract.
C. No, because Ashgrove will not launch another tender.
D. Yes, and it states precisely what Verdana would need to show.

4. What is suggested about the pilot at the Perth property?
A. It is a firm commitment that Verdana will receive.
B. It is a possibility that depends on future needs.
C. It replaces the main contract proposal.
D. It is covered by the existing contract.

Corrigé

1. A — Ashgrove has decided not to accept the proposal for now.. « We have given your proposal careful consideration. On balance, however… we are not in a position to change our current arrangements… at this stage » : c'est un refus adouci. La résiliation anticipée est jugée trop coûteuse.
2. B — To reveal a further, less diplomatic reason for the refusal.. Au-delà du contrat en cours, elle révèle un doute sur la capacité d'un site unique et sur des plans de secours « not yet sufficiently detailed ». La présentation a au contraire été saluée ; le taux d'occupation est élevé, pas en baisse.
3. D — Yes, and it states precisely what Verdana would need to show.. L'ouverture est assortie d'une condition concrète (second site ou accord de secours) et d'un calendrier (appel d'offres au printemps 2027) : c'est une vraie porte ouverte. Rien ne dit que Verdana est déjà retenue.
4. B — It is a possibility that depends on future needs.. « we may have a requirement… will be in touch if this materialises » : simple possibilité, conditionnelle. L'hôtel de Perth n'est justement pas couvert par le contrat actuel.

Exercice 4 — C1-M3-L6-I4 (C2, C1.2)

Complétez ce courriel délicat avec le terme qui convient.

Dear Mr Okafor,

[1] _____, our order was confirmed in writing on 4 May, so I would like to [2] _____ on the delivery date. I was, I must admit, [3] _____ disappointed by your reply, which seemed to [4] _____ blame onto our planning team. I [5] _____ you will understand why we cannot accept a further delay. Should the goods not arrive by 20 June, we will have no option but to [6] _____ the matter to our Purchasing Director.

Yours sincerely,

[1] On record / For the record / By the record / Off the record

[2] set the record straight / set the score / straighten the record up / put the record right up

[3] barely / scarcely / hardly / somewhat

[4] defer / reflect / deflect / deter

[5] doubt / trust / wonder / suspect

[6] escalate / elevate / accelerate / evaluate

Corrigé

[1] For the record. « For the record » = pour mémoire, pour que ce soit consigné. « Off the record » signifie « officieusement », sens opposé.
[2] set the record straight. Expression figée : « set the record straight » = rétablir les faits. Les autres formes n'existent pas.
[3] somewhat. « somewhat disappointed » est une litote typique. « barely / hardly / scarcely » nieraient presque la déception, ce qui contredirait la suite du courriel.
[4] deflect. « deflect blame onto » = rejeter la responsabilité sur. « reflect » (refléter) et « deter » (dissuader) ne conviennent pas.
[5] trust. « I trust you will understand » = je ne doute pas que vous comprendrez : attente ferme. « I doubt » inverserait le sens.
[6] escalate. « escalate the matter to » = faire remonter à un niveau hiérarchique supérieur. « elevate » ne s'emploie pas dans cette collocation.

title: C1-M3 — Classe virtuelle 1 — Atelier de lecture critique : voix, attitudes et non-dits
description: Attribuer correctement à chaque personne citée dans un article de 400 mots son opinion et son degré d'adhésion, sans confondre avec l'avis du journaliste. Traduire en langage direct au moins cinq euphémismes d'une communication interne de restructuration. Justifier oralement chaque réponse de QCM en citant le passage exact du texte et en expliquant pourquoi le distracteur le plus proche est faux.

sections.title: C1-M3-L7 — Classe virtuelle 1 — Atelier de lecture critique : voix, attitudes et non-dits
sections.contentHtml:
Objectifs :

  • Attribuer correctement à chaque personne citée dans un article de 400 mots son opinion et son degré d'adhésion, sans confondre avec l'avis du journaliste.
  • Traduire en langage direct au moins cinq euphémismes d'une communication interne de restructuration.
  • Justifier oralement chaque réponse de QCM en citant le passage exact du texte et en expliquant pourquoi le distracteur le plus proche est faux.

Compétence C2 — niveau C1.2 — 60 min — classe virtuelle

Cette classe virtuelle d'une heure met en pratique, avec le formateur et en petits groupes, les stratégies vues dans les leçons 1 à 6. Elle porte sur deux difficultés typiques du niveau C1 : les textes à plusieurs voix et les communications qui disent une chose pour en signifier une autre.

1. Les textes à plusieurs voix. Un article de presse économique cite souvent plusieurs acteurs : le dirigeant, un analyste, un syndicaliste, un concurrent. Le journaliste, lui, organise ces voix. Les questions C1 demandent fréquemment : According to X, …? ou What is the journalist's view of…? Pour y répondre :

  • reliez chaque citation à son auteur (said, according to, argues, a person familiar with the matter) ;
  • observez le verbe introducteur : admits (concession), concedes, insists (fermeté, parfois mise à distance), claims (doute possible), points out (fait présenté comme exact) ;
  • cherchez les rares phrases non attribuées : elles portent l'avis du journaliste, souvent en fin de paragraphe ou en conclusion.

2. Les communications de restructuration. Une note annonçant une réorganisation évite les mots job cuts, redundancies ou closure. On y lit plutôt : simplifying our structure, reducing layers of management, consolidating sites, a number of roles will be affected, colleagues whose roles are at risk, a period of consultation. Votre travail consiste à traduire ces formules en faits : combien de postes, quels sites, quel calendrier, quelles options pour les salariés. Repérez aussi ce qui n'est pas dit : l'absence de chiffre est elle-même une information.

3. Déroulement de la séance.

  • Échauffement collectif : le formateur projette des phrases courtes (We are consolidating our two Midlands sites) ; chacun propose une reformulation directe.
  • Travail en binômes sur les deux textes de la séance, avec chronomètre (9 minutes par texte).
  • Mise en commun : chaque binôme justifie ses réponses en anglais, en citant la phrase exacte (The answer is B because the text says…), puis explique pourquoi l'option la plus tentante est fausse.
  • Synthèse : construction collective d'une fiche « euphémismes et verbes introducteurs ».

4. Formulations utiles pour justifier à l'oral. The key phrase is…, This is attributed to…, not to the journalist, The option overstates the writer's position, The text implies rather than states that…, This distractor uses words from the text but reverses the logic.

5. Pourquoi justifier ? Au niveau C1, la plupart des erreurs ne viennent pas d'un manque de vocabulaire mais d'une lecture trop rapide de la relation entre les idées. Obliger chaque réponse à s'appuyer sur une citation développe l'habitude de vérifier avant de valider, réflexe décisif en conditions d'examen.

Préparation demandée : relire les leçons 2 et 6 et noter trois euphémismes rencontrés dans votre propre environnement professionnel (anonymisés).

Langue clé

AnglaisFrançaisUsage
The key phrase here is “…”, which suggests that…L'expression clé ici est « … », qui laisse entendre que…justifier une réponse en citant le texte
This view is attributed to the analyst, not the journalist.Cet avis est attribué à l'analyste, pas au journaliste.distinguer les voix d'un article
The option overstates the writer's position.L'option exagère la position de l'auteur.éliminer un distracteur trop catégorique
The text implies rather than states that…Le texte sous-entend plutôt qu'il n'affirme que…parler d'implicite
A number of roles will be affected.Un certain nombre de postes seront concernés.euphémisme pour des suppressions de postes
This distractor reverses the cause and the effect.Ce distracteur inverse la cause et l'effet.analyser un piège de QCM

Vocabulaire

TermeTraductionExemple
to concedeconcéder, reconnaîtreThe CEO conceded that the timing was poor.
to downplayminimiserThe memo downplays the scale of the cuts.
redundancylicenciement économique (UK)Around 120 redundancies are expected.
role at riskposte menacé de suppressionColleagues whose roles are at risk will be contacted individually.
consultation periodpériode de consultation (des représentants du personnel)A 45-day consultation period begins on Monday.
to consolidate sitesregrouper des sites (souvent : en fermer)We will consolidate our two warehouses into one.
layer of managementéchelon hiérarchiqueWe are removing one layer of management.
redeploymentreclassement interneRedeployment opportunities will be prioritised.
a person familiar with the matterune source proche du dossierAccording to a person familiar with the matter, talks have stalled.
to weigh inintervenir dans un débatSeveral investors have weighed in on the succession.
heir apparentsuccesseur désignéShe is widely seen as the heir apparent.
to be at odds withêtre en désaccord avecThe founder is at odds with the board.
to streamlinerationaliser, simplifierWe are streamlining our regional structure.

Dialogue : Présentation de l'atelier par la formatrice

Ouverture de la classe virtuelle : la formatrice présente l'atelier à deux apprenants connectés et lance l'échauffement.

PersonnageRépliqueTraduction
Hannah ClarkeWelcome, everyone. Today is all about voices and silences: who is speaking in a text, and what isn't being said.Bienvenue à tous. Aujourd'hui, tout tourne autour des voix et des silences : qui parle dans un texte, et ce qui n'est pas dit.
Hannah ClarkeLet's warm up. Julien, if a memo says 'we are consolidating our two Midlands sites', what does that mean?Échauffement. Julien, si une note dit « nous regroupons nos deux sites des Midlands », qu'est-ce que cela signifie ?
Julien MorelProbably that one site is closing, and the work moves to the other one.Probablement qu'un site ferme et que l'activité est transférée sur l'autre.
Hannah ClarkeExactly. And is the word 'closure' anywhere in the sentence?Exactement. Et le mot « fermeture » figure-t-il dans la phrase ?
Julien MorelNo. It's carefully avoided.Non. Il est soigneusement évité.
Hannah ClarkeAïcha, your turn: 'We are reducing layers of management to empower our teams.'Aïcha, à toi : « Nous réduisons les échelons hiérarchiques pour responsabiliser nos équipes. »
Aïcha BenaliSome middle managers will lose their jobs, but it's presented as something positive for everyone else.Certains cadres intermédiaires vont perdre leur poste, mais c'est présenté comme positif pour tous les autres.
Hannah ClarkeVery good. Notice how the benefit is placed at the end of the sentence, so that's what you remember.Très bien. Remarquez que le bénéfice est placé en fin de phrase : c'est ce qu'on retient.
Julien MorelWhat about articles? Sometimes I can't tell if it's the journalist's opinion or someone else's.Et pour les articles ? Parfois je n'arrive pas à savoir si c'est l'avis du journaliste ou de quelqu'un d'autre.
Hannah ClarkeThat's the second part of today. Look at the reporting verbs. 'Admits', 'insists', 'claims' — each one colours the quote.C'est la deuxième partie de la séance. Regardez les verbes introducteurs : « admet », « insiste », « affirme » — chacun colore la citation.
Aïcha BenaliAnd if a sentence has no quotation marks and no name?Et si une phrase n'a ni guillemets ni nom ?
Hannah ClarkeThen it's usually the journalist speaking. Those sentences are rare, so they matter.Alors c'est généralement le journaliste qui parle. Ces phrases sont rares, donc elles comptent.
Hannah ClarkeRight. You'll work in pairs, nine minutes per text. Then you'll justify every answer by quoting the text.Bien. Vous allez travailler en binômes, neuf minutes par texte. Ensuite, vous justifierez chaque réponse en citant le texte.
Julien MorelIn English, I suppose?En anglais, je suppose ?
Hannah ClarkeOf course. 'The key phrase is…' — you'll be saying it a lot today. Off you go.Bien sûr. « The key phrase is… » — vous allez beaucoup le dire aujourd'hui. C'est parti.

Déroulé de la classe virtuelle

  1. 5 min — Accueil, objectifs de la séance, rappel des stratégies des leçons 2 et 6 (verbes introducteurs, litotes, euphémismes).
  2. 8 min — Échauffement collectif : 8 phrases euphémiques projetées, reformulation directe à l'oral par chaque apprenant.
  3. 12 min — Binômes (salles de sous-groupe) : item C1-M3-L7-I1, 9 min chronométrées + 3 min de préparation des justifications en anglais.
  4. 12 min — Binômes : item C1-M3-L7-I2, même déroulé ; relevé des euphémismes et traduction en langage direct.
  5. 15 min — Mise en commun : chaque binôme justifie une réponse (« The key phrase is… »), analyse du distracteur le plus tentant, débat sur les divergences.
  6. 8 min — Synthèse : fiche collective « verbes introducteurs et euphémismes » (item C1-M3-L7-I3), consignes pour les leçons 8 et 9.

Exercices corrigés

Exercice 1 — C1-M3-L7-I1 (C2, C1.2)

Travail en binôme, 9 minutes. Lisez l'article et répondez aux questions, puis préparez une justification en anglais pour chaque réponse.

Succession question looms over Ravensby Foods

For more than forty years, Ravensby Foods has been run by the family that founded it as a single bakery in Harrogate. Today, it employs 2,300 people, supplies three of the country's five largest supermarket chains and reported revenue of £410 million last year. But as its chairman, 74-year-old Geoffrey Ravensby, prepares to step back, the question of who will lead the business next has exposed tensions that the family has long kept private.

The most obvious candidate is his daughter, Clara Ravensby, who has run the company's fast-growing snacks division since 2019. Under her leadership, the division's sales have almost doubled, and several analysts regard her as the heir apparent. “She has done exactly what the business needed in that part of the market,” said Tom Hadley, a consumer goods analyst at Pellham Securities. “The question is whether the skills that work in a growth division translate to running a group with complex supply relationships.”

Her cousin, Andrew Ravensby, who has been finance director for eight years, is said to favour a different approach. According to two people familiar with the matter, he has argued that the family should appoint an external chief executive and focus on its role as owner. Andrew Ravensby declined to comment for this article.

Geoffrey Ravensby himself insists that there is no rivalry. “Clara and Andrew have different strengths, and the board will make a decision based on what is right for the company,” he said in a rare interview. He conceded, however, that the process had taken “rather longer than I would have liked.”

The stakes are considerable. Two of the company's supermarket customers are understood to be reviewing their supplier arrangements next year, and a prolonged period of uncertainty at the top would hardly strengthen Ravensby's hand in those negotiations. Family businesses that manage succession well tend to do so by planning years in advance. Ravensby, it seems, has left itself rather less time than that.

1. What does Tom Hadley suggest about Clara Ravensby?
A. She has failed to grow the snacks division.
B. She should replace her father as chairman immediately, given the remarkable growth of her division.
C. She has done well in her current role, but this may not prove she can run the whole group.
D. She lacks experience in supply relationships because she is too young.

2. Where does the information about Andrew Ravensby's position come from?
A. From anonymous sources, since he did not wish to comment.
B. From an interview he gave to the journalist.
C. From Geoffrey Ravensby's statement.
D. From the company's annual report.

3. How does the use of “insists” and “conceded” shape the presentation of Geoffrey Ravensby's statement?
A. It shows that the journalist fully accepts his version of events and sees no rivalry in the family.
B. It casts some doubt on his denial of rivalry and notes his admission that the process was slow.
C. It indicates that he has already chosen his successor.
D. It shows that he refused to answer the journalist's questions.

4. What is the journalist's own view, expressed in the final paragraph?
A. The company should sell itself to a supermarket chain.
B. The supermarket customers are certain to leave Ravensby.
C. Family businesses like Ravensby should always appoint external managers rather than family members.
D. The firm has left succession planning late, to its cost.

Corrigé

1. C — She has done well in her current role, but this may not prove she can run the whole group.. L'analyste salue son action (« exactly what the business needed ») puis pose une question sur la transposition de ces compétences à l'échelle du groupe. Il ne parle ni de son âge ni d'un remplacement immédiat.
2. A — From anonymous sources, since he did not wish to comment.. « According to two people familiar with the matter… Andrew Ravensby declined to comment » : sources anonymes, et l'intéressé n'a pas répondu. « is said to favour » marque également une information rapportée, non confirmée.
3. B — It casts some doubt on his denial of rivalry and notes his admission that the process was slow.. « insists » peut signaler une affirmation que le journaliste ne reprend pas à son compte ; « conceded » introduit un aveu (le processus a été trop long). Il a bien répondu : c'est « a rare interview ».
4. D — The firm has left succession planning late, to its cost.. Phrases non attribuées : l'incertitude « would hardly strengthen Ravensby's hand », et « Ravensby, it seems, has left itself rather less time than that ». Les clients « are understood to be reviewing » leurs accords : leur départ n'est pas certain.

Exercice 2 — C1-M3-L7-I2 (C2, C1.2)

Travail en binôme, 9 minutes. Lisez la note interne et répondez aux questions. Préparez la traduction en langage direct des euphémismes relevés.

To: All colleagues, Northgate Building Supplies
From: Simon Achterberg, Chief Executive
Subject: Shaping Northgate for the next decade

Dear colleagues,

Over the past two years, our industry has faced a combination of challenges that few of us have experienced in our careers: a sharp slowdown in new housing projects, sustained pressure on prices from online competitors and significant increases in energy and transport costs. Thanks to your hard work, Northgate has weathered this period better than many of our peers. But it has become clear that our current structure was designed for a different market, and that we need to act now to secure the long-term future of the business.

Today, I am announcing a programme to simplify how we operate. There are three main elements.

First, we will consolidate our distribution network. Our depots in Wakefield and Doncaster, which are less than thirty miles apart, will be brought together on a single site in Doncaster by the end of next year. This will allow us to serve customers more efficiently and to invest in a modern, energy-efficient facility.

Second, we will streamline our regional management structure, moving from six regions to four and removing one layer of management. This will bring decision-making closer to our branches and our customers.

Third, we will move a number of finance and administrative activities to our shared service centre in Leeds.

I want to be open with you: these changes will affect a number of roles across the business. We expect that, after redeployment, around 140 positions may no longer be required. We will begin a formal consultation with employee representatives next week, and nobody's role will change before that consultation has concluded. Colleagues whose roles are at risk will be contacted individually by their line manager over the coming days, and we will do everything we can to find alternative positions within the Group.

I know that this news will be difficult for many of you, and that it comes at a time when you have already given a great deal. I will be holding open sessions at every affected site over the next three weeks, and I would encourage you to come and ask any question you have.

Simon Achterberg

1. What does “we will consolidate our distribution network” mean in concrete terms?
A. The Doncaster depot will close and its activity will move to Wakefield.
B. Both depots will remain open but share their management.
C. A new depot will be opened in addition to the existing ones.
D. The Wakefield depot will close and its activity will move to Doncaster.

2. How is the reduction from six regions to four presented?
A. As a benefit for customers and branches, without mentioning its effect on managers.
B. As a temporary measure that the company intends to reverse once market conditions improve.
C. As a decision imposed by the shared service centre.
D. As a way of increasing the number of managers.

3. What does the phrase “after redeployment, around 140 positions may no longer be required” reveal?
A. Exactly 140 employees will be dismissed next week.
B. No jobs will be lost at all, because every affected employee will be redeployed within the Group.
C. About 140 net job losses are expected.
D. 140 new positions will be created in Leeds.

4. What is the overall tone of the memo?
A. Triumphant, celebrating the company's success.
B. Carefully reassuring and partly euphemistic, though it eventually gives a figure.
C. Angry with employees for the company's difficulties.
D. Completely transparent from the first line to the last.

Corrigé

1. D — The Wakefield depot will close and its activity will move to Doncaster.. Les deux dépôts seront « brought together on a single site in Doncaster » : en clair, Wakefield ferme. Le mot « closure » n'apparaît jamais : c'est l'euphémisme à traduire. La première option inverse les deux villes.
2. A — As a benefit for customers and branches, without mentioning its effect on managers.. La phrase met en avant le bénéfice (« closer to our branches and our customers ») ; la conséquence pour les managers dont l'échelon disparaît n'est pas mentionnée. Elle signifie pourtant moins de postes d'encadrement.
3. C — About 140 net job losses are expected.. C'est l'aveu chiffré derrière « affect a number of roles » : environ 140 suppressions nettes, après reclassements. « may » et « around » nuancent, et rien ne change avant la fin de la consultation : la première option est donc fausse.
4. B — Carefully reassuring and partly euphemistic, though it eventually gives a figure.. Le dirigeant valorise les équipes, enrobe les mesures (« simplify », « consolidate », « streamline »), puis donne le chiffre de 140 postes et un calendrier. « Completely transparent » est excessif puisque les premiers paragraphes évitent les mots directs.

Exercice 3 — C1-M3-L7-I3 (C2, C1.2)

Mise en commun : complétez la fiche « verbes introducteurs et euphémismes » avec le terme qui convient.

The CEO [1] _____ that the timing was unfortunate, but he [2] _____ that no decision had yet been taken. According to a person [3] _____ with the matter, the plan involves [4] _____ the two warehouses into one, and staff whose roles are [5] _____ will be offered [6] _____ opportunities elsewhere in the group.

[1] rejected / denied / refused / conceded

[2] confessed / admitted / insisted / regretted

[3] close / familiar / aware / acquainted

[4] consolidating / consulting / consoling / conserving

[5] at stake / in danger / on risk / at risk

[6] redundancy / deployment / redeployment / replacement

Corrigé

[1] conceded. « conceded that… » = a reconnu, a admis (un point défavorable). « denied » signifierait qu'il nie, ce qui contredit « but ».
[2] insisted. Après « but », on attend une affirmation ferme qui s'oppose à la concession : « insisted ». « admitted » répéterait l'idée de concession.
[3] familiar. Formule journalistique figée : « a person familiar with the matter ». « close » se construit avec « to » (« a source close to the company »).
[4] consolidating. « consolidating… into one » = regrouper, en pratique fermer un site. Les autres verbes sont des paronymes sans rapport.
[5] at risk. « roles at risk » = postes menacés de suppression, terme RH consacré. « at stake » signifie « en jeu ».
[6] redeployment. « redeployment opportunities » = possibilités de reclassement interne. « redundancy » désigne au contraire le licenciement.
