sections.title: C1-M3-L8 — Rapports d'audit : constats, niveaux de gravité et réponses de la direction
sections.contentHtml:
Objectifs :

  • Identifier dans un rapport d'audit de 350 à 450 mots l'opinion globale, les constats prioritaires, leur cause racine et les actions convenues (responsable, échéance).
  • Distinguer un défaut de conception d'un contrôle d'un défaut d'application, et une acceptation totale d'une acceptation partielle d'une recommandation.
  • Repérer le degré de réserve de l'auditeur à travers ses formulations, avec au moins 75 % de réponses correctes aux QCM.

Compétence C2 — niveau C1.1 — 40 min

Les rapports d'audit (internal audit reports, management letters des commissaires aux comptes, rapports de conformité) sont rédigés dans une langue sobre, codifiée et prudente. Chaque mot y est pesé : comprendre le niveau de gravité et le degré d'accord entre auditeur et direction est essentiel.

1. La structure. On trouve généralement : Scope and objectives (périmètre), Overall opinion ou Assurance rating, Key findings, puis pour chaque constat Observation / Risk / Root cause / Recommendation / Management response / Agreed action / Owner / Due date.

2. Les niveaux d'opinion. Les échelles varient, mais l'ordre est souvent : substantial (ou full) assurance > reasonable assurance > limited assurance > no assurance. Une opinion limited signifie que des faiblesses significatives exposent l'organisation à des risques. Les constats sont classés high / medium / low priority (ou critical, significant, minor).

3. Conception ou application ? Un contrôle peut être mal conçu (the control is not designed to prevent…) ou bien conçu mais mal appliqué (the control is well designed but was not operating effectively). Exemple : une procédure exige deux signatures, mais en pratique un seul responsable valide les paiements. Autres notions clés : segregation of duties (séparation des tâches), audit trail (piste d'audit), exceptions (anomalies relevées dans l'échantillon), management override (contournement des contrôles par la direction).

4. La prudence de l'auditeur. L'auditeur affirme rarement : il écrit we were unable to obtain evidence that… (aucune preuve fournie, ce qui ne prouve pas que le contrôle n'a pas eu lieu), we noted (nous avons constaté), in 7 of the 25 transactions sampled (proportion sur un échantillon, pas sur l'ensemble), no exceptions were noted (aucune anomalie). Une question C1 vérifie souvent que vous ne transformez pas un constat d'échantillon en vérité générale.

5. La réponse de la direction. Elle peut être agreed (acceptée), partially agreed (acceptée en partie) ou, plus rarement, not agreed avec acceptation du risque (management accepts the risk). Le ton de la réponse révèle l'attitude : défensive (this reflects a temporary situation), coopérative (we welcome the review), ou dilatoire (une échéance lointaine pour un risque élevé). L'auditeur peut ajouter un commentaire (Internal Audit's view), signe d'un désaccord persistant.

6. Vocabulaire indispensable. Remediation (correction), compensating control (contrôle compensatoire), follow-up review (audit de suivi), overdue actions (actions en retard), materiality (seuil de signification), misstatement (anomalie dans les comptes).

Méthode : commencez par l'opinion globale et les priorités, puis, pour chaque question, repérez qui parle (auditeur ou direction), sur quelle base (échantillon, entretien, document) et avec quel degré de certitude.

Langue clé

AnglaisFrançaisUsage
Overall, we provide limited assurance over…Globalement, nous apportons une assurance limitée sur…opinion d'audit défavorable
In 7 of the 25 transactions sampled, …Dans 7 des 25 opérations de l'échantillon, …constat sur un échantillon, pas sur l'ensemble
We were unable to obtain evidence that the review took place.Nous n'avons pas pu obtenir la preuve que la revue a eu lieu.absence de preuve, formulation prudente
The control is well designed but is not operating effectively.Le contrôle est bien conçu mais n'est pas appliqué efficacement.défaut d'application
Management response: partially agreed.Réponse de la direction : acceptée en partie.désaccord partiel sur une recommandation
Internal Audit continues to regard this risk as high.L'audit interne continue de considérer ce risque comme élevé.désaccord persistant de l'auditeur

Vocabulaire

TermeTraductionExemple
assurance ratingniveau d'assurance (opinion d'audit)The review received a limited assurance rating.
findingconstatThe report contains two high-priority findings.
root causecause racineThe root cause was unclear ownership of the process.
segregation of dutiesséparation des tâchesThere is no segregation of duties between ordering and payment.
audit trailpiste d'auditManual changes leave no audit trail.
exceptionanomalie (dans un échantillon)No exceptions were noted in the sample.
compensating controlcontrôle compensatoireA monthly review acts as a compensating control.
remediationcorrection, plan de remédiationRemediation is due by the end of the second quarter.
overdue actionaction en retardThree actions from the previous audit are overdue.
management overridecontournement des contrôles par la directionThe risk of management override cannot be eliminated.
materialityseuil de significationThe error is below our materiality threshold.
misstatementanomalie (dans les états financiers)No material misstatement was identified.
follow-up reviewaudit de suiviA follow-up review is planned for September.
privileged accessaccès à privilèges (administrateur)Privileged access rights should be reviewed quarterly.

Dialogue : Préparer le comité d'audit : lire le rapport avant la réunion

Bureau du directeur financier d'un groupe d'ingénierie, à Bristol, la veille d'un comité d'audit. Il passe en revue le rapport d'audit interne avec la responsable du contrôle interne.

PersonnageRépliqueTraduction
David AshcombePriya, the procurement audit came back as 'limited assurance'. How bad is that, honestly?Priya, l'audit des achats est revenu avec une « assurance limitée ». C'est grave à quel point, honnêtement ?
Priya NatarajanIt's the second-lowest rating. The committee will expect a clear plan, not reassurance.C'est l'avant-dernier niveau. Le comité attendra un plan clair, pas des paroles rassurantes.
David AshcombeThe main finding is about purchase orders raised after the invoice. Is that widespread?Le constat principal porte sur des bons de commande émis après la facture. C'est généralisé ?
Priya NatarajanThey found it in nine of the forty transactions they sampled. We can't say it's everywhere, but nearly a quarter is significant.Ils l'ont relevé dans neuf des quarante opérations de l'échantillon. On ne peut pas dire que c'est partout, mais près d'un quart, c'est significatif.
David AshcombeAnd the second one — 'unable to obtain evidence' of the supplier reviews. Does that mean they weren't done?Et le deuxième — « pas pu obtenir la preuve » des revues fournisseurs. Ça veut dire qu'elles n'ont pas été faites ?
Priya NatarajanNot necessarily. It means nobody could prove they were done. For an auditor, that's almost the same thing.Pas forcément. Ça veut dire que personne n'a pu prouver qu'elles avaient été faites. Pour un auditeur, c'est presque pareil.
David AshcombeFair point. I see our response to the third finding is 'partially agreed'.C'est juste. Je vois que notre réponse au troisième constat est « acceptée en partie ».
Priya NatarajanYes, operations accepted the training, but not a second approver for urgent orders. They say it would slow them down.Oui, l'exploitation a accepté la formation, mais pas un second valideur pour les commandes urgentes. Ils disent que cela les ralentirait.
David AshcombeAnd audit added a comment underneath?Et l'audit a ajouté un commentaire en dessous ?
Priya Natarajan'Internal Audit continues to regard this risk as high.' That's their polite way of saying they disagree with us.« L'audit interne continue de considérer ce risque comme élevé. » C'est leur façon polie de dire qu'ils ne sont pas d'accord avec nous.
David AshcombeThen the committee will ask me about it first. Is there a compensating control we could offer?Alors le comité m'interrogera d'abord là-dessus. Y a-t-il un contrôle compensatoire que nous pourrions proposer ?
Priya NatarajanA weekly review of all urgent orders by finance. It doesn't slow anything down, and it leaves an audit trail.Une revue hebdomadaire de toutes les commandes urgentes par la finance. Ça ne ralentit rien et ça laisse une piste d'audit.
David AshcombeGood. Draft it as a proposal and I'll present it tomorrow.Bien. Rédige-le sous forme de proposition et je le présenterai demain.
Priya NatarajanI'll have it to you by six, with an owner and a due date.Tu l'auras avant dix-huit heures, avec un responsable et une échéance.

Exercices corrigés

Exercice 1 — C1-M3-L8-I1 (C2, C1.1)

Lisez la synthèse du rapport d'audit interne et répondez aux questions dans l'ordre du texte.

INTERNAL AUDIT REPORT — PROCUREMENT AND ACCOUNTS PAYABLE
Calloway Engineering Group — Report ref. IA-2026-07
Distribution: Chief Financial Officer; Group Procurement Director; Audit Committee

  1. Scope

The review covered the purchase-to-pay process for the UK business units between 1 July 2025 and 31 March 2026. We assessed the design and operating effectiveness of key controls over supplier set-up, purchase order approval, goods receipt and payment. The overseas subsidiaries were excluded from scope and will be reviewed in 2027.

  1. Overall opinion: LIMITED ASSURANCE

While a sound framework of policies is in place, we identified weaknesses in the way several key controls operate in practice. Taken together, these expose the Group to an increased risk of unauthorised or uncompetitive spending.

  1. Summary of key findings

Finding 1 (High priority) — Retrospective purchase orders. In 9 of the 40 transactions sampled, the purchase order was raised after the supplier's invoice had been received, in some cases several weeks later. In these cases, the approval step served only to record a commitment that had already been made, rather than to authorise it.

Finding 2 (High priority) — Supplier performance reviews. The procurement policy requires an annual review of all suppliers with spending above £250,000. We were unable to obtain evidence that such reviews had been completed for 6 of the 11 suppliers in this category.

Finding 3 (Medium priority) — Urgent orders. The policy allows orders marked “urgent” to be approved by a single manager, regardless of value. Use of this category has increased from 4% to 15% of orders over two years, and we noted orders above £100,000 approved under this route.

Finding 4 (Low priority) — Supplier master data. Changes to supplier bank details were correctly verified by telephone in all 15 cases tested. However, the verification is recorded in a spreadsheet that can be edited without leaving an audit trail.

  1. Positive observations

The segregation of duties between the procurement and payment teams is well established, and no exceptions were noted in our testing of payment authorisation.

  1. Follow-up

Management has agreed action plans for all findings, with the exception of part of Finding 3 (see section 6). A follow-up review will be carried out in the first quarter of 2027.

1. What does the overall opinion suggest about the Group's procurement policies?
A. The policies themselves are adequate, but they are not consistently applied.
B. The policies are badly designed and will have to be rewritten before controls can work.
C. There are no written policies covering procurement.
D. The policies work perfectly in the UK business units.

2. Why is Finding 1 considered serious?
A. Because invoices were paid twice.
B. Because all purchase orders in the Group were raised late.
C. Because approval came after the commitment, so it no longer controlled the spending.
D. Because suppliers refused to send invoices.

3. What exactly do the auditors state about the supplier reviews in Finding 2?
A. The auditors proved that the reviews had not taken place for six of the eleven suppliers.
B. No evidence could be provided that the reviews took place for six suppliers.
C. All eleven suppliers had been reviewed but the results were lost.
D. The policy does not require any supplier reviews.

4. What concern is implied in Finding 3?
A. Urgent orders are processed too slowly because they currently require too many approvals.
B. The single-approver route may be used to bypass normal controls, even for large sums.
C. Managers are refusing to approve urgent orders.
D. The urgent category has been abolished.

5. Why is Finding 4 rated as low priority?
A. Because only the record-keeping is weak.
B. Because bank details are never changed.
C. Because the auditors did not test any cases.
D. Because the overseas subsidiaries, which were excluded from scope, are responsible for supplier data.

Corrigé

1. A — The policies themselves are adequate, but they are not consistently applied.. « While a sound framework of policies is in place, we identified weaknesses in the way several key controls operate in practice » : problème d'application, pas de conception. L'opinion « limited assurance » exclut un fonctionnement parfait.
2. C — Because approval came after the commitment, so it no longer controlled the spending.. L'approbation « served only to record a commitment that had already been made, rather than to authorise it » : le contrôle perd sa fonction. Le constat porte sur 9 opérations sur 40, pas sur toutes : c'est le piège de généralisation.
3. B — No evidence could be provided that the reviews took place for six suppliers.. « We were unable to obtain evidence that such reviews had been completed » : l'absence de preuve n'équivaut pas à une preuve d'absence. La formule prudente de l'auditeur doit être restituée telle quelle.
4. B — The single-approver route may be used to bypass normal controls, even for large sums.. La forte hausse de la catégorie « urgent » (4 % → 15 %) et des commandes de plus de 100 000 £ validées par une seule personne laissent entendre un contournement des contrôles. Le texte ne le dit pas explicitement : c'est l'implicite.
5. A — Because only the record-keeping is weak.. Les vérifications ont été faites correctement « in all 15 cases tested » ; seul l'enregistrement (tableur modifiable, sans piste d'audit) est fragile. D'où une priorité faible.

Exercice 2 — C1-M3-L8-I2 (C2, C1.2)

Lisez le détail d'un constat d'audit et la réponse de la direction, puis répondez aux questions.

INTERNAL AUDIT REPORT IA-2026-07 — SECTION 6: DETAILED FINDING AND MANAGEMENT RESPONSE

Finding 3 — Use of the “urgent order” route (Medium priority)

Observation
The procurement policy allows orders flagged as “urgent” to be approved by a single budget-holding manager, without the second approval required for standard orders above £25,000. The policy does not define what constitutes an urgent order. Over the period reviewed, 15% of all orders by value were processed through this route, compared with 4% two years ago. Our sample included three urgent orders above £100,000, two of which related to services that had been planned several months in advance.

Risk
Without a clear definition and appropriate oversight, the urgent route can be used, intentionally or not, to bypass competitive tendering and dual approval, increasing the risk of uncompetitive pricing or inappropriate spending.

Root cause
The policy was written for genuine operational emergencies, such as equipment breakdowns. Discussions with managers indicated that it is now widely regarded as a convenient way of avoiding delays in the standard approval workflow, which several described as “slow and frustrating”.

Recommendations
(a) Define “urgent” in the policy, with examples.
(b) Require a second approval for urgent orders above £50,000, which may be obtained retrospectively within two working days.
(c) Provide training to budget holders.

Management response — PARTIALLY AGREED
We accept recommendations (a) and (c) and will implement them by 30 September 2026 (Owner: Group Procurement Director). We do not agree with recommendation (b). Our operations teams frequently need to act within hours to avoid costly downtime, and introducing a further approval step, even retrospectively, would add administrative burden at precisely the moment when speed matters most. We consider that the training and clearer definition will address the issue adequately.

Internal Audit comment
We acknowledge management's concerns about operational speed and note that recommendation (b) was designed to allow approval after the event. We remain of the view that, without independent oversight of high-value urgent orders, the risk will not be adequately mitigated. Internal Audit continues to regard this risk as high and will report on it specifically at the follow-up review. The Audit Committee may wish to consider whether a compensating control, such as a weekly finance review of all urgent orders, would be acceptable.

1. What does the observation suggest about the two urgent orders for planned services?
A. They were genuine emergencies caused by equipment breakdowns.
B. They were approved by two managers as required.
C. They were below the £25,000 threshold.
D. They were probably not genuinely urgent.

2. According to the root cause section, why has use of the urgent route increased?
A. Because there have been more equipment breakdowns, which the policy was designed to deal with.
B. Because managers see it as a way to avoid a standard process they find too slow.
C. Because the policy requires all large orders to be urgent.
D. Because the auditors recommended it two years ago.

3. What is management's position on the recommendations?
A. It accepts the definition and the training but rejects the additional approval.
B. It rejects all three recommendations.
C. It accepts all three recommendations but needs more time than Internal Audit proposed to implement them.
D. It accepts the additional approval but rejects the training.

4. What is the attitude of Internal Audit in its final comment?
A. It withdraws recommendation (b) after accepting management's arguments about the need for operational speed.
B. It accuses management of deliberately misusing the policy.
C. It acknowledges the concern but maintains its view.
D. It considers the issue closed.

Corrigé

1. D — They were probably not genuinely urgent.. Des services « planned several months in advance » ne relèvent pas de l'urgence : l'auditeur le suggère sans l'affirmer. Ils dépassaient 100 000 £, bien au-delà du seuil de 25 000 £, et n'ont eu qu'un seul valideur.
2. B — Because managers see it as a way to avoid a standard process they find too slow.. Les managers la considèrent comme « a convenient way of avoiding delays in the standard approval workflow », jugé « slow and frustrating ». Les pannes sont l'usage prévu à l'origine, pas la cause de la hausse.
3. A — It accepts the definition and the training but rejects the additional approval.. « We accept recommendations (a) and (c)… We do not agree with recommendation (b) » : d'où « partially agreed ». La recommandation rejetée est le second niveau d'approbation.
4. C — It acknowledges the concern but maintains its view.. « We acknowledge management's concerns » (reconnaissance) puis « We remain of the view that… » (maintien du désaccord), et suggestion d'un contrôle compensatoire. L'audit ne retire rien et n'accuse personne de mauvaise foi.

Exercice 3 — C1-M3-L8-I3 (C2, C1.1)

Lisez la lettre du commissaire aux comptes au comité d'audit et répondez aux questions.

Ashby Wren LLP — Chartered Accountants

To: The Audit Committee, Marlowe Retail plc
Date: 18 March 2026

Dear Members of the Committee,

Audit of the financial statements for the year ended 31 January 2026 — Internal control observations

Further to our audit of the Group's financial statements, we are writing to bring to your attention certain matters relating to internal control that came to our notice during the course of our work. Our audit was not designed to identify all weaknesses that may exist, and the matters below should not be regarded as a comprehensive statement of all deficiencies.

We are pleased to report that we did not identify any material misstatement in the financial statements, and we expect to issue an unmodified audit opinion following the Board's approval of the accounts.

  1. Privileged IT access (Significant deficiency)

Our testing identified 23 user accounts with administrator-level access to the Group's finance system. Of these, eight belonged to employees who had left the Group, in two cases more than a year earlier. Although we found no evidence that these accounts had been used after the individuals' departure, the absence of a regular review of privileged access creates a risk of unauthorised changes to financial data. We note that a similar observation was made in our letter last year, and that the action agreed at that time has not yet been completed.

  1. Manual journal entries (Other deficiency)

Journals above £500,000 require review by a second member of the finance team. In our sample of 30 such journals, the review had been performed in all cases. However, in five cases the review took place more than ten days after posting, which reduces its value as a preventive control.

  1. Inventory counts at distribution centres (Other deficiency)

Count procedures were generally well executed. At one of the four centres we attended, count sheets were not pre-numbered, which makes it more difficult to confirm that all sheets have been returned.

We would be grateful if management's responses to these points could be provided before the Committee's meeting on 2 April. We would like to thank the finance team for their cooperation during the audit.

Yours faithfully,

Ashby Wren LLP

1. Why does the auditor state that the audit “was not designed to identify all weaknesses”?
A. To admit that the audit was badly carried out.
B. To limit expectations: the list may not cover every control weakness.
C. To warn that the financial statements contain errors.
D. To announce that a second audit will take place.

2. What does the auditor imply by noting that “a similar observation was made in our letter last year”?
A. Management has been slow to act on a known issue.
B. The issue is new and could not have been anticipated.
C. Last year's letter contained an error.
D. The former employees have used their accounts.

3. What is the weakness identified in point 2?
A. Some journals above £500,000 were never reviewed by a second member of the team.
B. Journals above £500,000 do not require any review.
C. Reviews were done, but sometimes too late to prevent errors effectively.
D. Thirty journals contained material errors.

4. How would you describe the overall tone of the letter?
A. Alarmist, suggesting the accounts cannot be approved.
B. Purely congratulatory, with no concerns raised.
C. Hostile towards the finance team.
D. Measured and professional, combining reassurance with clearly prioritised concerns.

Corrigé

1. B — To limit expectations: the list may not cover every control weakness.. C'est une réserve d'usage : la lettre n'est pas « a comprehensive statement of all deficiencies ». Le paragraphe suivant précise qu'aucune anomalie significative n'a été relevée dans les comptes.
2. A — Management has been slow to act on a known issue.. Rappeler que le même point a été signalé l'an dernier et que l'action convenue « has not yet been completed » souligne, sans le dire crûment, la lenteur de la direction. L'auditeur précise en revanche n'avoir aucune preuve d'utilisation des comptes.
3. C — Reviews were done, but sometimes too late to prevent errors effectively.. « the review had been performed in all cases. However, in five cases the review took place more than ten days after posting » : la revue existe, mais tardive, elle perd sa valeur préventive. Aucune erreur significative n'est signalée.
4. D — Measured and professional, combining reassurance with clearly prioritised concerns.. La lettre rassure (pas d'anomalie significative, opinion sans réserve attendue), hiérarchise les faiblesses (« significant » / « other ») et remercie l'équipe : ton mesuré. Elle n'empêche pas l'approbation des comptes.

Exercice 4 — C1-M3-L8-I4 (C2, C1.1)

Complétez l'extrait de rapport d'audit avec le terme qui convient.

Overall, we provide [1] _____ assurance. The main weakness is a lack of [2] _____ of duties: the same person can create a supplier and approve its invoices. No [3] _____ were noted in the sample of payments tested. Changes made directly in the database leave no audit [4] _____. Pending full [5] _____, a monthly review by the controller will act as a [6] _____ control. Three actions agreed last year are now [7] _____.

[1] restricted / limited / narrow / minor

[2] segregation / separation / segmentation / distribution

[3] expectations / exemptions / excerpts / exceptions

[4] path / track / trail / line

[5] remuneration / remediation / recommendation / reconciliation

[6] compensating / compensatory / complementing / compensated

[7] overrun / overtime / overdone / overdue

Corrigé

[1] limited. « limited assurance » est le niveau d'opinion consacré. « restricted » ou « narrow » ne font pas partie de l'échelle.
[2] segregation. Terme consacré : « segregation of duties ». « separation of duties » existe parfois, mais « segregation » est l'usage standard en audit.
[3] exceptions. « No exceptions were noted » = aucune anomalie relevée. « exemptions » signifie dispenses.
[4] trail. Collocation figée : « audit trail » (piste d'audit).
[5] remediation. « Pending full remediation » = en attendant la correction complète. « reconciliation » (rapprochement) est un contrôle comptable distinct.
[6] compensating. « compensating control » est le terme standard. « compensatory » s'emploie pour des dommages (« compensatory damages »).
[7] overdue. « overdue actions » = actions dont l'échéance est dépassée. « overrun » s'emploie pour un dépassement de coûts ou de délai d'un projet.

Repérer l'angle et l'intérêt de chaque émetteur (entreprise, journaliste, analyste, organisation professionnelle) et leur effet sur la sélection des faits. Détecter une incohérence chiffrée ou une information omise par l'une des sources, avec au moins 75 % de réponses correctes aux QCM.

sections.title: C1-M3-L9 — Comparer plusieurs sources : convergences, contradictions et angles
sections.contentHtml:
Objectifs :

  • Comparer deux ou trois documents de 300 à 450 mots au total portant sur le même événement et identifier les points de convergence et de divergence.
  • Repérer l'angle et l'intérêt de chaque émetteur (entreprise, journaliste, analyste, organisation professionnelle) et leur effet sur la sélection des faits.
  • Détecter une incohérence chiffrée ou une information omise par l'une des sources, avec au moins 75 % de réponses correctes aux QCM.

Compétence C2 — niveau C1.2 — 40 min

Dans la vie professionnelle, on lit rarement un document isolé : un communiqué d'entreprise est suivi d'articles de presse, une publication de résultats de notes d'analystes, une statistique officielle de commentaires d'organisations professionnelles. Le niveau C1 suppose de croiser ces sources pour se faire une opinion juste.

1. Identifier l'émetteur et son intérêt. Avant de lire, demandez-vous : qui écrit, pour qui, et dans quel but ? Une entreprise met en avant ses réussites (record, transformational, strategic milestone) ; un journaliste cherche l'angle critique ou l'information nouvelle ; un analyste formule une recommandation (buy, hold, sell) ; une organisation professionnelle défend les intérêts de ses membres. Chacun sélectionne les faits qui servent son propos.

2. Repérer convergences et divergences. Faites un tableau mental : quels faits figurent dans toutes les sources (souvent les plus fiables) ? Lesquels n'apparaissent que dans une seule ? Les divergences peuvent porter sur :

  • les chiffres (un prix d'acquisition « jusqu'à 900 M€ » dans le communiqué devient « 650 M€ payés d'avance, le reste conditionnel » dans la presse) ;
  • l'interprétation (a strong quarter vs flattered by one-offs) ;
  • la période ou le périmètre (croissance sur un an vs sur cinq ans, exportations totales vs exportations des PME).

3. Les omissions. Ce qu'une source tait est souvent ce qu'une autre souligne : le coût d'une acquisition, une baisse de marge, une enquête en cours. Une question C1 typique : Which information appears in the article but not in the press release? ou What does the trade body's statement fail to mention?

4. Le vocabulaire de la comparaison. Both sources agree that…, Unlike the press release, the article…, The two analysts diverge on…, This is corroborated by… (confirmé par), This contradicts…, There is a discrepancy between… (écart, incohérence), The figures can be reconciled if… (concilier).

5. Attention aux chiffres qui « ne disent pas la même chose ». Deux sources peuvent sembler se contredire alors qu'elles mesurent des choses différentes : valeur ou volume, nominal ou corrigé de l'inflation, moyenne ou médiane, chiffre trimestriel ou annuel. Avant de conclure à une contradiction, vérifiez ce qui est mesuré.

6. Stratégie de lecture. Lisez d'abord rapidement chaque source pour en identifier l'émetteur et la thèse ; lisez ensuite les questions ; enfin, revenez aux passages précis en gardant les sources séparées. Les questions suivent l'ordre du document (source A, puis B, puis C), mais certaines portent sur l'ensemble : gardez-les pour la fin.

Cette compétence est directement utile pour une veille concurrentielle, la préparation d'une négociation ou la rédaction d'une note de synthèse fiable.

Langue clé

AnglaisFrançaisUsage
Both sources agree that the deal will close in the third quarter.Les deux sources s'accordent à dire que l'opération sera finalisée au troisième trimestre.point de convergence
Unlike the press release, the article mentions the debt involved.Contrairement au communiqué, l'article mentionne la dette engagée.signaler une différence de contenu
The two analysts diverge on the sustainability of the margin.Les deux analystes divergent sur la pérennité de la marge.désaccord d'interprétation
There is a discrepancy between the two figures.Il y a un écart entre les deux chiffres.incohérence chiffrée
The figures can be reconciled if we take inflation into account.Les chiffres peuvent être conciliés si l'on tient compte de l'inflation.expliquer une contradiction apparente
This claim is not corroborated by the official data.Cette affirmation n'est pas confirmée par les données officielles.évaluer la fiabilité d'une affirmation

Vocabulaire

TermeTraductionExemple
to corroboratecorroborer, confirmerThe official figures corroborate the company's claim.
discrepancyécart, divergenceThere is a discrepancy between the two reports.
to divergedivergerAnalysts diverge on the outlook.
to reconcileconcilier, rapprocherIt is hard to reconcile these two statements.
upfront paymentpaiement initial (à la signature)The deal includes an upfront payment of €650 million.
earn-out / contingent paymentcomplément de prix conditionnelUp to €250 million is payable as an earn-out.
accretiverelutif (qui améliore le bénéfice par action)The deal should be accretive to earnings by 2028.
to flatter (results)embellir (des résultats)Margins were flattered by a one-off property gain.
price targetobjectif de coursWe raise our price target to 420p.
rating (buy / hold / sell)recommandation (achat / conserver / vente)We maintain our hold rating.
trade bodyorganisation professionnelleThe trade body welcomed the figures.
in real termsen termes réels (corrigé de l'inflation)Exports fell 2% in real terms.
to cherry-picksélectionner à sa convenanceThe statement cherry-picks the most favourable data.
regulatory approvalautorisation réglementaireThe deal is subject to regulatory approval.

Dialogue : Note de veille : trois sources, une seule synthèse

Service stratégie d'un laboratoire concurrent, à Bâle. Une chargée de veille présente à son directeur sa synthèse sur une acquisition annoncée la veille.

PersonnageRépliqueTraduction
Marcus BellSo, Stellan is buying Brindle Diagnostics. What's the real price?Alors, Stellan rachète Brindle Diagnostics. Quel est le vrai prix ?
Lena HoffmannThat depends on who you read. The press release says 'up to nine hundred million euros'.Ça dépend de qui on lit. Le communiqué parle de « jusqu'à neuf cents millions d'euros ».
Marcus Bell'Up to'. I see.« Jusqu'à ». Je vois.
Lena HoffmannExactly. The financial press explains that only six hundred and fifty million is paid upfront. The rest depends on a test getting approval.Exactement. La presse financière explique que seuls six cent cinquante millions sont payés d'emblée. Le reste dépend de l'autorisation d'un test.
Marcus BellSo the sources don't actually contradict each other.Donc les sources ne se contredisent pas vraiment.
Lena HoffmannNo, the figures can be reconciled. But the press release puts the biggest number in the headline.Non, les chiffres se concilient. Mais le communiqué met le plus gros chiffre dans le titre.
Marcus BellWhat does the article add that Stellan didn't mention?Qu'apporte l'article que Stellan n'a pas mentionné ?
Lena HoffmannTwo things: the deal is financed with new debt, and Brindle's main test faces competition from a cheaper product.Deux choses : l'opération est financée par une nouvelle dette, et le principal test de Brindle fait face à un produit concurrent moins cher.
Marcus BellAnd the analysts?Et les analystes ?
Lena HoffmannThey diverge. One calls it 'strategically compelling'. The other thinks Stellan is overpaying for a single product.Ils divergent. L'un la juge « stratégiquement très convaincante ». L'autre pense que Stellan paie trop cher pour un seul produit.
Marcus BellWhere do they agree?Sur quoi s'accordent-ils ?
Lena HoffmannBoth say the approval decision next year is the key risk. That's corroborated by every source.Tous deux disent que la décision d'autorisation de l'an prochain est le risque principal. Toutes les sources le confirment.
Marcus BellThen that's the headline for our note. Facts first, then the interpretations, clearly labelled.Alors c'est le titre de notre note. Les faits d'abord, puis les interprétations, clairement identifiées.
Lena HoffmannUnderstood. I'll put the sources in a table so the board can see who says what.Compris. Je mettrai les sources dans un tableau pour que le conseil voie qui dit quoi.

Exercices corrigés

Exercice 1 — C1-M3-L9-I1 (C2, C1.2)

Lisez le communiqué de presse puis l'article consacré à la même opération. Répondez aux questions en comparant les deux sources.

SOURCE A — Press release, Stellan Pharma AG, 6 May 2026

Stellan Pharma to acquire Brindle Diagnostics in transformational deal worth up to €900 million

Stellan Pharma today announced a definitive agreement to acquire Brindle Diagnostics, a fast-growing developer of rapid diagnostic tests, for a total consideration of up to €900 million. The acquisition marks a strategic milestone in Stellan's journey towards becoming a leader in integrated diagnostics and treatment. Brindle's flagship sepsis test, currently used in more than 400 hospitals, is expected to benefit significantly from Stellan's global commercial network. “This is a perfect fit for our strategy,” said Chief Executive Katrin Vogel. The transaction is expected to be accretive to earnings from 2028 and to close in the third quarter of 2026, subject to customary conditions.

SOURCE B — Article, European Business Daily, 7 May 2026

Stellan's diagnostics bet hinges on US approval

Stellan Pharma's acquisition of Brindle Diagnostics, announced yesterday, has been billed by the company as transformational. A closer look at the terms suggests a more cautious structure. Stellan will pay €650 million upfront, funded largely through a new bond issue, with up to €250 million more payable only if Brindle's sepsis test receives approval from US regulators by the end of 2027.

That approval is far from certain. Brindle's first application was rejected in 2024, and a rival test developed by a larger competitor, priced around 30% lower, is already on the US market. “Without the US, the numbers are much harder to justify,” said one healthcare analyst, who asked not to be named.

Stellan's shares fell 4% on the day of the announcement, while Brindle's privately held investors are understood to have pushed for the earn-out structure in order to secure a higher headline price. The company also confirmed that it expects around €40 million in integration costs, a figure that did not appear in its press release.

Katrin Vogel, who became chief executive last year, has made acquisitions a central part of her strategy. This deal is the largest so far, and investors will be watching the US decision closely.

1. How can the two figures given for the price (up to €900 million and €650 million) be reconciled?
A. Source B has made a calculation error.
B. Stellan has reduced the price it is paying since the press release was issued the previous day.
C. €900m is a ceiling; €650m is paid upfront.
D. €650 million is the cost of integration only.

2. What is the attitude of Source B towards the company's description of the deal as “transformational”?
A. It fully endorses it.
B. It treats it with some scepticism and highlights the risks.
C. It ignores it entirely.
D. It claims the deal will be cancelled.

3. Which information appears in Source B but not in Source A?
A. The number of hospitals using the sepsis test.
B. The expected closing date of the deal.
C. The fact that the deal is expected to be accretive to Stellan's earnings from 2028.
D. The financing through new debt and the expected integration costs.

4. According to Source B, why was the price structured with a large conditional payment?
A. Brindle's investors wanted a higher headline figure.
B. US regulators required it as a condition for approving the sepsis test.
C. Stellan could not raise any debt.
D. The rival test is more expensive.

5. On which point do both sources implicitly agree?
A. The deal is certain to be accretive to Stellan's earnings from 2028 onwards.
B. Brindle's sepsis test is central to the value of the acquisition.
C. Stellan's share price rose after the announcement.
D. Katrin Vogel opposed the acquisition.

Corrigé

1. C — €900m is a ceiling; €650m is paid upfront.. 650 M€ payés d'emblée + jusqu'à 250 M€ conditionnels = jusqu'à 900 M€ : les deux sources sont compatibles. Le communiqué met en avant le maximum (« up to »). Les coûts d'intégration sont de 40 M€.
2. B — It treats it with some scepticism and highlights the risks.. « has been billed by the company as transformational » prend ses distances (c'est la formule de l'entreprise), puis « A closer look… suggests a more cautious structure » et l'incertitude réglementaire. Rien n'annonce une annulation.
3. D — The financing through new debt and the expected integration costs.. L'émission obligataire et les 40 M€ de coûts d'intégration n'apparaissent que dans l'article, qui souligne même que ce chiffre « did not appear in its press release ». Les trois autres informations figurent dans le communiqué.
4. A — Brindle's investors wanted a higher headline figure.. Les investisseurs de Brindle « are understood to have pushed for the earn-out structure in order to secure a higher headline price ». Le concurrent est au contraire environ 30 % moins cher, et Stellan finance l'opération par une émission obligataire.
5. B — Brindle's sepsis test is central to the value of the acquisition.. Le communiqué présente le test sepsis comme le produit phare appelé à bénéficier du réseau de Stellan ; l'article fait dépendre toute l'opération de son autorisation aux États-Unis. Le cours a baissé de 4 %, et la relution 2028 n'est qu'une prévision de l'entreprise.

Exercice 2 — C1-M3-L9-I2 (C2, C1.2)

Lisez les deux notes d'analystes consacrées aux mêmes résultats et répondez aux questions.

Two analyst notes on Harwick & Lowe plc — Full-year results, 12 March 2026

NOTE 1 — Pellham Securities (Rating: BUY, price target raised to 420p)

Harwick & Lowe delivered a strong set of results, with revenue up 7% to £2.3 billion and operating margin expanding by 90 basis points to 8.4%. Like-for-like sales grew 4.1%, comfortably ahead of the sector average, driven by the continued success of the home furnishings range and a further increase in online penetration, now 31% of sales. Net cash also improved, giving the board scope to raise the final dividend by 8%. We believe the market continues to underestimate the benefits of the store refurbishment programme, which is now two-thirds complete, and we see further room for margin expansion as the remaining stores are upgraded. Management's confident tone on the outlook was, in our view, entirely justified. We raise our price target and reiterate our buy rating.

NOTE 2 — Corbett Hale Research (Rating: HOLD, price target unchanged at 340p)

Headline numbers look good, but we would caution against taking them at face value. Of the 90 basis points of margin improvement, around 60 came from a one-off gain on the sale and leaseback of the Birmingham distribution centre. Excluding this, the underlying improvement is modest. We also note that like-for-like growth slowed to 2.2% in the final quarter, from over 5% in the first half, and that the group has, for the first time, stopped disclosing like-for-like figures for its clothing division, which we estimate declined. The refurbishment programme is clearly helping, but the stores already refurbished were, understandably, the most profitable ones. Returns on the remaining third are likely to be lower. Management's outlook was upbeat, but we would like to see evidence of stabilisation in the clothing business before becoming more positive. We maintain our hold rating.

1. On which fact do the two notes agree?
A. Operating margin rose by 90 basis points.
B. The margin improvement was entirely underlying.
C. Like-for-like growth accelerated in the final quarter.
D. The clothing division performed strongly.

2. What does Note 2 suggest by pointing out that the group stopped disclosing like-for-like figures for clothing?
A. The clothing division has been sold.
B. The figures were too small to be relevant.
C. The company may be hiding a disappointing performance.
D. The regulators prohibited the disclosure.

3. How do the two analysts differ regarding the refurbishment programme?
A. Note 1 thinks the programme has failed, whereas Note 2 thinks it has clearly succeeded.
B. Note 1 expects further margin gains; Note 2 expects weaker returns from the rest.
C. Both believe it should be stopped immediately.
D. Note 2 says it has not yet started.

4. How do the analysts' views of management's outlook compare?
A. Both consider it overly pessimistic.
B. Note 2 considers it entirely justified, whereas Note 1 would like to see more evidence.
C. Neither analyst mentions the outlook.
D. Note 1 considers it justified, while Note 2 wants further evidence first.

Corrigé

1. A — Operating margin rose by 90 basis points.. Les deux notes reprennent la hausse de 90 points de base ; la seconde l'interprète différemment (60 points viennent d'une plus-value ponctuelle). La décélération au dernier trimestre contredit la troisième option.
2. C — The company may be hiding a disappointing performance.. L'analyste relève que la publication cesse « for the first time » et estime que la division « declined » : l'omission est interprétée comme le signe d'une mauvaise performance. Rien n'indique une cession.
3. B — Note 1 expects further margin gains; Note 2 expects weaker returns from the rest.. Note 1 : « further room for margin expansion as the remaining stores are upgraded ». Note 2 : les magasins déjà rénovés étaient les plus rentables, donc « Returns on the remaining third are likely to be lower ». Les deux reconnaissent que le programme aide.
4. D — Note 1 considers it justified, while Note 2 wants further evidence first.. Note 1 : « entirely justified ». Note 2 : « upbeat, but we would like to see evidence of stabilisation… before becoming more positive ». La deuxième option inverse les positions.

Exercice 3 — C1-M3-L9-I3 (C2, C1.1)

Lisez la note statistique officielle puis le communiqué d'une organisation professionnelle. Répondez aux questions.

SOURCE A — National Statistics Office, Quarterly Trade Bulletin (extract), 20 February 2026

The value of goods exported by small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) reached £41.2 billion in 2025, an increase of 6.1% compared with 2024. After adjusting for price changes, export volumes were broadly flat, rising by 0.3%. The number of SMEs that exported at least once during the year fell slightly, from 68,400 to 67,100, continuing a decline observed since 2022. Growth in value was concentrated in a small number of sectors, notably machinery and specialist chemicals, while exports of food and drink fell by 3.5% in value. Exports to non-European markets grew faster than exports to Europe. Detailed sectoral and regional tables are available in the annex to this bulletin. Figures for the fourth quarter are provisional and may be revised.

SOURCE B — Press release, Federation of Independent Exporters, 21 February 2026

Record year for small business exports shows the strength of British enterprise

The Federation of Independent Exporters today welcomed official figures showing that small and medium-sized businesses exported a record £41.2 billion of goods last year, up more than 6% on 2024. “These figures are a tribute to the resilience and ambition of our members,” said Director General Hugh Pemberton. “Despite a challenging global environment, independent exporters are winning in markets around the world.”

The Federation highlighted strong performance in machinery and chemicals, as well as rapid growth in sales to Asia and North America. However, it warned that the government's planned changes to export credit support risked undermining this success, and called on ministers to reconsider them before the spring budget. “If we want this growth to continue, now is not the time to reduce support,” Mr Pemberton added. The Federation represents around 9,000 exporting businesses across the country, which it estimates to be roughly one in seven of all exporting SMEs.

1. According to Source A, what explains most of the 6.1% increase in export value?
A. A large rise in the volume of goods exported.
B. An increase in the number of SMEs that exported at least once during the year.
C. Higher prices rather than more goods being sold.
D. Strong growth in food and drink exports.

2. Which information from Source A is omitted in Source B?
A. The total value of SME exports in 2025.
B. The strong performance of machinery and chemicals.
C. The faster growth of exports to markets outside Europe than to European markets.
D. The flat volumes and the fall in the number of exporting SMEs.

3. How does the word “record” in Source B relate to the official data?
A. It is accurate but selectively flattering.
B. It is contradicted by the official figure of £41.2 billion.
C. It refers to the record number of exporting SMEs.
D. It is taken directly from the title of the official bulletin published the previous day.

4. What is the main purpose of Source B?
A. To provide a neutral statistical analysis.
B. To correct errors in the official bulletin.
C. To use the figures to support its lobbying against cuts to export support.
D. To announce that its membership has doubled.

Corrigé

1. C — Higher prices rather than more goods being sold.. « After adjusting for price changes, export volumes were broadly flat, rising by 0.3% » : la hausse en valeur vient surtout des prix. Le nombre d'exportateurs a baissé et l'agroalimentaire a reculé de 3,5 %.
2. D — The flat volumes and the fall in the number of exporting SMEs.. Le communiqué reprend la valeur record, les machines et la chimie, et les marchés hors d'Europe, mais passe sous silence la stagnation des volumes et la baisse du nombre d'exportateurs, deux données moins flatteuses.
3. A — It is accurate but selectively flattering.. La valeur de 41,2 Md£ est bien exacte, mais présentée seule elle masque des volumes stables et moins d'entreprises exportatrices. Le nombre d'exportateurs a diminué : la troisième option est fausse.
4. C — To use the figures to support its lobbying against cuts to export support.. Le communiqué mobilise des chiffres flatteurs pour appuyer sa demande aux ministres (« reconsider them before the spring budget ») : c'est un texte de plaidoyer. Il ne corrige rien et ne parle pas d'une hausse du nombre d'adhérents.

Exercice 4 — C1-M3-L9-I4 (C2, C1.2)

Complétez la note de synthèse comparant plusieurs sources avec le terme qui convient.

The company's claim of a 'record quarter' is not [1] _____ by the regulator's data, which show volumes falling. There is a clear [2] _____ between the two revenue figures, although they can be [3] _____ once currency effects are excluded. The two analysts [4] _____ sharply on the outlook: one argues that margins were [5] _____ by a property sale. The trade body's statement appears to [6] _____ the most favourable statistics.

[1] correlated / collaborated / corroborated / consolidated

[2] discretion / discrepancy / disparity of view / distinction

[3] reconciled / recovered / reconsidered / recounted

[4] differ in / deviate / divert / diverge

[5] fattened / flattened / flattered / flourished

[6] pick up / cherry-pick / hand-pick / pick on

Corrigé

[1] corroborated. « not corroborated by » = non confirmé par. « collaborated » (collaborer) est un paronyme fréquent.
[2] discrepancy. « discrepancy between two figures » = écart, incohérence chiffrée. « discretion » signifie discrétion ou pouvoir d'appréciation.
[3] reconciled. « can be reconciled » = peuvent être conciliés (mis en cohérence). « recounted » signifie recompté ou raconté.
[4] diverge. « diverge sharply on » = divergent fortement sur. « differ in » serait suivi d'un nom (differ in their views) et non de « on the outlook ».
[5] flattered. « margins were flattered by » = embellies artificiellement par. « flattened » signifierait aplaties, stabilisées.
[6] cherry-pick. « cherry-pick » = ne retenir que ce qui arrange. « hand-pick » signifie sélectionner avec soin, sans connotation négative.

title: C1-M3 — Classe virtuelle 2 — Simulation chronométrée et bilan du module
description: Traiter en conditions chronométrées (18 minutes) deux documents complexes de 350 à 450 mots avec au moins 75 % de réponses correctes. Expliquer à l'oral, pour au moins deux erreurs personnelles, le mécanisme du distracteur choisi (exagération, inversion, avis mal attribué, généralisation). Établir un plan individuel de progression comportant trois stratégies de lecture prioritaires pour la suite du parcours.

sections.title: C1-M3-L10 — Classe virtuelle 2 — Simulation chronométrée et bilan du module
sections.contentHtml:
Objectifs :

  • Traiter en conditions chronométrées (18 minutes) deux documents complexes de 350 à 450 mots avec au moins 75 % de réponses correctes.
  • Expliquer à l'oral, pour au moins deux erreurs personnelles, le mécanisme du distracteur choisi (exagération, inversion, avis mal attribué, généralisation).
  • Établir un plan individuel de progression comportant trois stratégies de lecture prioritaires pour la suite du parcours.

Compétence C2 — niveau C1.2 — 60 min — classe virtuelle

Cette seconde classe virtuelle clôt le module par une simulation d'entraînement en temps limité, suivie d'une analyse collective des erreurs et d'un bilan individuel. Il s'agit d'un entraînement pédagogique : les textes sont originaux et la note obtenue est un indicateur interne, jamais un score VTest.

1. Gérer le temps. Pour un texte C1 de 400 mots accompagné de 4 ou 5 questions, comptez environ 8 à 9 minutes : 1 minute de survol (émetteur, type de document, thèse probable), 1 minute de lecture des questions, 6 minutes de lecture ciblée et de réponse, 1 minute de vérification. Si une question vous bloque, choisissez provisoirement la réponse la plus plausible, marquez-la et revenez-y à la fin : les questions suivant l'ordre du texte, vous ne perdrez pas le fil.

2. Les quatre familles de distracteurs C1. Au fil du module, vous avez rencontré systématiquement :

  • l'exagération : certainly, entirely, always, guaranteed face à un texte nuancé ;
  • l'inversion : bons mots du texte, mais relation logique inversée (cause/effet, avant/après, qui fait quoi) ;
  • l'attribution erronée : opinion d'un tiers cité présentée comme celle de l'auteur ;
  • la généralisation : un constat sur un échantillon ou un segment étendu à l'ensemble (9 of 40 transactions devient all transactions).

Identifier la famille de vos propres erreurs est le moyen le plus rapide de progresser.

3. Les questions d'attitude et d'implicite. Pour What is the writer's attitude…?, cherchez les adjectifs évaluatifs, les concessions (while, although, to be fair) et les litotes. Pour What is implied…?, la bonne réponse n'est jamais écrite telle quelle : elle se déduit d'un indice précis. Si une option reprend mot pour mot une phrase du texte, elle répond rarement à une question d'implicite.

4. Les questions de sens d'une expression. Remplacez l'expression par chaque option dans la phrase d'origine : la bonne réponse conserve le sens et le ton du passage.

5. Le bilan. Après la correction, chaque apprenant complète une grille : nombre de bonnes réponses par type de question (information précise, attitude, implicite, expression), famille de distracteurs la plus fréquente, stratégie prioritaire. Le formateur valide ce plan, qui oriente le travail dans le module 6 (mises en situation et évaluation finale).

6. Les acquis du module. Vous savez désormais lire un rapport annuel au-delà des chiffres, repérer la position d'un éditorialiste, évaluer la fiabilité d'une étude ou d'un livre blanc, comprendre la logique d'une clause contractuelle (sans en faire l'analyse juridique), mesurer la force d'une règle interne, décoder une correspondance délicate, lire un rapport d'audit et croiser plusieurs sources. Ces compétences relèvent directement de la compétence C2 du référentiel RS6905 : comprendre en détail des textes longs et complexes et identifier attitudes et opinions, implicites ou déclarées.

Langue clé

AnglaisFrançaisUsage
I fell for the distractor because it exaggerated the writer's view.Je suis tombé dans le piège parce que l'option exagérait l'avis de l'auteur.analyser une erreur personnelle
The answer is implied by the phrase “…”, not stated.La réponse est sous-entendue par l'expression « … », non affirmée.justifier une réponse d'implicite
This option generalises from a sample to the whole population.Cette option généralise d'un échantillon à l'ensemble.identifier un distracteur de généralisation
My priority strategy is to check who is speaking before answering.Ma stratégie prioritaire est de vérifier qui parle avant de répondre.formuler un objectif de progression
Trading has been below our expectations.L'activité a été inférieure à nos attentes.formule typique d'un avertissement sur résultats
We now expect full-year profit to be at the lower end of the range.Nous prévoyons désormais un bénéfice annuel dans le bas de la fourchette.révision à la baisse adoucie

Vocabulaire

TermeTraductionExemple
profit warningavertissement sur résultatsThe shares fell 18% after the profit warning.
trading updatepoint d'activitéThe company will publish a trading update in July.
at the lower end of the rangedans le bas de la fourchetteProfit is expected at the lower end of the range.
activist investorinvestisseur activisteAn activist investor has built a 6% stake.
stakeparticipation (au capital)The fund holds a 6.2% stake in the company.
to underperformfaire moins bien (que le marché, les concurrents)The shares have underperformed the sector for three years.
capital allocationallocation du capitalShareholders question the board's capital allocation.
strategic reviewrevue stratégiqueThe fund calls for a strategic review of the division.
to divestcéder (une activité)The group should divest its non-core businesses.
boardroomconseil d'administration, sphère dirigeanteThe dispute has spilled out of the boardroom.
destockingdéstockage (par les clients)Customer destocking hit volumes in the second quarter.
order intakeprises de commandesOrder intake recovered in May.
to engage constructivelydialoguer de manière constructiveThe board is willing to engage constructively with all shareholders.

Dialogue : Débriefing de la simulation

Fin de la simulation chronométrée en classe virtuelle : le formateur analyse les résultats avec deux apprenantes.

PersonnageRépliqueTraduction
Ben CarterTime's up. Let's look at the results. The question most of you got wrong was number three on the activist letter.Le temps est écoulé. Regardons les résultats. La question la plus ratée est la numéro trois sur la lettre de l'investisseur activiste.
Inès GarnierI chose 'the fund will vote against the chairman'. It seemed obvious.J'ai choisi « le fonds votera contre le président ». Ça me semblait évident.
Ben CarterWhat exactly does the letter say?Que dit exactement la lettre ?
Inès Garnier'We are not, at this stage, seeking changes to the board, but we reserve the right to…' Oh. It's conditional.« Nous ne demandons pas, à ce stade, de changement au conseil, mais nous nous réservons le droit de… » Ah. C'est conditionnel.
Ben CarterExactly. Which family of distractor was that?Exactement. De quelle famille de distracteur s'agissait-il ?
Inès GarnierExaggeration. It turned a possibility into a decision.L'exagération. Elle transformait une possibilité en décision.
Ben CarterSarah, you got that one right, but you missed question two on the trading update.Sarah, tu as eu celle-là juste, mais tu as raté la question deux sur le point d'activité.
Sarah KaplanI said the problem affected all divisions. But it was only the industrial coatings business.J'ai dit que le problème touchait toutes les divisions. Mais c'était seulement les revêtements industriels.
Ben CarterSo that's a generalisation. Funny, given that you're an auditor.Donc c'est une généralisation. Amusant, pour une auditrice.
Sarah KaplanI know! In my job I'd never extend a finding from one unit to the whole group.Je sais ! Dans mon métier, je n'étendrais jamais un constat d'une entité à tout le groupe.
Ben CarterThen use that professional reflex when you read. Ask yourself: what's the scope of this statement?Alors utilise ce réflexe professionnel en lisant. Demande-toi : quel est le périmètre de cette affirmation ?
Inès GarnierAnd for me: check whether it's a fact, an intention or a possibility.Et pour moi : vérifier s'il s'agit d'un fait, d'une intention ou d'une possibilité.
Ben CarterPerfect. Write those down as your priority strategies in the progress grid.Parfait. Notez-les comme stratégies prioritaires dans la grille de progression.
Sarah KaplanWill we have another timed practice in module six?Aurons-nous un autre entraînement chronométré au module six ?
Ben CarterYes, a longer one covering all four skills. Remember, it's practice, not the real test, so use it to experiment.Oui, un plus long qui couvre les quatre compétences. N'oubliez pas : c'est un entraînement, pas le vrai test, alors servez-vous-en pour expérimenter.

Déroulé de la classe virtuelle

  1. 5 min — Accueil, consignes de la simulation (entraînement pédagogique, score interne), rappel des quatre familles de distracteurs.
  2. 18 min — Simulation chronométrée individuelle : items C1-M3-L10-I1 et C1-M3-L10-I2 (9 min chacun), caméras allumées, sans dictionnaire.
  3. 15 min — Correction collective : pour chaque question, citation du passage décisif et identification de la famille du distracteur le plus choisi.
  4. 7 min — Révision lexicale rapide : item C1-M3-L10-I3 et retour sur les expressions clés du module.
  5. 10 min — Bilan individuel : grille de progression (réussite par type de question, famille d'erreur dominante, trois stratégies prioritaires), validation par le formateur.
  6. 5 min — Clôture : consignes de la mise en pratique du module et du quiz de validation, présentation du module 6.

Exercices corrigés

Exercice 1 — C1-M3-L10-I1 (C2, C1.2)

Simulation chronométrée (9 minutes). Lisez la lettre ouverte d'un investisseur et répondez aux questions dans l'ordre du texte.

Open letter to the Board of Directors of Dunmore Industrial plc
From: Albright Hollis Capital Partners
2 June 2026

Dear Members of the Board,

As you know, funds managed by Albright Hollis now hold approximately 6.2% of Dunmore's issued share capital, making us one of the company's largest shareholders. We have invested in Dunmore because we believe it owns several excellent businesses whose value is not reflected in the current share price. We are writing publicly today because our private discussions with management over the past nine months have not, in our view, produced a satisfactory response.

The facts are straightforward. Over the past five years, Dunmore's shares have underperformed the sector index by 38%. During the same period, the Group has spent more than £600 million on acquisitions, most of which have delivered returns below the company's own cost of capital. Meanwhile, the precision instruments division — by some distance the Group's most profitable business — has been starved of investment and has lost market share to more focused competitors.

We recognise that the Board has recently announced a cost reduction programme, and we welcome it as far as it goes. It does not, however, address the central issue, which is capital allocation. A conglomerate structure that may have made sense two decades ago now obscures the value of the Group's best assets and allows weaker businesses to absorb resources that would be better used elsewhere.

We therefore urge the Board to commission an independent strategic review of the Group's portfolio, including the option of separating the precision instruments division, and to report its conclusions to shareholders before the end of the year.

We are not, at this stage, seeking changes to the composition of the Board, and we have no wish to engage in a public dispute. We have great respect for the company's employees and for its long history. We do, however, reserve the right to take further steps to protect the interests of all shareholders should the Board decline to act.

We would welcome the opportunity to discuss these proposals with the Chairman at his earliest convenience.

Yours faithfully,

Miriam Albright
Managing Partner

1. Why has the fund decided to write an open letter?
A. Because it has just bought its first shares in Dunmore.
B. Because the company refused to meet the fund's representatives.
C. Because it believes private talks have not produced an adequate response.
D. Because the fund intends to sell its stake.

2. What is the fund's attitude towards the cost reduction programme?
A. It considers it the solution to Dunmore's problems.
B. It rejects it outright as harmful to employees and damaging to the company's long history.
C. It considers it a positive step that leaves the real problem unaddressed.
D. It says it has not yet been informed of it.

3. What does the fund state about its intentions regarding the Board?
A. It will vote against the re-election of the Chairman at the next Annual General Meeting.
B. It has already demanded the replacement of several directors.
C. It will never take any further action.
D. No Board changes for now, but more action possible.

4. What is the overall tone of the letter?
A. Courteous on the surface but firm and implicitly threatening.
B. Hostile and insulting towards the management.
C. Enthusiastic and fully supportive of the Board's recent cost reduction programme.
D. Uncertain and apologetic.

Corrigé

1. C — Because it believes private talks have not produced an adequate response.. « our private discussions with management over the past nine months have not, in our view, produced a satisfactory response ». Des discussions ont donc eu lieu : la direction n'a pas refusé de rencontrer le fonds.
2. C — It considers it a positive step that leaves the real problem unaddressed.. « we welcome it as far as it goes. It does not, however, address the central issue » : accueil limité (« as far as it goes »), puis réserve sur l'essentiel, l'allocation du capital.
3. D — No Board changes for now, but more action possible.. « We are not, at this stage, seeking changes… We do, however, reserve the right to take further steps… should the Board decline to act » : possibilité conditionnelle, ni décision ni renoncement. Le vote contre le président est une exagération.
4. A — Courteous on the surface but firm and implicitly threatening.. Formules courtoises (« great respect », « no wish to engage in a public dispute », invitation au dialogue) mais faits durs et menace voilée (« reserve the right »). Il n'y a ni insulte ni excuse.

Exercice 2 — C1-M3-L10-I2 (C2, C1.2)

Simulation chronométrée (9 minutes). Lisez le point d'activité publié par une entreprise cotée et répondez aux questions.

Lindqvist Coatings Group plc — Trading Update for the five months to 31 May 2026

Lindqvist Coatings Group, the international supplier of protective and decorative coatings, issues the following update ahead of its Annual General Meeting today.

Group revenue for the five months to 31 May was 3% lower than in the same period last year at constant currency, and 4% lower on a reported basis. Performance has varied significantly across our divisions. The Decorative division, which represents around 45% of Group revenue, has continued to perform well, with revenue up 5% and margins slightly ahead of last year, supported by the successful launch of our low-odour interior range.

Trading in the Industrial Coatings division has, however, been below our expectations. Several large customers in the automotive and agricultural equipment sectors have reduced orders as they work through elevated inventory levels built up in 2025. As a result, divisional revenue declined by 14% over the period. Order intake has shown early signs of stabilisation in May, but visibility for the second half remains limited, and we do not expect a meaningful recovery in volumes before the final quarter.

We have taken prompt action to protect profitability, including a reduction in temporary staffing, tighter control of discretionary spending and the deferral of a planned capacity expansion at our Gdańsk plant. These measures are expected to deliver annualised savings of around £12 million, of which approximately half will benefit the current financial year.

Taking these factors into account, the Board now expects adjusted operating profit for the full year to be at the lower end of the range of market expectations, which currently stands at £118–131 million. The Group's balance sheet remains strong, with net debt of 1.1 times earnings, and the Board continues to expect to recommend a progressive dividend.

The Group will publish its interim results on 28 July 2026.

1. What does the second paragraph tell us about the Decorative division?
A. It accounts for most of the fall in Group revenue.
B. It has performed well, helped by a new product line.
C. It represents the majority of Group revenue.
D. Its margins have fallen because of the cost of launching the new low-odour range.

2. Which division is responsible for the disappointing performance, and why?
A. Industrial Coatings, due to customer destocking.
B. All divisions equally, because of currency movements.
C. Decorative, because the launch costs of the new range have reduced its profitability.
D. Industrial Coatings, because the Gdańsk plant was closed.

3. What does “visibility for the second half remains limited” imply?
A. The company will stop publishing forecasts.
B. The second half is certain to be worse than the first.
C. Customers have cancelled all their orders for the year.
D. The company cannot predict second-half demand with confidence.

4. What is the real message of the sentence about full-year profit?
A. Profit will exceed market expectations.
B. The Board is withdrawing its full-year guidance altogether because visibility is limited.
C. This is a cautiously worded downgrade of profit expectations.
D. Profit will fall below £118 million.

Corrigé

1. B — It has performed well, helped by a new product line.. Revenue +5 %, marges « slightly ahead », grâce à la nouvelle gamme intérieure peu odorante. La division pèse environ 45 % du chiffre d'affaires, donc pas la majorité.
2. A — Industrial Coatings, due to customer destocking.. Les clients industriels « have reduced orders as they work through elevated inventory levels » (déstockage). Les chiffres sont à taux de change constants, et l'usine de Gdańsk n'est pas fermée : seul un projet d'extension est reporté.
3. D — The company cannot predict second-half demand with confidence.. « visibility » = capacité à prévoir. La formule signale l'incertitude, sans prédire forcément une dégradation ; d'ailleurs les commandes montrent « early signs of stabilisation ».
4. C — This is a cautiously worded downgrade of profit expectations.. « at the lower end of the range » est une révision à la baisse formulée avec prudence : le bénéfice resterait dans la fourchette, mais près de 118 M£. C'est un avertissement atténué, pas un abandon des prévisions.

Exercice 3 — C1-M3-L10-I3 (C2, C1.2)

Révision finale : complétez le paragraphe avec le terme qui convient.

After a second profit [1] _____ in six months, an activist investor has built a 7% [2] _____ in the group and is calling for a [3] _____ review. The fund argues that the shares have [4] _____ the sector for years because of poor capital [5] _____, and that the board should [6] _____ its loss-making packaging business.

[1] warning / alert / notice / alarm

[2] stock / share / steak / stake

[3] strategical / strategy / strategic / stratified

[4] underestimated / underperformed / undergone / underwritten

[5] allocation / allowance / allotment / location

[6] devise / invest / divert / divest

Corrigé

[1] warning. Collocation figée : « profit warning » (avertissement sur résultats). « profit alert » n'est pas l'expression d'usage.
[2] stake. « build a 7% stake » = constituer une participation de 7 %. « steak » est un homophone ; « share » désignerait une action à l'unité.
[3] strategic. Il faut l'adjectif : « a strategic review ». « strategy review » existe parfois, mais « strategic review » est la formule consacrée ; « strategical » est rare et vieilli.
[4] underperformed. « have underperformed the sector » = ont fait moins bien que le secteur. « underwritten » signifie garanti (une émission).
[5] allocation. « capital allocation » = la façon dont l'entreprise affecte ses ressources. « allotment » désigne l'attribution d'actions lors d'une émission.
[6] divest. « divest a business » = céder une activité. « invest » dirait l'inverse ; « divert » signifie détourner.

title: C1-M3 — Bilan du module : Analyse de documents complexes
description: Ce module entraîne l'apprenant à comprendre en détail des documents professionnels longs et complexes : rapports annuels et lettres aux actionnaires, éditoriaux et tribunes économiques, études de marché et livres blancs, clauses contractuelles, politiques internes ESG et de conformité, correspondance sensible et rapports d'audit. Il apprend à identifier les attitudes et opinions, implicites ou déclarées, à décoder euphémismes, litotes et précautions oratoires, et à croiser plusieurs sources pour en dégager convergences, contradictions et omissions. Deux classes virtuelles permettent de s'exercer à la justification des réponses et à une simulation chronométrée.
