sections.title: C1-M6-L1 — Simulation C1 n° 1 : écouter et interpréter
sections.contentHtml:
Objectifs :

  • Répondre en 30 minutes maximum aux six activités d'écoute de la simulation (deux déclarations, un dialogue court, un dialogue long, un monologue, une réponse construite).
  • Identifier dans chaque enregistrement la position implicite ou la réserve d'au moins un locuteur.
  • Obtenir au moins 8 bonnes réponses sur 10 aux QCM et relever sans erreur trois informations précises dans la réponse construite.

Compétence C1 — niveau C1.1 — 45 min

Cette première simulation de compréhension orale reprend toutes les familles d'activités décrites dans le référentiel de la compétence C1 : déclarations suivies d'une question, dialogue court avec trois questions, dialogue long et monologue en deux parties (une question par partie) et réponse construite. Rappel important : il s'agit d'un entraînement interne conçu par l'organisme, pas du test VTest. Les enregistrements, les questions et le pourcentage affiché sont les nôtres ; ils donnent un niveau estimé, jamais un résultat officiel.

Ce qui change au niveau C1

Le critère C1 du référentiel parle de discours étendu sur des sujets abstraits et complexes, de nuances élevées et d'un bon niveau de discernement. Concrètement, les bonnes réponses ne reprennent presque jamais les mots entendus. Il faut interpréter :

  • les réserves polies : I'm not entirely convinced, I'd be wary of…, that's a big if signalent un désaccord sans le dire ;
  • les idiomes professionnels : a stopgap, to move the goalposts, to bite the bullet, to be stretched thin ;
  • les concessions : Granted, … but…, Admittedly… — l'idée qui suit but est souvent celle qui compte ;
  • les changements de position dans les dialogues longs : la décision finale contredit parfois la première proposition.

Gestion du temps (30 minutes pour 6 activités)

  1. Lisez la question et les options avant d'écouter (15 à 20 secondes). Repérez le mot interrogatif et ce qui distingue les quatre options.
  2. Première écoute complète, réponse provisoire immédiate.
  3. Réécoute ciblée seulement si vous hésitez entre deux options. Dans cette simulation, comme le prévoit le référentiel, l'audio peut être rejoué tant que le chronomètre tourne — mais chaque réécoute coûte entre 30 secondes et 2 minutes.
  4. Budget indicatif : 2 minutes par déclaration, 5 minutes pour le dialogue court, 7 minutes pour le dialogue long et le monologue, 5 minutes pour la réponse construite, 2 minutes de marge.
  5. Ne restez jamais bloqué : si une question résiste, cochez l'option la plus probable, notez-la et revenez-y à la fin.

Pièges typiques des distracteurs C1

  • l'option qui reprend un mot entendu dans une idée fausse ;
  • l'option trop forte (refuses, always) quand le locuteur ne fait qu'exprimer un doute ;
  • l'option qui correspond à la position initiale, abandonnée ensuite.

Après la simulation, lisez toutes les explications, y compris pour les questions réussies, et notez dans votre carnet le type d'activité et le type de piège qui vous ont coûté des points. Ces notes alimenteront le bilan de la leçon 8.

Langue clé

AnglaisFrançaisUsage
I'm not entirely convinced that's the right call.Je ne suis pas tout à fait convaincu que ce soit la bonne décision.désaccord atténué à interpréter comme une réserve
Granted, it's cheaper, but the lead times are a real concern.Certes, c'est moins cher, mais les délais posent un vrai problème.concession : l'idée importante suit « but »
That's a stopgap, not a solution.C'est une solution provisoire, pas une vraie solution.jugement critique formulé par un idiome
On reflection, I'd rather we held off until the audit.Réflexion faite, je préférerais qu'on attende l'audit.changement de position dans un dialogue long
We're stretched thin as it is.Nous sommes déjà débordés.argument implicite contre une charge supplémentaire

Vocabulaire

TermeTraductionExemple
stopgapsolution provisoire, bouche-trouThe temporary staff are a stopgap until we automate the line.
to move the goalpostschanger les règles en cours de routeThe client keeps moving the goalposts on the specifications.
to be stretched thinêtre débordé, avoir trop de chargeThe support team is stretched thin after the launch.
to hold offattendre, différerLet's hold off on the announcement until Monday.
lead timedélai d'approvisionnementLead times have doubled since the spring.
headcounteffectifHeadcount will remain flat next year.
to roll outdéployerWe'll roll out the new portal region by region.
pilot schemeprojet piloteThe pilot scheme covers two sites.
buy-inadhésionWithout buy-in from the sales team, the tool will fail.
caveatréserve, mise en gardeThere's one caveat: the data only covers six months.
to backfillremplacer (un poste) temporairementWe need to backfill her role during the secondment.
sign-offvalidation formelleWe still need sign-off from legal.

Dialogue : Conseils : écouter entre les lignes

Capsule de conseils filmée dans le studio de l'organisme. Une formatrice échange avec un apprenant, responsable achats, juste avant la simulation.

PersonnageRépliqueTraduction
Karim BenaliHelen, in the last practice test I understood every word and still got three questions wrong. How is that possible?Helen, au dernier entraînement j'ai compris chaque mot et j'ai quand même eu trois questions fausses. Comment est-ce possible ?
Helen MarshAt this level, understanding the words is only half the job. The questions test what people mean, not just what they say.À ce niveau, comprendre les mots n'est que la moitié du travail. Les questions portent sur ce que les gens veulent dire, pas seulement sur ce qu'ils disent.
Karim BenaliYou mean the implicit opinions?Tu veux dire les opinions implicites ?
Helen MarshExactly. If a manager says 'I'm not entirely convinced', the answer won't be 'she agrees with some reservations'. She's actually against it.Exactement. Si une responsable dit « je ne suis pas tout à fait convaincue », la réponse ne sera pas « elle est d'accord avec quelques réserves ». En réalité, elle est contre.
Karim BenaliThat's subtle. And what about the long dialogues? I tend to lose track.C'est subtil. Et pour les dialogues longs ? J'ai tendance à décrocher.
Helen MarshListen for the turning points: 'on reflection', 'having said that', 'actually'. The final decision often comes after one of those.Écoute les points de bascule : « on reflection », « having said that », « actually ». La décision finale vient souvent après l'un d'eux.
Karim BenaliAnd should I replay everything? The audio can be replayed while the timer runs.Et je dois tout réécouter ? L'audio peut être rejoué tant que le chronomètre tourne.
Helen MarshOnly when you're torn between two options. Replaying everything is the quickest way to run out of time.Seulement quand tu hésites entre deux options. Tout réécouter, c'est le moyen le plus rapide de manquer de temps.
Karim BenaliSo, one full listen, a provisional answer, and a targeted replay if needed.Donc une écoute complète, une réponse provisoire et une réécoute ciblée si besoin.
Helen MarshThat's it. And remember, this is our internal practice, not the VTest itself. Use it to find your weak spots.C'est ça. Et souviens-toi : c'est notre entraînement interne, pas le VTest lui-même. Sers-t'en pour repérer tes points faibles.
Karim BenaliGot it. I'll keep a note of the traps that catch me.Compris. Je vais noter les pièges qui me font tomber.
Helen MarshPerfect. Thirty minutes on the clock, and good luck.Parfait. Trente minutes au chronomètre, et bonne chance.

Exercices corrigés

Exercice 1 — C1-M6-L1-I1 (C1, C1.1)

Déclaration : écoutez l'énoncé et choisissez l'interprétation correcte. Budget conseillé : 2 minutes.

Transcription :

Operations DirectorBringing in agency staff will get us through the peak, granted, but if we're still relying on them in March, we'll have to admit that the scheduling problem was never really fixed.

1. What is the speaker's view of using agency staff?
A. It is the best long-term option for getting through the peak season
B. It should be stopped before the peak begins
C. It is a short-term fix that leaves the real problem unsolved
D. It has already solved the scheduling problem

Corrigé

1. C — It is a short-term fix that leaves the real problem unsolved. « granted » concède l'utilité immédiate (passer le pic), puis « the scheduling problem was never really fixed » montre que ce n'est qu'un palliatif. L'option « already solved » est le piège : la locutrice dit précisément le contraire.

Exercice 2 — C1-M6-L1-I2 (C1, C1.1)

Déclaration : écoutez l'énoncé et choisissez l'interprétation correcte.

Transcription :

Finance ManagerI'd be wary of announcing the new pricing before the board has signed it off; last time we did that, we ended up walking it back within a week.

1. What does the speaker imply?
A. An early announcement might have to be withdrawn
B. The board has already rejected the new pricing
C. The pricing was successfully announced early last time
D. He wants to announce the pricing within a week

Corrigé

1. A — An early announcement might have to be withdrawn. « we ended up walking it back » = nous avons dû faire marche arrière. Il met en garde contre une annonce prématurée. Le conseil n'a pas rejeté le tarif : il ne l'a simplement pas encore validé (« before the board has signed it off »).

Exercice 3 — C1-M6-L1-I3 (C1, C1.1)

Dialogue court : écoutez l'échange puis répondez aux trois questions. Budget conseillé : 5 minutes.

Transcription :

Priya NairTom, have you seen the latest draft of the Harrowgate contract? They've added a clause about quarterly volume reviews.
Tom EllisonI have. On paper it sounds harmless, but it basically lets them renegotiate prices every three months. That's moving the goalposts after we agreed a two-year deal.
Priya NairSo you'd push back on it?
Tom EllisonNot reject it outright; they'd dig their heels in. I'd rather propose annual reviews with a cap of three per cent either way.
Priya NairThat seems fair. I'll run it past legal this afternoon and get back to them by Thursday.

1. What is Tom's main concern about the new clause?
A. It shortens the length of the contract
B. It would let the supplier change prices often
C. It reduces the volumes the company can order each quarter
D. It was added without informing the legal team

2. How does Tom suggest responding?
A. By rejecting the clause completely
B. By accepting the clause without changes
C. By asking for quarterly reviews with no limit on prices
D. By offering less frequent, capped reviews

3. What will Priya do next?
A. Have the proposal checked internally
B. Sign the contract on Thursday
C. Call the supplier this afternoon
D. Draft a new two-year contract

Corrigé

1. B — It would let the supplier change prices often. « it basically lets them renegotiate prices every three months » : le fournisseur pourrait revoir ses prix chaque trimestre. La durée du contrat (deux ans) n'est pas modifiée.
2. D — By offering less frequent, capped reviews. « annual reviews with a cap of three per cent » : revue annuelle avec un plafond. Il écarte explicitement le rejet total : « Not reject it outright ».
3. A — Have the proposal checked internally. « I'll run it past legal » = je vais le faire vérifier par le service juridique. Le jeudi est l'échéance de la réponse au fournisseur, pas une date de signature.

Exercice 4 — C1-M6-L1-I4 (C1, C1.1)

Dialogue long en deux parties : écoutez chaque partie puis répondez à la question correspondante. Repérez le changement de position. Budget conseillé : 7 minutes.

Transcription :

Sofia DelgadoSo, the proposal is to roll out the new scheduling software across all five depots in January. Daniel, you've been running the pilot scheme in Leeds. How has it gone?
Daniel OkaforMixed, honestly. Route planning is about fifteen per cent faster, which is great. But the drivers found the mobile app confusing, and for the first month we had more missed slots, not fewer.
Sofia DelgadoAnd now?
Daniel OkaforNow it's settled down, but only because our supervisor spent hours coaching people one to one. Without that, I doubt we'd have got the buy-in.
Sofia DelgadoMy instinct was to go for all five depots at once, to avoid running two systems. But if the coaching is what made the difference, the other sites simply don't have that capacity in January.
Daniel OkaforNo, they're stretched thin with the post-holiday returns.
Sofia DelgadoThen, on reflection, let's phase it: Bristol and Derby in February, the remaining two in April, and we'll budget for a trainer on each site for the first three weeks.
Daniel OkaforThat would make a big difference. I can share the training notes we put together in Leeds.

1. What does Daniel suggest about the pilot?
A. It failed because the software was too slow for route planning
B. It was successful from the very first week
C. Its success relied mainly on one-to-one support
D. The drivers refused to use the mobile app

2. What does Sofia finally decide?
A. To launch the software in all depots in January
B. To phase in the software with on-site training
C. To postpone the project until the returns period is over
D. To keep the pilot running in Leeds only

Corrigé

1. C — Its success relied mainly on one-to-one support. « only because our supervisor spent hours coaching people one to one » : la réussite tient à l'accompagnement individuel. Le logiciel a au contraire accéléré la planification de 15 %, et les chauffeurs ont trouvé l'appli confuse, pas refusé de l'utiliser.
2. B — To phase in the software with on-site training. « on reflection, let's phase it » + « a trainer on each site » : déploiement progressif avec formateur sur place. Le lancement simultané en janvier était son idée initiale, abandonnée : c'est le distracteur le plus tentant.

Exercice 5 — C1-M6-L1-I5 (C1, C1.1)

Monologue en deux parties : écoutez chaque partie puis répondez à la question correspondante. Budget conseillé : 7 minutes.

Transcription :

Rebecca LoweGood morning, everyone. As you know, our customer satisfaction score dipped to seventy-one last quarter, its lowest in three years. The instinctive reaction would be to blame the new ticketing system, and it certainly had teething problems.
Rebecca LoweBut when we dug into the comments, the system was mentioned in fewer than one complaint in ten. What customers actually objected to was being passed from one agent to another without anyone taking ownership of their case.
Rebecca LoweSo, from next month, every case will have a named owner from first contact to resolution. Agents will be able to call in specialists, but the owner stays the customer's single point of contact.
Rebecca LoweI'm not expecting miracles in the first few weeks; handling times will probably go up before they come down. That's a trade-off I'm prepared to accept, and I'd ask team leaders not to judge the change on the first month's figures.

1. According to the speaker, what mainly caused the drop in satisfaction?
A. Technical problems with the new ticketing system
B. A reduction in the number of support agents
C. Long waiting times on the phone
D. Cases being transferred with no clear owner

2. What does she ask team leaders to do?
A. Be patient before evaluating the new approach
B. Reduce handling times immediately
C. Assign specialists to every case
D. Report the first month's figures to her daily

Corrigé

1. D — Cases being transferred with no clear owner. « being passed from one agent to another without anyone taking ownership » : transferts sans responsable du dossier. Le système de tickets est cité dans moins d'une réclamation sur dix : c'est le piège, présenté comme la « réaction instinctive ».
2. A — Be patient before evaluating the new approach. « not to judge the change on the first month's figures » : ne pas juger trop tôt. Elle prévoit au contraire que les temps de traitement augmentent d'abord.

Exercice 6 — C1-M6-L1-I6 (C1, C1.1)

Réponse construite : écoutez le message vocal et écrivez uniquement l'information demandée (un nom, un chiffre, une date). Attention aux informations corrigées en cours de message.

Transcription :

Martin KeaneHi Laura, Martin Keane from Veltrane Packaging. Quick update on the recyclable trays. We'd quoted you a minimum order of forty thousand units, but our plant manager has agreed to bring that down to twenty-five thousand for the first run, so you can test the market. Unit price stays at eleven pence. The only catch is the tooling: we'd need your final artwork by the ninth of May at the latest, not the fifteenth as I said last week. Give me a ring if that's tight.

1. What is the name of the supplier?

2. What is the new minimum order for the first run (number of units)?

3. What is the deadline for the final artwork?

Corrigé

1. Veltrane Packaging / Veltrane / veltrane packaging / veltrane. « Martin Keane from Veltrane Packaging ».
2. 25000 / 25,000 / 25 000 / twenty-five thousand / twenty five thousand. Le minimum initial (40 000) est ramené à 25 000 : « bring that down to twenty-five thousand ». Le piège est de noter le premier chiffre entendu.
3. 9 May / May 9 / 9th May / May 9th / the 9th of May / ninth of May / 9/5 / 09/05. « by the ninth of May at the latest, not the fifteenth » : la date du 15 est corrigée.

title: C1-M6 — Simulation C1 n° 2 : débats, prises de position et nuances
description: Réaliser en 30 minutes une seconde série complète d'activités d'écoute de niveau C1.2, sans dépasser deux réécoutes au total par activité. Distinguer, dans un échange entre deux ou trois personnes, la position de chaque locuteur et le point exact de désaccord. Obtenir au moins 8 bonnes réponses sur 10 et comparer son résultat avec celui de la simulation n° 1 pour mesurer sa progression.
imageQuery: business English Simulation C1 n° 2 : débats, prises de position et nuances

sections.title: C1-M6-L2 — Simulation C1 n° 2 : débats, prises de position et nuances
sections.contentHtml:
Objectifs :

  • Réaliser en 30 minutes une seconde série complète d'activités d'écoute de niveau C1.2, sans dépasser deux réécoutes au total par activité.
  • Distinguer, dans un échange entre deux ou trois personnes, la position de chaque locuteur et le point exact de désaccord.
  • Obtenir au moins 8 bonnes réponses sur 10 et comparer son résultat avec celui de la simulation n° 1 pour mesurer sa progression.

Compétence C1 — niveau C1.2 — 45 min

Cette deuxième simulation conserve la même structure que la première (deux déclarations, un dialogue court, un dialogue long, un monologue, une réponse construite) mais elle monte d'un cran : les enregistrements sont plus denses, les locuteurs argumentent et prennent position, et les questions portent davantage sur l'attitude et le point de désaccord. C'est exactement ce que vise le troisième volet de la compétence C1 du référentiel : identifier la problématique lors d'un échange en repérant les interactions menant à des débats et à des prises de position. Il s'agit, là encore, d'un entraînement interne de l'organisme, et non du test VTest.

Repérer une prise de position

Au niveau C1.2, les locuteurs signalent rarement leur avis par I agree ou I disagree. Écoutez plutôt :

  • l'adhésion conditionnelle : I could live with that, provided… — l'accord dépend d'une condition, et la question portera souvent sur cette condition ;
  • le désaccord stratégique : I take your point, but I'd question the timing — la personne n'est pas contre l'idée, elle conteste un aspect précis ;
  • l'ironie et l'euphémisme : That's one way of putting it ou It wasn't our finest hour traduisent une critique ;
  • la mise à distance : Officially, the line is… suggère que le locuteur ne partage pas la position officielle.

Méthode pour les questions sur l'attitude

  1. Classez mentalement chaque option sur une échelle : enthousiaste — favorable — réservé — opposé.
  2. Comparez avec l'intensité réelle des mots entendus. Les distracteurs C1 sont souvent un cran trop forts ou un cran trop faibles.
  3. Vérifiez que l'option attribue bien l'opinion au bon locuteur : dans les dialogues, un distracteur fréquent prête à l'un ce que dit l'autre.

Gestion du temps

Gardez le même budget que dans la simulation n° 1 (2 + 2 + 5 + 7 + 7 + 5 minutes, 2 minutes de marge). Fixez-vous une règle supplémentaire : pas plus de deux réécoutes au total par activité. Si, après la seconde écoute, vous hésitez toujours entre deux options, choisissez celle qui respecte le mieux l'intensité de l'opinion exprimée et passez à la suite. Pour la réponse construite, notez les chiffres pendant l'écoute sous forme brute (« 3,2 M », « 18/6 »), puis recopiez-les proprement.

Comparer vos deux simulations

À la fin, reportez votre score interne dans le tableau de suivi et comparez-le avec celui de la simulation n° 1. Une baisse légère est normale, puisque le niveau visé est plus élevé ; ce qui compte, c'est le type d'erreur. Si vous perdez des points surtout sur les questions d'attitude, travaillez les marqueurs de nuance ; si ce sont les chiffres et dates, entraînez-vous à la prise de notes rapide.

Langue clé

AnglaisFrançaisUsage
I could live with that, provided we review it in six months.Je pourrais m'en accommoder, à condition qu'on le revoie dans six mois.accord conditionnel : la condition est l'information clé
I take your point, but I'd question the timing.Je comprends votre argument, mais je m'interroge sur le calendrier.désaccord partiel sur un aspect précis
It wasn't exactly our finest hour.Ce n'était pas vraiment notre heure de gloire.euphémisme exprimant une critique
Officially, the line is that nothing has changed.Officiellement, le discours est que rien n'a changé.mise à distance de la position officielle
Where I'd part company with you is on the budget.Là où je ne vous suis plus, c'est sur le budget.identification du point exact de désaccord

Vocabulaire

TermeTraductionExemple
to part company with someonene plus être d'accord avec quelqu'unThat's where I part company with the consultants.
to dig one's heels incamper sur ses positionsThe union dug its heels in over weekend shifts.
a hard sellune idée difficile à faire accepterA price increase will be a hard sell this year.
to hedge one's betsménager ses arrièresWe're hedging our bets with two suppliers.
attritiondéparts naturels (non remplacés)We'll reduce headcount through attrition, not layoffs.
churntaux d'attrition des clientsChurn rose sharply after the price change.
to front-loadconcentrer en début de périodeThe costs are front-loaded, but savings come later.
upsidepotentiel de gain, avantageThe upside is a much shorter delivery time.
to cannibalisecannibaliser (les ventes)The cheaper model may cannibalise sales of the premium range.
ballpark figureordre de grandeurCan you give me a ballpark figure for the cost?
contingencyprovision pour imprévus, plan de secoursWe've built a ten per cent contingency into the budget.
to take something on boardprendre en compteWe've taken your feedback on board.
the bottom linel'essentiel ; le résultat netThe bottom line is that we can't afford a delay.

Dialogue : Débrief : qui pense quoi ?

Classe d'entraînement enregistrée. Le formateur revient avec une apprenante sur un extrait de réunion à trois voix qui l'a mise en difficulté.

PersonnageRépliqueTraduction
Claire VasseurIn the meeting recording, I thought the finance director supported the new product line. Apparently she didn't.Dans l'enregistrement de la réunion, j'ai cru que la directrice financière soutenait la nouvelle gamme. Visiblement, ce n'était pas le cas.
Owen FletcherWhat exactly did she say?Qu'a-t-elle dit exactement ?
Claire VasseurSomething like: 'I can see the upside, but where I'd part company with you is the launch date.'Quelque chose comme : « Je vois l'intérêt, mais là où je ne vous suis plus, c'est la date de lancement. »
Owen FletcherSo is she against the product?Donc elle est contre le produit ?
Claire VasseurNot the product itself. She's against launching it so soon.Pas contre le produit lui-même. Elle est contre un lancement aussi rapide.
Owen FletcherRight. And that's the trap. One option said 'she opposes the new line', which is too strong. The correct one was about the timing.Voilà. Et c'est ça le piège. Une option disait « elle s'oppose à la nouvelle gamme », ce qui est trop fort. La bonne portait sur le calendrier.
Claire VasseurSo I need to measure how strong the opinion is, not just whether it's positive or negative.Donc je dois mesurer la force de l'opinion, pas seulement savoir si elle est positive ou négative.
Owen FletcherExactly. And check who said it. With three speakers, distractors often swap the opinions around.Exactement. Et vérifier qui l'a dit. Avec trois locuteurs, les distracteurs intervertissent souvent les opinions.
Claire VasseurShould I take notes with initials, then?Je devrais prendre des notes avec les initiales, alors ?
Owen FletcherYes, initials and an arrow: up for support, down for opposition, a question mark for doubt. It takes seconds.Oui, les initiales et une flèche : vers le haut pour le soutien, vers le bas pour l'opposition, un point d'interrogation pour le doute. Ça prend quelques secondes.
Claire VasseurI'll try that in the second simulation. Same thirty minutes?Je vais essayer dans la deuxième simulation. Toujours trente minutes ?
Owen FletcherSame thirty minutes, and no more than two replays per activity. It's internal practice, so experiment freely.Toujours trente minutes, et pas plus de deux réécoutes par activité. C'est un entraînement interne, alors expérimente librement.

Exercices corrigés

Exercice 1 — C1-M6-L2-I1 (C1, C1.2)

Déclaration : écoutez l'énoncé et choisissez l'interprétation correcte.

Transcription :

Head of SalesOfficially, the line is that the merger won't affect our sales territories, but I'd be surprised if we got through next year without at least some of them being redrawn.

1. What does the speaker believe?
A. The official announcement about territories is entirely accurate
B. Sales territories were redrawn last year
C. The merger will be cancelled next year
D. Territory changes are likely despite the official line

Corrigé

1. D — Territory changes are likely despite the official line. « Officially, the line is… » marque une mise à distance, puis « I'd be surprised if we got through next year without… » signifie qu'il s'attend à des changements. L'option « entirely accurate » reprend la position officielle qu'il met en doute.

Exercice 2 — C1-M6-L2-I2 (C1, C1.2)

Déclaration : écoutez l'énoncé et choisissez l'interprétation correcte.

Transcription :

HR DirectorFreezing recruitment and letting attrition do the rest might look painless on a spreadsheet, but it tends to hollow out exactly the teams that can least afford to lose people.

1. What is the speaker's attitude towards the recruitment freeze?
A. She thinks it is the least painful option available
B. She warns that its impact may be uneven and damaging
C. She believes it should be combined with layoffs
D. She is confident it will reduce costs without risk

Corrigé

1. B — She warns that its impact may be uneven and damaging. « might look painless on a spreadsheet, but… hollow out exactly the teams that can least afford to lose people » : l'effet est inégal et nuisible. L'option « least painful » reprend l'apparence qu'elle conteste.

Exercice 3 — C1-M6-L2-I3 (C1, C1.2)

Dialogue court : écoutez l'échange entre trois personnes puis répondez aux trois questions. Notez qui défend quelle position.

Transcription :

Anita RaoThe data is clear: the budget range is cannibalising our premium sales. I'd discontinue it by the end of the year.
George WhitfieldI take your point, but if we drop it, those customers won't trade up; they'll go straight to Corvane. We'd lose them altogether.
Anita RaoPossibly, but at those margins I'm not sure we'd miss them.
Lucy HarperCouldn't we hedge our bets? Keep the budget range online only, and stop stocking it in stores. That frees up shelf space for premium without abandoning the entry-level market.
George WhitfieldI could live with that, provided we track churn closely for the first two quarters.

1. Why does George object to Anita's proposal?
A. He thinks the budget range is very profitable
B. He believes premium sales are already falling for other reasons
C. He fears customers would switch to a competitor
D. He wants to raise the price of the budget range

2. What does Lucy propose?
A. Selling the budget range through a single channel
B. Discontinuing the budget range immediately
C. Moving premium products online
D. Lowering the price of premium products

3. What is George's position on Lucy's idea?
A. He rejects it as too risky
B. He supports it with no conditions
C. He prefers Anita's original proposal to drop the range
D. He accepts it if customer losses are monitored

Corrigé

1. C — He fears customers would switch to a competitor. « they'll go straight to Corvane. We'd lose them altogether » : les clients partiraient chez un concurrent. Anita, elle, juge les marges faibles ; George ne prétend pas que la gamme est très rentable.
2. A — Selling the budget range through a single channel. « Keep the budget range online only, and stop stocking it in stores » : un seul canal de vente, en ligne. Il ne s'agit pas d'arrêter la gamme, mais de la retirer des magasins.
3. D — He accepts it if customer losses are monitored. « I could live with that, provided we track churn closely » : accord conditionnel au suivi de l'attrition clients. « no conditions » est trop fort.

Exercice 4 — C1-M6-L2-I4 (C1, C1.2)

Dialogue long en deux parties : écoutez chaque partie puis répondez à la question correspondante. Identifiez la problématique puis la position finale.

Transcription :

Nathan PriceElena, thanks for making time. I wanted to talk about the four-day week trial before it goes to the executive committee.
Elena MorettiOf course. Productivity held up well, as you know. Output per hour went up eight per cent, and sick leave halved.
Nathan PriceThose are impressive numbers. My hesitation is about the customer-facing teams. Our response times on Fridays slipped, and two key accounts noticed.
Elena MorettiThat's fair. The trial was designed around internal teams; we bolted the client teams on at the last minute, and frankly it showed.
Nathan PriceSo what would you recommend to the committee?
Elena MorettiI'd originally planned to recommend a company-wide rollout. Having looked at the client feedback, I'd now argue for making it permanent for back-office functions and running a separate, properly designed trial for client teams, with staggered days off so that Friday is always covered.
Nathan PriceThat's a much easier sell. The committee won't want to hear 'everyone, immediately'.
Elena MorettiAgreed. I'll redraft the paper and put the client-team trial in as a second phase, with its own success criteria.

1. What problem did the trial reveal?
A. Service to clients deteriorated on certain days
B. Productivity fell among back-office staff
C. Sick leave increased significantly
D. Internal teams refused to take part

2. What will Elena now recommend?
A. Extending the four-day week to every department immediately
B. Ending the trial because of client complaints
C. Postponing any decision until key accounts are consulted
D. Adopting it in some departments and retesting it in others

Corrigé

1. A — Service to clients deteriorated on certain days. « response times on Fridays slipped, and two key accounts noticed » : le service client s'est dégradé le vendredi. La productivité a au contraire augmenté et les arrêts maladie ont diminué de moitié.
2. D — Adopting it in some departments and retesting it in others. « making it permanent for back-office functions and running a separate… trial for client teams ». La généralisation immédiate était sa recommandation initiale (« I'd originally planned »), abandonnée.

Exercice 5 — C1-M6-L2-I5 (C1, C1.2)

Monologue en deux parties : écoutez chaque partie puis répondez à la question correspondante.

Transcription :

Dr Samuel AdeyemiThere's a widespread assumption that remote teams are less innovative because people no longer bump into each other at the coffee machine. It's an appealing story, and it isn't entirely wrong.
Dr Samuel AdeyemiBut in the forty firms we studied, what predicted innovation wasn't where people sat. It was whether managers deliberately created moments for loosely connected colleagues to exchange ideas, online or in person.
Dr Samuel AdeyemiThe practical implication is uncomfortable for some leaders. Ordering people back to the office three days a week, without redesigning how those days are used, mostly produces people answering emails at a different desk.
Dr Samuel AdeyemiMy recommendation, then, is to start with purpose. Decide what the office is for, whether that's workshops, onboarding or cross-team reviews, and schedule attendance around those activities rather than around a fixed number of days.

1. What did the speaker's research find?
A. Remote teams are clearly less innovative than office teams
B. Deliberate exchanges mattered more than location
C. Informal coffee-machine conversations drive most innovation
D. Innovation depends mainly on the size of the firm

2. What does he recommend?
A. Requiring everyone in the office three fixed days a week
B. Allowing employees to work fully remotely
C. Linking attendance to specific collaborative activities
D. Replacing workshops with online meetings

Corrigé

1. B — Deliberate exchanges mattered more than location. « what predicted innovation wasn't where people sat. It was whether managers deliberately created moments… » : l'organisation délibérée des échanges compte plus que le lieu. La première option reprend « l'hypothèse répandue » qu'il nuance.
2. C — Linking attendance to specific collaborative activities. « schedule attendance around those activities rather than around a fixed number of days ». Le retour imposé trois jours par semaine est justement critiqué (« people answering emails at a different desk »).

Exercice 6 — C1-M6-L2-I6 (C1, C1.2)

Réponse construite : écoutez l'extrait de point d'avancement et notez uniquement l'information demandée. Notez les chiffres sous forme brute pendant l'écoute.

Transcription :

Fiona GrantQuick update on the Kestrel warehouse project for the steering group. The original budget was four point two million; we're now forecasting four point six, mainly because of the steel price increase, and that's after drawing down the whole contingency. Handover was planned for the end of September; realistically, we're looking at the third of November. The one piece of good news is that the solar roof came in under budget, so the energy savings case still holds. Any questions, contact Ravi Mehta, who's taking over as project lead from Monday.

1. What is the current budget forecast (in millions)?

2. What is the new expected handover date?

3. Who will be the new project lead?

Corrigé

1. 4.6 / 4.6 million / 4,6 / 4,6 M / four point six / four point six million. Le budget initial (4,2 M) est dépassé : « we're now forecasting four point six ».
2. 3 November / November 3 / 3rd November / November 3rd / the third of November / third of November / 3/11 / 03/11. « realistically, we're looking at the third of November » ; la fin septembre était la date initiale.
3. Ravi Mehta / Ravi / Mehta / ravi mehta. « contact Ravi Mehta, who's taking over as project lead from Monday ».

title: C1-M6 — Simulation C2 n° 1 : emails et rapports longs
description: Lire quatre textes professionnels longs (email, rapport, article, compte rendu) et répondre à 12 questions en 35 minutes maximum. Identifier dans chaque texte l'objet, la demande ou la conclusion principale et la position de l'auteur, déclarée ou implicite. Obtenir au moins 9 bonnes réponses sur 12 en justifiant chaque choix par une phrase précise du texte.
imageQuery: business English Simulation C2 n° 1 : emails et rapports longs

sections.title: C1-M6-L3 — Simulation C2 n° 1 : emails et rapports longs
sections.contentHtml:
Objectifs :

  • Lire quatre textes professionnels longs (email, rapport, article, compte rendu) et répondre à 12 questions en 35 minutes maximum.
  • Identifier dans chaque texte l'objet, la demande ou la conclusion principale et la position de l'auteur, déclarée ou implicite.
  • Obtenir au moins 9 bonnes réponses sur 12 en justifiant chaque choix par une phrase précise du texte.

Compétence C2 — niveau C1.1 — 45 min

Cette simulation de compréhension écrite reprend la famille d'activités « lire et sélectionner » du référentiel : un texte professionnel (courriel, rapport, article, compte rendu), suivi de questions à choix multiple à quatre options posées dans l'ordre du texte. Le critère C1 précise que le candidat comprend en détail une grande variété de textes longs et complexes et identifie des points de détail y compris des attitudes et des opinions, implicites ou déclarées. Ceci est un entraînement interne de l'organisme ; ce n'est pas le test VTest et le score affiché n'a aucune valeur officielle.

Méthode de lecture en trois temps

  1. Survol (30 secondes) : repérez le type de texte, l'émetteur, le destinataire et l'objet. Dans un email, la ligne Subject et la dernière phrase du premier paragraphe donnent souvent l'enjeu.
  2. Lecture des questions : comme elles suivent l'ordre du texte, la question 1 concerne en général le début, la dernière la fin. Soulignez les mots de la question qui indiquent ce que l'on cherche : implies, main purpose, concern, attitude.
  3. Lecture ciblée : relisez le passage correspondant à chaque question et cherchez la reformulation. La bonne option dit la même chose avec d'autres mots ; les distracteurs reprennent souvent les mêmes mots pour dire autre chose.

Les pièges spécifiques au niveau C1

  • Opinion implicite : It would be premature to… signifie que l'auteur est contre une décision immédiate, sans le dire.
  • Nuance de degré : largely, to some extent, marginally — une option qui transforme marginally en significantly est fausse.
  • Cause et conséquence inversées : vérifiez quel élément entraîne l'autre.
  • Information vraie mais hors sujet : l'option peut être exacte d'après le texte sans répondre à la question posée.

Gestion du temps : 35 minutes pour 4 textes et 12 questions

Comptez environ 8 minutes par texte (2 minutes de lecture globale, 6 minutes pour les trois questions) et gardez 3 minutes pour revenir sur les questions marquées. Si un texte vous semble difficile, ne relisez pas tout : allez directement au passage concerné par la question. Ne laissez jamais une réponse vide ; une option bien éliminée vaut mieux qu'une absence de réponse.

Après la simulation, pour chaque erreur, recopiez la phrase du texte qui donnait la réponse et le distracteur choisi. Classez l'erreur : opinion implicite, nuance de degré, cause/conséquence ou information hors sujet. Ce classement vous servira lors du bilan pour cibler vos derniers entraînements.

Langue clé

AnglaisFrançaisUsage
It would be premature to draw firm conclusions.Il serait prématuré de tirer des conclusions définitives.opinion implicite : l'auteur est contre une décision immédiate
This is largely, though not entirely, attributable to…Cela s'explique en grande partie, mais pas entièrement, par…nuance de degré à respecter
I would urge you to reconsider.Je vous invite instamment à reconsidérer.demande ferme mais polie
Contrary to what was initially reported…Contrairement à ce qui avait été annoncé au départ…correction d'une information antérieure
The committee noted, without endorsing, the proposal.Le comité a pris acte de la proposition, sans l'approuver.nuance typique d'un compte rendu

Vocabulaire

TermeTraductionExemple
prematureprématuréIt would be premature to cut the budget now.
to attribute toattribuer àThe delay is attributable to the strike.
shortfalldéficit, manqueThere's a shortfall of 300 units.
to endorseapprouver, soutenirThe board endorsed the plan.
liabilityresponsabilité (juridique) ; passifWe cannot accept liability for third-party delays.
to waiverenoncer à, leverThey agreed to waive the penalty.
provisionalprovisoireThese figures are provisional.
to flagsignalerPlease flag any errors before Friday.
uptaketaux d'adoptionUptake of the app has been slow.
to outsourceexternaliserWe outsourced payroll last year.
benchmarkréférence, point de comparaisonWe used last year's results as a benchmark.
marginallylégèrementCosts rose marginally in Q3.

Dialogue : Conseils : lire vite sans lire mal

Capsule de conseils. Une formatrice montre à l'écran comment elle annote un rapport long avant de répondre aux questions.

PersonnageRépliqueTraduction
Julien MoreauMy problem with long texts is simple: I read every word, and by the time I reach the questions, I've forgotten the beginning.Mon problème avec les textes longs est simple : je lis chaque mot, et quand j'arrive aux questions, j'ai oublié le début.
Helen MarshThen flip the order. Skim for thirty seconds, read the questions, and only then read closely.Alors inverse l'ordre. Survole pendant trente secondes, lis les questions, et seulement ensuite lis attentivement.
Julien MoreauDoesn't skimming make me miss details?Le survol ne me fait pas rater des détails ?
Helen MarshSkimming isn't for details. It tells you who's writing, to whom, and why. The questions then tell you which details matter.Le survol ne sert pas aux détails. Il te dit qui écrit, à qui et pourquoi. Ensuite, les questions te disent quels détails comptent.
Julien MoreauAnd the questions follow the order of the text, right?Et les questions suivent l'ordre du texte, c'est ça ?
Helen MarshYes, which is a huge help. Question one is usually near the top, the last one near the end.Oui, et ça aide énormément. La question un est en général vers le début, la dernière vers la fin.
Julien MoreauWhat about the questions on attitude? Those are the ones I get wrong.Et les questions sur l'attitude ? Ce sont celles que je rate.
Helen MarshLook at the verbs and adverbs: 'urge', 'caution', 'somewhat', 'largely'. They tell you how strongly the writer feels.Regarde les verbes et les adverbes : « urge », « caution », « somewhat », « largely ». Ils indiquent la force de l'opinion de l'auteur.
Julien MoreauAnd timing? Thirty-five minutes for four texts feels tight.Et le temps ? Trente-cinq minutes pour quatre textes, ça paraît serré.
Helen MarshEight minutes per text, three minutes spare. If a question takes more than two minutes, mark it and move on.Huit minutes par texte, trois minutes de marge. Si une question prend plus de deux minutes, marque-la et passe à la suite.
Julien MoreauUnderstood. And this is just practice, not the real test.Compris. Et c'est juste un entraînement, pas le vrai test.
Helen MarshExactly, it's our internal simulation. The point is to build habits you can rely on later.Exactement, c'est notre simulation interne. L'objectif est de prendre des habitudes sur lesquelles tu pourras compter ensuite.

Exercices corrigés

Exercice 1 — C1-M6-L3-I1 (C2, C1.1)

Lisez l'email puis répondez aux trois questions, posées dans l'ordre du texte. Budget conseillé : 8 minutes.

From: Imogen Clarke, Head of Procurement, Brindlewood Foods
To: Marcus Hale, Account Director, Ostfield Logistics
Subject: Service levels under our current agreement

Dear Marcus,

Thank you for your call on Tuesday and for the candour with which you described the staffing difficulties at your Northampton hub. I appreciate that the past quarter has been exceptionally challenging for the whole sector, and I want to be clear that this email is not intended as a prelude to terminating our agreement.

That said, the figures speak for themselves. On-time delivery to our stores fell from 97 per cent in the first quarter to 88 per cent in the third, well below the 95 per cent threshold in our service-level agreement. More concerning than the headline figure is the pattern: almost all late deliveries involved chilled products, which have the shortest shelf life and the highest cost when wasted.

Under clause 9.2, we would be entitled to a service credit of roughly £64,000 for the quarter. I am prepared to waive half of that amount, on the condition that Ostfield presents a written recovery plan by 15 November, including named responsibilities and weekly reporting on chilled deliveries until performance is back above the threshold for two consecutive months.

I would also ask that you consider ring-fencing a dedicated team for our chilled volumes over the Christmas period. I recognise this has a cost, and I am open to discussing how it might be shared.

I look forward to your proposal.

Kind regards,
Imogen Clarke

1. What does Imogen make clear at the start of the email?
A. She intends to end the contract with Ostfield
B. She is not planning to cancel the agreement
C. She was unaware of the staffing problems
D. She blames the whole sector for the delays

2. According to Imogen, what is the most worrying aspect of the performance?
A. The overall drop in on-time deliveries to stores
B. The number of stores affected
C. The cost of the service credit
D. The concentration of delays on chilled products

3. What is Imogen's position on the cost of a dedicated team?
A. She is willing to negotiate a shared arrangement
B. She expects Ostfield to pay the full cost
C. She will pay for it if the recovery plan is accepted
D. She considers it unnecessary before Christmas

Corrigé

1. B — She is not planning to cancel the agreement. « this email is not intended as a prelude to terminating our agreement » : elle ne compte pas résilier. Elle avait été informée des difficultés de personnel lors de l'appel de mardi, ce qui écarte la troisième option.
2. D — The concentration of delays on chilled products. « More concerning than the headline figure is the pattern: almost all late deliveries involved chilled products » : la concentration sur les produits frais. Le chiffre global (88 %) est explicitement jugé moins préoccupant.
3. A — She is willing to negotiate a shared arrangement. « I am open to discussing how it might be shared » : partage du coût négociable. Elle ne promet pas de payer seule, et ne lie pas ce point au plan de redressement.

Exercice 2 — C1-M6-L3-I2 (C2, C1.1)

Lisez l'extrait de rapport puis répondez aux trois questions, posées dans l'ordre du texte.

Internal Report: Twelve-Month Review of the Shared Services Centre
Prepared for: Executive Committee, Harlow & Pryce Engineering

  1. Summary

The Shared Services Centre (SSC) in Gdańsk took over accounts payable, payroll and travel expenses from the four national offices twelve months ago. The business case projected annual savings of £1.8 million. Actual savings for the first year stand at £1.3 million. This shortfall is largely, though not entirely, attributable to one-off transition costs, notably the parallel running of payroll in two countries for longer than planned.

  1. Service quality

Invoice processing times have improved markedly, from an average of 11 days to 4. Payroll accuracy, however, remains below the 99.5 per cent benchmark set in the business case, at 98.7 per cent. While the number of errors is small in absolute terms, each one generates a disproportionate volume of complaints and erodes trust in the centre among staff.

  1. Stakeholder views

Finance managers in the national offices are broadly positive. Line managers are more ambivalent: several reported that they now spend more time, not less, resolving expense queries, because the SSC's online portal is not intuitive.

  1. Recommendations

It would be premature to extend the SSC's scope to procurement, as originally planned for next year. The committee should instead prioritise payroll accuracy and a redesign of the expenses portal, and revisit the question of scope in nine months, once two further quarters of data are available.

1. What does the report say about the gap between projected and actual savings?
A. It is entirely due to transition costs
B. It shows the business case was unrealistic
C. It is mostly explained by temporary costs
D. It will increase in the second year

2. Why does the report consider payroll errors significant?
A. They damage staff trust despite being few
B. They have increased since the centre opened
C. They are more frequent than invoice errors
D. They have caused most of the savings shortfall

3. What does the report recommend regarding procurement?
A. Transferring it to the centre next year as planned
B. Outsourcing it to an external provider
C. Abandoning the idea of extending the centre's scope
D. Delaying a decision until more data is available

Corrigé

1. C — It is mostly explained by temporary costs. « largely, though not entirely, attributable to one-off transition costs » : principalement des coûts ponctuels. L'option « entirely » ignore la nuance « though not entirely ».
2. A — They damage staff trust despite being few. « While the number of errors is small… each one generates a disproportionate volume of complaints and erodes trust » : peu nombreuses, mais fort impact sur la confiance. Le texte n'indique pas qu'elles augmentent.
3. D — Delaying a decision until more data is available. « It would be premature… revisit the question of scope in nine months » : décision reportée, pas abandonnée. Le piège « abandoning » est trop fort.

Exercice 3 — C1-M6-L3-I3 (C2, C1.1)

Lisez l'article puis répondez aux trois questions, posées dans l'ordre du texte. Attention aux opinions implicites.

The Quiet Cost of Always-On Collaboration

When Tamsin Rowe became operations director at Fennick Software, she inherited a culture she describes as 'wonderfully open and completely exhausting'. Every decision, however minor, was discussed in a group chat; every meeting had at least eight attendees, in case someone felt left out.

None of this was born of bad intentions. Fennick had grown from twelve to two hundred employees in four years, and its founders were determined not to lose the sense that everyone had a voice. Yet by the time Rowe arrived, engineers were spending an average of 23 hours a week in meetings and chats, and the release schedule had slipped three times in a year.

Rowe's response was not, as some colleagues feared, to clamp down on communication. Instead, she introduced what she calls 'decision owners': for every project, one person is explicitly responsible for making the call after consulting whoever they judge relevant. Meetings now require a written purpose and are capped at five people; others receive a two-line summary.

The results after six months are encouraging, if not spectacular. Meeting time has fallen by roughly a third, and the last two releases shipped on schedule. Not everyone is convinced. Some long-serving employees say they feel 'informed rather than involved', and Rowe concedes that the line between efficiency and exclusion needs constant attention.

'Collaboration isn't the goal,' she says. 'Good decisions are. Collaboration is how you get there, and like anything, you can overdo it.'

1. According to the article, why had Fennick developed this culture?
A. Its founders wanted to stay inclusive as the firm grew
B. Its engineers had asked for more meetings
C. It had to compensate for poor management decisions
D. Its software releases required constant group discussion

2. How does the article describe Rowe's approach?
A. She drastically restricted communication between teams
B. She replaced all meetings with written summaries
C. She named decision owners and limited meeting size
D. She let each employee decide which meetings to attend

3. How would you best describe the writer's view of the results?
A. Overwhelmingly enthusiastic
B. Positive but measured, with acknowledged drawbacks
C. Sceptical about the long-term benefits
D. Neutral, as the data is not yet available

Corrigé

1. A — Its founders wanted to stay inclusive as the firm grew. « its founders were determined not to lose the sense that everyone had a voice » : préserver l'inclusion pendant la croissance. Le texte dit explicitement « None of this was born of bad intentions ».
2. C — She named decision owners and limited meeting size. « decision owners » + « capped at five people » : responsabilité claire des décisions et réunions limitées. L'article précise qu'elle n'a pas restreint la communication (« not… to clamp down »), contrairement à ce que craignaient certains.
3. B — Positive but measured, with acknowledged drawbacks. « encouraging, if not spectacular » + « Not everyone is convinced » : bilan positif mais mesuré, avec des réserves reconnues. « Overwhelmingly » est trop fort ; des données chiffrées existent, ce qui exclut « neutral ».

Exercice 4 — C1-M6-L3-I4 (C2, C1.1)

Lisez le compte rendu puis répondez aux trois questions, posées dans l'ordre du texte.

Minutes: Product Steering Committee, Calloway Medical Devices
Date: 14 October
Present: R. Osei (Chair), L. Brandt, P. Kowalski, S. Tan, M. Duarte

  1. Launch of the HM-40 monitor in Southeast Asia

L. Brandt reported that regulatory approval in Singapore had been granted ahead of schedule. Approval in Malaysia, contrary to what was reported at the last meeting, has not yet been obtained; a request for additional clinical data was received on 2 October. L. Brandt estimated a delay of eight to ten weeks.

P. Kowalski proposed launching in Singapore alone in January rather than waiting for a joint launch. S. Tan expressed concern that a staggered launch would double marketing costs and confuse regional distributors. After discussion, the committee agreed to a Singapore-only launch, provided that the distributor contracts allow a single regional campaign to be run later.

  1. Customer complaints on the HM-30

M. Duarte presented the quarterly complaints analysis. Complaints rose marginally (from 41 to 46), all relating to battery life. The committee noted, without endorsing, M. Duarte's proposal to offer free battery replacements to all existing customers; the chair asked for a full cost estimate before any decision.

  1. Actions
  • L. Brandt: submit the additional clinical data to the Malaysian authority by 31 October.
  • S. Tan: check the distributor contracts and report to the chair by 21 October.
  • M. Duarte: prepare a cost estimate for battery replacements for the next meeting.

1. What correction is made regarding Malaysia?
A. Approval was granted earlier than expected
B. The application was rejected on 2 October
C. No additional data will be required
D. Approval had wrongly been reported as obtained

2. On what condition was the Singapore-only launch approved?
A. That marketing costs remain unchanged
B. That a single regional campaign remains possible later
C. That Malaysian approval is obtained by January at the latest
D. That S. Tan agrees to manage the launch

3. What was decided about M. Duarte's battery proposal?
A. It was approved for all existing customers
B. It was rejected because complaints were stable
C. No decision was taken until costs are known
D. It was limited to customers who had complained

Corrigé

1. D — Approval had wrongly been reported as obtained. « contrary to what was reported at the last meeting, has not yet been obtained » : l'approbation avait été annoncée à tort. La demande du 2 octobre réclame des données supplémentaires ; ce n'est pas un rejet.
2. B — That a single regional campaign remains possible later. « provided that the distributor contracts allow a single regional campaign to be run later » : une campagne régionale commune doit rester possible. La hausse des coûts était l'objection de S. Tan, pas la condition retenue.
3. C — No decision was taken until costs are known. « noted, without endorsing… asked for a full cost estimate before any decision » : aucune décision avant l'estimation. « noted » ne signifie pas « approved » : c'est le piège principal.

title: C1-M6 — Simulation C2 n° 2 : articles, textes commerciaux et nuances implicites
description: Lire quatre textes longs de registres variés (note de politique interne, texte commercial, tribune, échange d'emails) et répondre à 12 questions en 35 minutes maximum. Repérer l'intention de l'auteur, le ton (promotionnel, critique, diplomatique) et les sous-entendus d'au moins trois textes sur quatre. Obtenir au moins 9 bonnes réponses sur 12 et classer chaque erreur selon son type.

sections.title: C1-M6-L4 — Simulation C2 n° 2 : articles, textes commerciaux et nuances implicites
sections.contentHtml:
Objectifs :

  • Lire quatre textes longs de registres variés (note de politique interne, texte commercial, tribune, échange d'emails) et répondre à 12 questions en 35 minutes maximum.
  • Repérer l'intention de l'auteur, le ton (promotionnel, critique, diplomatique) et les sous-entendus d'au moins trois textes sur quatre.
  • Obtenir au moins 9 bonnes réponses sur 12 et classer chaque erreur selon son type.

Compétence C2 — niveau C1.2 — 45 min

Cette seconde simulation de lecture élargit la palette des textes. Le référentiel mentionne, pour l'activité « lire et sélectionner », des notes, mémos, courriels, textes commerciaux et extraits d'articles. Au niveau C1.2, la difficulté ne vient plus du vocabulaire seul mais du registre et de l'intention : un texte commercial promet plus qu'il ne garantit, une tribune défend une thèse en concédant des arguments adverses, un échange d'emails cache parfois une tension derrière une politesse irréprochable. Rappel : il s'agit d'un entraînement interne de l'organisme, pas du test VTest ; le score obtenu est un repère pédagogique.

Lire un texte commercial avec discernement

Repérez la différence entre ce qui est affirmé et ce qui est suggéré. Up to 40 % faster ne signifie pas 40 % faster ; designed to reduce errors ne garantit pas que les erreurs diminuent. Les notes de bas de page et les conditions (subject to, terms apply, for orders over…) contiennent souvent la réponse aux questions de détail.

Lire une tribune ou un article d'opinion

L'auteur commence souvent par résumer la position qu'il va contester (It is often argued that…, Conventional wisdom holds that…). Une question sur l'avis de l'auteur piège ceux qui s'arrêtent au premier paragraphe. Cherchez le pivot (Yet, This view, however, overlooks…) et la conclusion, où la thèse est reformulée.

Lire un échange d'emails

Dans une chaîne de messages, la question porte souvent sur l'évolution de la position d'un correspondant, ou sur ce qu'il demande réellement. Lisez les messages dans l'ordre chronologique (attention, l'affichage est parfois inversé) et notez en marge la demande de chacun. Les formules de politesse C1 (I wonder whether it might be possible…, With respect, …) peuvent exprimer une insistance forte.

Gestion du temps

Même budget que la simulation n° 1 : 8 minutes par texte, 3 minutes de marge, 35 minutes au total. Deux conseils supplémentaires :

  • commencez par le texte qui vous paraît le plus accessible si la plateforme d'entraînement le permet, pour sécuriser des points ;
  • pour les questions sur le ton ou l'intention, lisez la conclusion du texte en premier : c'est souvent là que l'auteur se dévoile.

Analyse des résultats

Comparez ce résultat avec celui de la simulation n° 1. Si vous perdez des points surtout sur les textes commerciaux et les tribunes, c'est le repérage de l'intention qu'il faut travailler ; si c'est sur les comptes rendus et les rapports, entraînez-vous à repérer les nuances de décision (noted, agreed in principle, deferred).

Langue clé

AnglaisFrançaisUsage
Conventional wisdom holds that…Selon l'idée reçue…introduction d'une position que l'auteur va contester
This view, however, overlooks…Ce point de vue néglige cependant…pivot vers la thèse de l'auteur
Subject to availability and terms of service.Sous réserve de disponibilité et des conditions de service.restriction dans un texte commercial
With respect, I don't think that addresses the issue.Sauf votre respect, je ne pense pas que cela règle le problème.désaccord ferme sous une forme polie
We agreed in principle, pending final figures.Nous avons donné un accord de principe, en attendant les chiffres définitifs.décision non définitive

Vocabulaire

TermeTraductionExemple
conventional wisdomidée reçue, opinion dominanteConventional wisdom says price is everything.
to overlooknégliger, ne pas tenir compte deThe plan overlooks training costs.
subject tosous réserve deDelivery is subject to stock availability.
pendingen attendantThe decision is pending legal review.
eligibleéligible, admissibleOnly full-time staff are eligible.
to reimburserembourserCosts will be reimbursed within 30 days.
seamlessfluide, sans ruptureWe promise a seamless migration.
to back downcéder, reculerThe supplier backed down on the price.
upfrontà l'avance, d'embléeThere's no upfront fee.
to scale backréduire (l'ampleur)We've scaled back the project.
disingenuousde mauvaise foi, hypocriteIt would be disingenuous to blame the weather.
to concedeconcéder, reconnaîtreShe conceded that the timing was poor.
in principleen principe, sur le principeThey agreed in principle.

Dialogue : Repérer l'intention de l'auteur

Atelier filmé. Le formateur et une apprenante comparent une brochure commerciale et une tribune sur le même sujet.

PersonnageRépliqueTraduction
Owen FletcherHere are two texts about the same HR software: a brochure and an opinion piece. What's the difference in intention?Voici deux textes sur le même logiciel RH : une brochure et une tribune. Quelle est la différence d'intention ?
Amira HaddadThe brochure wants to sell it. The article seems to criticise it, but it starts by praising it.La brochure veut le vendre. L'article semble le critiquer, mais il commence par en faire l'éloge.
Owen FletcherThat's the classic structure. The writer concedes a point, then pivots. Where's the pivot?C'est la structure classique. L'auteur concède un point, puis bascule. Où est la bascule ?
Amira HaddadHere: 'This view, however, overlooks the people who have to use it every day.'Ici : « Ce point de vue néglige cependant les personnes qui doivent l'utiliser tous les jours. »
Owen FletcherGood. And in the brochure, what's actually promised?Bien. Et dans la brochure, qu'est-ce qui est réellement promis ?
Amira HaddadIt says 'up to sixty per cent less admin time'. So that's a maximum, not a guarantee.Elle dit « jusqu'à soixante pour cent de temps administratif en moins ». C'est donc un maximum, pas une garantie.
Owen FletcherExactly. And there's a footnote: 'based on organisations with over five hundred employees'.Exactement. Et il y a une note : « sur la base d'organisations de plus de cinq cents salariés ».
Amira HaddadSo a question might ask who benefits most, and the answer is hidden in the footnote.Donc une question pourrait demander qui en profite le plus, et la réponse est cachée dans la note.
Owen FletcherVery often, yes. With commercial texts, always read the small print.Très souvent, oui. Avec les textes commerciaux, lis toujours les petits caractères.
Amira HaddadAnd with opinion pieces, read the conclusion first?Et avec les tribunes, lire la conclusion d'abord ?
Owen FletcherWhen the question is about the writer's view, yes. It saves time. Thirty-five minutes go quickly in this internal simulation.Quand la question porte sur l'avis de l'auteur, oui. Ça fait gagner du temps. Trente-cinq minutes passent vite dans cette simulation interne.

Exercices corrigés

Exercice 1 — C1-M6-L4-I1 (C2, C1.2)

Lisez la note de politique interne puis répondez aux trois questions, posées dans l'ordre du texte. Budget conseillé : 8 minutes.

To: All employees, Pellmore Insurance Group
From: People & Culture Directorate
Subject: Revised policy on professional development funding

Following the consultation held in the spring, the Executive Board has approved a revised policy on funding for external professional development, which will take effect on 1 January.

Under the previous scheme, funding was allocated on a first-come, first-served basis, which, as several respondents pointed out, tended to favour employees in head-office functions who were better informed about the process. The new policy replaces this with two application windows per year, in February and September, and a cross-departmental panel that will assess applications against published criteria, including relevance to the employee's development plan and to business priorities.

The individual ceiling will rise from £1,500 to £2,500 per year. However, employees who receive more than £2,000 in a given year will be asked to remain with the company for twelve months after completing the course; those who leave earlier will be required to repay a proportion of the cost, calculated on a sliding scale. This clause will not apply to employees whose roles are made redundant.

Many respondents asked for time off to study as well as financial support. The Board has agreed in principle to grant up to five days of paid study leave per year, pending a review of the impact on operational teams, which is expected to conclude in March.

Questions about the policy may be addressed to your HR business partner.

1. What problem with the previous scheme does the memo mention?
A. The funding ceiling was too low for most courses
B. Applications were assessed by a single manager
C. Access to funding was unequal across the organisation
D. Head-office staff were excluded from the scheme

2. Which employees would have to repay part of their funding?
A. Any employee receiving more than £1,500
B. Those receiving over £2,000 who resign within a year
C. Employees whose roles are made redundant
D. All employees who leave within twelve months of applying

3. What is the status of paid study leave?
A. It is agreed in principle but not yet confirmed
B. It will start on 1 January
C. It was rejected because of operational constraints
D. It will be decided by the cross-departmental panel

Corrigé

1. C — Access to funding was unequal across the organisation. « tended to favour employees in head-office functions who were better informed » : l'accès était inégal. Le siège était au contraire favorisé, pas exclu : c'est l'inverse du distracteur.
2. B — Those receiving over £2,000 who resign within a year. « more than £2,000… those who leave earlier [que 12 mois après le cours] will be required to repay a proportion » ; les salariés licenciés économiques en sont explicitement exclus.
3. A — It is agreed in principle but not yet confirmed. « agreed in principle… pending a review… expected to conclude in March » : accord de principe, non définitif. Seule la politique de financement prend effet le 1er janvier.

Exercice 2 — C1-M6-L4-I2 (C2, C1.2)

Lisez le texte commercial puis répondez aux trois questions, posées dans l'ordre du texte. Lisez les petits caractères.

LUMENTRA FLEET: smarter energy for commercial vehicle fleets

Running a fleet of delivery vans has never been more complex. Fuel prices are volatile, low-emission zones are spreading across city centres, and your customers increasingly want to know the carbon footprint of every delivery. Lumentra Fleet brings charging, route planning and emissions reporting together in a single platform.

Why fleet managers choose Lumentra

  • Up to 30% lower energy costs* through smart charging that automatically shifts charging to off-peak hours.
  • Emissions reports ready for your customers and auditors at the click of a button.
  • A seamless transition: our onboarding team configures the platform around your existing depots and vehicles, so there's no need to replace your current chargers if they meet our compatibility standard.

Flexible pricing
Choose a monthly subscription per vehicle with no upfront fee, or an annual plan with two months free. Fleets of 50 vehicles or more benefit from a dedicated account manager.

Try before you commit
Book a 60-day pilot on up to ten vehicles. If you don't see measurable savings, you can walk away with no cancellation charge.**

  • Based on average results of fleets with overnight charging at depot level, compared with uncontrolled charging. Savings depend on tariff structure and vehicle usage.

** Pilot available to companies operating at least 20 vehicles. Hardware installation costs, where required, are not refundable.

1. What is the main purpose of the text?
A. To present an integrated platform to fleet operators
B. To compare electric and diesel delivery vans
C. To announce new low-emission zone regulations
D. To recruit fleet managers for a pilot study

2. According to the footnote, the 30% saving…
A. is guaranteed for every customer
B. applies only to fleets of more than 50 vehicles on annual plans
C. is achieved by replacing existing chargers
D. is an average for one charging pattern and may vary

3. Which company could NOT take part in the pilot?
A. A company with 25 vans and no compatible chargers
B. A company operating 12 delivery vans
C. A company with 60 vehicles wanting to test ten of them
D. A company that wants to cancel after 60 days

Corrigé

1. A — To present an integrated platform to fleet operators. Le texte présente une plateforme réunissant « charging, route planning and emissions reporting » pour gestionnaires de flottes. Les zones à faibles émissions ne sont qu'un élément de contexte.
2. D — is an average for one charging pattern and may vary. « Based on average results of fleets with overnight charging at depot level… Savings depend on tariff structure » : moyenne liée à un mode de recharge, variable. « Up to » exclut toute garantie.
3. B — A company operating 12 delivery vans. La note ** réserve le pilote aux entreprises d'au moins 20 véhicules : une flotte de 12 est exclue. L'absence de bornes compatibles entraîne seulement des frais d'installation non remboursables, pas une exclusion.

Exercice 3 — C1-M6-L4-I3 (C2, C1.2)

Lisez la tribune puis répondez aux trois questions, posées dans l'ordre du texte. Repérez la concession et le pivot.

Opinion: Stop Treating Customer Surveys as a Scoreboard
By Dominic Achterberg, independent service design consultant

Conventional wisdom holds that what gets measured gets managed, and few things are measured as obsessively as customer satisfaction. Companies run surveys after every call, every delivery and every invoice, and the resulting scores feed directly into bonuses and league tables. In fairness, this has had real benefits: it has forced executives who once ignored service to pay attention to it.

This view, however, overlooks what happens once a score becomes a target. In one retailer I worked with, store managers learned that customers who were asked to complete a survey at the till scored around ten points higher than those who received it by email the next day. Within a quarter, emailed surveys had quietly disappeared. Scores rose; complaints did not fall.

It would be disingenuous to blame the managers. They responded rationally to the incentives they were given. The problem lies in treating a diagnostic tool as a performance measure. A satisfaction survey is at its most useful when it tells you something you didn't know, and at its least useful when everyone involved has a reason to make it look good.

My recommendation is not to abolish surveys, but to decouple them from individual rewards and to give far more weight to what customers write in the comments box than to the number they tick. Read a hundred comments and you will learn more than from a thousand scores.

1. What does the writer concede in the first paragraph?
A. Customer surveys are usually too long
B. Satisfaction scores should be linked to bonuses
C. Executives have always paid close attention to customer service
D. Measuring it has made executives take service seriously

2. What does the retailer example illustrate?
A. Scores improved without a real improvement in service
B. Email surveys produce more reliable results than in-store surveys
C. Store managers deliberately falsified survey results
D. Customers complained more after surveys were changed

3. What does the writer ultimately recommend?
A. Abolishing satisfaction surveys altogether
B. Surveying customers only by email
C. Decoupling surveys from rewards and prioritising comments
D. Increasing the number of surveys to improve the accuracy of scores

Corrigé

1. D — Measuring it has made executives take service seriously. « In fairness, this has had real benefits: it has forced executives who once ignored service to pay attention to it » : c'est la concession. Le lien avec les primes est décrit, pas approuvé.
2. A — Scores improved without a real improvement in service. « Scores rose; complaints did not fall » : les scores montent sans amélioration réelle. Les managers n'ont pas falsifié les résultats, ils ont modifié la méthode de collecte ; l'auteur refuse d'ailleurs de les blâmer.
3. C — Decoupling surveys from rewards and prioritising comments. « decouple them from individual rewards and… give far more weight to what customers write » ; il précise : « not to abolish surveys ».

Exercice 4 — C1-M6-L4-I4 (C2, C1.2)

Lisez l'échange d'emails (du plus ancien au plus récent) puis répondez aux trois questions, posées dans l'ordre du texte.

From: Valeria Costa, Project Manager, Arkwell Interiors
To: Benedict Shaw, Facilities Director, Norbridge University
Subject: Library refurbishment, revised schedule

Dear Benedict,

Further to our site meeting, I am writing to confirm that, owing to the asbestos discovered in the east wing ceiling, the specialist removal work will add approximately four weeks to the programme. We therefore propose moving practical completion from 30 June to 28 July. Since the asbestos could not reasonably have been identified from the survey provided at tender stage, we will be submitting a claim for the additional costs under clause 14.

Kind regards,
Valeria

-----

From: Benedict Shaw
To: Valeria Costa
Subject: RE: Library refurbishment, revised schedule

Dear Valeria,

Thank you for the prompt notification. I accept that the asbestos is a genuine unforeseen condition, and we will consider your claim in good faith once we have the breakdown.

The new date, however, is a serious problem. The library must be open for the start of the summer school on 14 July, which brings in 600 international students and a significant share of our annual income. With respect, I do not think a four-week extension across the whole building addresses that.

Could you look at whether the west wing and the ground-floor reading rooms, which are unaffected, could be completed and handed over by 10 July, with the east wing following later? We would be prepared to accept some restrictions on access in that case.

Best regards,
Benedict

1. Why does Valeria believe her company is entitled to extra payment?
A. The university changed the design after the tender
B. The problem could not have been detected from the tender survey
C. The removal work was requested by Benedict at their recent site meeting
D. The contract allows four weeks of delay at no cost

2. What is Benedict's attitude towards the claim for additional costs?
A. He rejects it because the delay is unacceptable
B. He accepts it immediately in full
C. He will consider it fairly once costs are detailed
D. He asks Valeria to withdraw it in exchange for an earlier date

3. What does Benedict propose?
A. Postponing the summer school until August
B. Keeping the original completion date of 30 June for the whole building
C. Closing the west wing during the summer school
D. A partial handover of the unaffected areas before the summer school

Corrigé

1. B — The problem could not have been detected from the tender survey. « could not reasonably have been identified from the survey provided at tender stage » : le problème n'était pas décelable avec les informations initiales. Aucun changement de conception n'est évoqué.
2. C — He will consider it fairly once costs are detailed. « we will consider your claim in good faith once we have the breakdown » : examen loyal après détail des coûts. Il conteste la date, pas le principe de la réclamation : c'est le distracteur tentant.
3. D — A partial handover of the unaffected areas before the summer school. « the west wing and the ground-floor reading rooms… handed over by 10 July, with the east wing following later » : réception partielle avant l'école d'été du 14 juillet.

title: C1-M6 — Simulation C3 complète : lire, répéter, argumenter
description: Enregistrer les treize activités d'une simulation orale complète (3 lectures à haute voix, 6 écoute-répétitions, 4 questions ouvertes) en une seule session de 45 minutes maximum. Lire trois textes de longueur croissante sans erreur de prononciation bloquante, avec un découpage en groupes de sens cohérent. Répondre à quatre questions ouvertes de 45 à 120 secondes en utilisant au moins 85 % du temps prévu et une structure annoncée (position, arguments, exemple, conclusion).
